title: Accumulation render 3D
description: Film-quality three.js frames by brute force: every frame is rendered N times with sub-pixel camera jitter (anti-aliasing), a jittered sun (soft area shadows) and sub-frame time offsets (true motion blur), then averaged in a float buffer — shown on a candy studio scene with a fast-spinning torus knot and an orbiting chrome ball, optionally split against the raw 1-sample render.
useFor: A Blender-like finish for 3D shots and a drop-in AccumPass pattern (copy the component) for any three.js motion that needs real motion blur and soft shadows; preview uses 2 samples, renders use all.
source: mg-styles-15 03-isometric js/render.js accumulation pass (MIT, Vincentwei1021) — technique after mg-styles-15

samples.doc: renders averaged per frame (render-time; preview always uses 2)

shutter.doc: shutter fraction of a frame covered by the sub-frame samples (0–1)

sunJitter.doc: sun position jitter in world units (soft shadow size)

spin.doc: torus-knot spin speed (rad/s) — faster = more visible motion blur

compare.doc: split screen: left = 1 sample, right = accumulated

seed.doc: unused variation seed (kept for spec compatibility)

title.doc: heading at the top of the frame (shown when labels is on)

title: Book open 3D
description: A closed cloth hardback on a felt desk mat swings its cover open round the spine, two leaves turn over with a bend, and the camera pushes in and levels out onto a lesson spread whose figure then draws itself in ink.
useFor: Textbook, storybook or "chapter 1" openers; education products; any brand story told as a book.
source: video x3 0.30-1.60 s (cover open, page turns, camera push)

coverTitle.doc: title on the cover and the title page

coverArt.doc: optional image for the cover inset (public/ path or URL); procedural ink jar drawing if empty

lessonEyebrow.doc: small caps eyebrow on the left page

lessonBody.default: Energy is never made or lost. It sits in stores and moves between them whenever something happens: a fall, a push, a spark.
lessonBody.doc: body paragraph on the left page

equation.doc: boxed italic equation on the left page ("" hides)

figureCaption.default: Fig. 1  Eight things, each with a store of its own.
figureCaption.doc: italic caption under the right-page figure

figureSrc.doc: optional image for the right-page figure; procedural ink rack drawing (drawn on) if empty

contents.doc: chapter titles on the contents leaf

editionLabel.doc: small caps line at the foot of the title page

prefaceEyebrow.doc: small caps eyebrow on the preface leaf

prefaceTitle.doc: italic heading on the preface leaf

hintLabel.doc: small caps label of the taped hint card on the left page

hintTitle.default: Lift the flap after you guess
hintTitle.doc: bold line on the hint card

hintNote.doc: handwritten note at the foot of the hint card

turns.doc: leaves that turn after the cover (0-2)

openAt.doc: frame the cover starts to open (source 0.40 s)

speed.doc: timing multiplier for everything after openAt (1 = source)

title: Brick collapse physics
description: A built brick tower creaks, tips about its base edge and breaks into independent bricks that bounce with restitution 0.3 and settle flat; the camera shakes on impact and tilts down to the rubble. Deterministic pre-simulated rigid bodies, bricks stepped at 12 fps.
useFor: Failure / pivot beats, "break it to rebuild it", playful destruction before a rebuild.

caption.default: Well. Back to the drawing board.
caption.doc: subtitle pill after the dust settles (empty = none)

title: Brick FX: fire & smoke
description: Stop-motion brick VFX on a toy rocket launch: the flame is 8–20 translucent orange round plates re-seeded every drawing at 12 fps, the smoke is white round bricks that grow and roll outward — no particles, no gradients — as the rocket shivers and lifts off.
useFor: Launch beats, "we have lift-off", stop-motion VFX vocabulary reusable across brick / clay / papercraft looks.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/brick-toy demo/rockets.js fire & smoke (MIT, LemoLab)

kind.doc: fire = flame + smoke, smoke = smoke only, water = cool splash plates + smoke

liftAt.doc: frame the rocket lifts off (ignition 12 frames earlier)

caption.default: And every launch starts with one brick.
caption.doc: subtitle pill (empty = none)

stepFps.doc: stop-motion re-seed rate of the flame drawings

title: Brick rebuild morph
description: The same set of glossy toy bricks lifts off one word and reassembles into a different one: bricks matched by size and colour arc across on staggered 8ths and snap on landing, with spare bricks flying in from bins behind the baseplate.
useFor: Transformation stories in a playful material: career change, before/after, rebrand, a word re-spelled.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/brick-toy "Rebuild into something else" + engine (MIT code / CC BY 4.0 docs, LemoLab)

captionFrom.default: It spelled one thing for years…
captionFrom.doc: subtitle shown with the first word

title: Brick snap build
description: Stop-motion macro toy bricks fly in on arcs, one per beat, and click into place with a tiny overshoot, stacking into a word (or custom voxel list) on a studded baseplate; bricks step at 12 fps while the camera glides on ones.
useFor: "Built from the ground up" brand / product / logo builds, education and kids' content, countdowns.

text.doc: word built from bricks via a 5×7 pixel font (A–Z 0–9, ♥)

bricks.doc: custom brick list [{x,y,z,w,d,h,color}] in stud units (y up, h 1.2 = brick); overrides text

colorBy.doc: letter = one colour per letter, row = per row stripes, random = scattered

stepFps.doc: stop-motion stepping of brick movement (12 = on twos at 24)

caption.doc: subtitle pill under the build (empty = none)

title: Chart to installation (crane to top view)
description: Two series of physical plate stacks spiral around a walnut dial; the camera tracks the spiral while they assemble, then cranes back and up to a ~70° top view where the stacks read as one data sculpture and the inlaid tick ring and years become the typography, with an end card beside it.
useFor: Signature ending / summary shot for any physical-data film: a decade of values revealed as one installation.

labels.doc: period labels inlaid on the dial (one per stack pair)

materialA.doc: aluminium | acrylic | brass | oak | stone | copper

materialB.doc: aluminium | acrylic | brass | oak | stone | copper

kicker.doc: tracked caps line above the title

verdict.doc: accent verdict line under the rule

craneAt.doc: frame the 4 s crane to the top view starts

title: Cloner bed ripple
description: A dense pin-art bed of glossy two-tone candy capsules in soft pastel studio light; effector bands roll across it raising and tilting the pills along the height gradient, and timed impacts send damped ripple rings racing outward — a satisfying C4D-cloner ASMR field.
useFor: Satisfying backdrop or floor for product idents, logo stings and hero sections; pair with jelly-type-drop for the full candy ident.
source: mg-styles-15 04-3d-render 0.0-5.5 s, blender/sim.py sweep/ring/wave_height (MIT, Vincentwei1021) — technique after mg-styles-15

sweeps.doc: how many effector bands roll through

title: Colour ignition wave
description: A matte white clay isometric city waits; the exposure dips, the hero tower flashes and a cyan pulse ring races out across the ground — as it reaches each object, colour climbs its facade from the ground behind a thin bright scan line, empty tiles hop and flip to their coloured undersides, windows light and the camera kicks.
useFor: A universal "before → after / switched on / launch" hero moment for product, city, platform and data dioramas.
source: mg-styles-15 03-isometric 6.0-6.5 s, world.js clayMat / flash delay / two-faced tiles (MIT, Vincentwei1021) — technique after mg-styles-15

map.doc: rows of map chars (see iso-city-build): r road, b block, p plaza, c core, w water, t tree, h house, s solar, u turbine, g grass

origin.doc: [x, z] grid offset from the centre where the pulse starts

speed.doc: pulse front speed in tiles per second

climbSpeed.doc: how fast colour climbs a facade (tiles per second)

title: Exploded stack (teardown 3D)
description: A stack of five flat layers (base, battery, board with chips, keyboard with keycaps, glass top) sits on a dark seamless; they lift apart top-first with a stagger while the keys and chips ripple up, the camera orbits and a leader-line label column cascades in; hold with a gentle float, then it closes bottom-first with each part landing with a tiny mechanical dip.
useFor: Hardware launches, "what is inside" explainers, layered architecture (UI, API, DB as slabs), feature stacks on landing pages; any product screenshot can be one layer via src.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/teardown demo/src/main.js, timeline.js, overlay.js (MIT, LemoLab)

layers.doc: bottom to top: name, spec, w, d, h (3D units), colour, optional src image on top face, optional parts grid (cols, rows, size, height, colour)

openAt.doc: frame the top layer starts to lift

closeAt.doc: frame the bottom layer starts to close

wave.doc: frames the part ripple takes to cross a surface

orbitFrom.doc: camera azimuth at the start, degrees

title: Exploded view (3D parts, labels, cutaway)
description: A real three.js assembly (end cap, battery, circuit board with chips, motor, shaft, spinning gear, front plate inside a hollow housing sleeve) lit by a studio environment separates part by part along its axis with a 3-frame stagger while the camera orbits and numbered leader-line labels project from the 3D parts, then reassembles; the cutaway variant stays closed and a clip plane slices the shell open.
useFor: Hardware launches, engineering and teaching explainers, "how it is made" and product feature call-outs. Replace `parts` (mesh box / cyl / tube / gear / board / sphere / ring) to explode your own object; the axis turns vertical in portrait.
source: prompt corpus x17 (procedural 3D object separates into labelled parts, orbits, reassembles; cutaway slices it open)

parts.doc: [{name, spec?, mesh:"box|cyl|tube|gear|board|sphere|ring", pos:[x,y,z], size:[...], dir:[dx,dy,dz], dist, color, spin?, shell?, metal?}] x is the assembly axis; size = box [x,y,z], cyl [radius,length], tube [outerR,length,innerR], gear [R,thickness,teeth]

variant.doc: 'explode' (parts separate) | 'cutaway' (closed assembly, shell parts sliced open by a clip plane)

explodeAt.doc: frame the first part starts to move (or the cut starts)

reassembleAt.doc: frame the parts start coming back

orbitSpeed.doc: camera orbit speed, degrees per second

sectionLabel.doc: mono caption top-left while the cutaway is open

title: Faceted sea
description: An endless low-poly ocean in orthographic view: every triangle glints on its own, a turquoise shallow rim and foam ring wrap a tiny hex islet that rises from the water, a boat bobs on the wave function, and the far water dissolves into a horizonless pastel sky while the light drifts from day to dusk.
useFor: Calm 3D backdrop for island / travel / logistics / calm-brand heroes and diorama scenes; a looping website hero; put title words in HTML over it.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/lowpoly-island demo/sea.js + post.js (MIT, LemoLab) — wave function, shallow rim, depth haze, time-of-day keys

timeStart.doc: time of day at the start: dawn | day | dusk | night

timeEnd.doc: time of day at the end (the light eases from start to end)

azimuthEnd.doc: camera azimuth at the end (slow turntable)

elevation.doc: camera elevation in degrees (25-35 day, 20-25 night, 50 map-like)

zoom.doc: orthographic frustum height in world units (12-16 = island scale)

glint.doc: sun specular strength on the facets (too high = white flashes)

islet.doc: show the small hex islet (drives the shallow rim and foam)

boat.doc: a small boat circling the islet

skyColor.doc: sky zenith colour, '' = from the time of day (overrides the whole clip)

horizonColor.doc: sky / haze colour at the horizon, '' = from the time of day

waterColor.doc: deep water colour, '' = from the time of day

shallowColor.doc: shallow rim water colour, '' = from the time of day

tree2Color.doc: big pine upper cone / small pine lower foliage colour

title: Glass strip-light sweep
description: A dark glass product in black space: a tall strip light passes behind the camera and its reflection slides across the object, drawing a thin white contour with rainbow fringing at the edges; between sweeps only side-strip silhouettes remain.
useFor: Premium product reveals for SaaS / hardware brands, app-icon glass hero, launch-film openers.

passes.doc: start frames of each strip sweep

passFrames.doc: frames one sweep takes (arc -1.35 to +1.35 rad)

dispersion.doc: rainbow fringe strength (rad of environment offset per channel; 0 = off)

sideStrips.doc: intensity of the permanent side strips that draw the silhouette

kicker.doc: small tracked caps above the name

orbit.doc: slow camera orbit amplitude in rad

title: Globe (3D, day/night, arcs)
description: A shaded three.js Earth (procedural land and ocean, soft day/night terminator with warm city lights, atmosphere rim) turns slowly; glowing arcs lift off the surface and fly between cities along great circles with pulsing markers and name labels, then the camera swings to a focus lat/lon and zooms in with a coordinates caption.
useFor: Global reach stats, travel and logistics routes, climate and space explainers, "we ship worldwide" beats. Use `textureSrc` for a real equirectangular map; set `background: "transparent"` to overlay.
source: prompt corpus x25 (globe with arcs, terminator, focus zoom)

points.doc: [{name, lat, lon, color?}] markers (only points used by an arc get a marker/label)

arcs.doc: [{from, to, at?, color?}] great-circle flights; from/to are point names or indexes, at = start frame

focus.doc: {lat, lon, at, label?, zoom?} camera swings and zooms to this place from frame `at`; null = never

textureSrc.doc: optional equirectangular day-map image (public/ path or URL); empty = procedural Earth

background.doc: backdrop outer colour ("transparent" to overlay the globe on your own scene)

nightLights.doc: show city lights on the night side

startLon.doc: longitude facing the camera at frame 0

stars.doc: draw a faint starfield behind the globe

size.doc: globe size multiplier (1 = about 80% of the short side)

title: Hex island grow
description: A flat-shaded low-poly hex island builds itself in an orthographic turntable: tiles rise from a faceted sea with a splash ring and damped overshoot, houses stack floor by floor with bounce and squash and get prism roofs, trees pop, a windmill turns, lamps and windows light as the day drifts to dusk.
useFor: "Growth" stories — a startup year, city planning, community, a product ecosystem; a satisfying loop for websites; pair with the faceted-sea look.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/lowpoly-island demo/world.js (MIT, LemoLab) — hex layout, rise/drop/pop arrival curves, one event per slot

radius.doc: island radius in hex rings (1-3); 2 = 19 tiles

buildings.doc: number of houses (1-3 floors each, prism roofs)

lamps.doc: number of lamp posts (glow at dusk)

boat.doc: a boat sails around the island once it is built

bpm.doc: build tempo: one tile per 16th note, floors per 8th

azimuthEnd.doc: camera azimuth at the end (turntable sweep)

timeStart.doc: time of day at the start: dawn | day | dusk | night

timeEnd.doc: time of day at the end (windows light as it darkens)

palette.doc: sand, sandSide, grass, earth, walls[], roofs[], pine[], leaves[] hex colours

title: Holographic globe
description: A wireframe Earth in cyan: coastlines draw on, a 10 degree graticule, fibonacci-dotted land, fresnel atmosphere, tilted orbit rings and a scan band; it turns onto a target, a beam and surface rings mark it, then the camera dives to a regional map with city dots and moving sea tracks.
useFor: Geo explainers, news intros, cyber / defence and logistics films. Pairs with target-lock and supply-route-map. transparent=true for an overlay.

turnAt.doc: frame the globe starts turning onto the target (1 s hermite)

diveAt.doc: frame of the dive into the regional map

dots.doc: fibonacci sample count for the dotted land

cities.doc: city dots on the regional map

tracks.doc: moving sea tracks on the regional map

title: Holo solid ignite
description: A cyan hologram wireframe builds up through a scan plane, then ignites into a translucent solid: faces fill with edge-bright Fresnel and scrolling interlace lines, a light wave climbs the model, lines thicken then settle, and a projector beam with rays and dust motes rises from the pad while it turntables.
useFor: The once-per-film "the whole thing is ready" launch beat for products, apps and logos.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/hologram-hud (MIT, LemoLab) — holo.js Fresnel faces + beam, STYLE.md

igniteAt.doc: frame the wireframe ignites into a solid

turns.doc: turntable turns over the whole duration

background.doc: stage colour, or "transparent" for an overlay

beam.doc: projector beam with rays and dust

motes.doc: number of dust motes in the beam

title: Iso blocks (3D clay)
description: Soft clay isometric 3D bar chart: a white ball with eyes hops down the bars painting each top orange, slams onto the tiled floor with a ripple, rolls back and rides a rising pillar while the caps un-paint — a seamless loop with a follow camera.
useFor: Declining (or any) metric stories, step-by-step progress, playful looping data explainers in real 3D.

values.doc: bar heights in slabs (any series; the ball hops left to right)

grooveColor.doc: colour of the gaps between tiles

ghost.doc: cap colour at the moment of touchdown

hopHeight.doc: hop arc height (world units, 1 = one cell)

zoomOut.doc: camera zoom at the reveal (1 = close follow)

title: Iso city build
description: A pastel isometric island builds itself in true orthographic 3D: floor tiles fall in rings from the centre with spin, squash and a cyan rim flash, the soil slab slides under, buildings, houses, trees, solar fields and wind turbines grow along a sweep front with overshoot and lagged roofs, a navy hero tower stacks in segments and lights up, windows glow, cars loop the ring road, drones ferry packets, and the camera pulls back to float the island top-right.
useFor: Smart-city, platform, ecosystem and architecture explainers; "watch it grow" openers; pass your own map rows and leave room for a title after the pull-back.
source: mg-styles-15 03-isometric 0.0-8.8 s, world.js / main.js / anim.js (MIT, Vincentwei1021) — technique after mg-styles-15

map.doc: rows of map chars: r road, b block, p plaza, c core (2x2 hero tower), w water, t tree, h house, s solar, u turbine, g grass

heroTower.doc: stack the navy hero tower on the c cells

drones.doc: drones carrying packets from the tower

pullback.doc: camera pulls back at 7.75 s to leave room for a title

pullTo.doc: where the island floats after the pull-back: top-right | center | top-left

title: Jelly type drop
description: Inflated glossy candy letters fall one per beat into a soft bed of two-tone capsules, sink past the surface, wobble back up with jelly squash-and-stretch and fire a damped ripple ring through the pill field on every landing; a late wave can hop the whole word again in reading order.
useFor: Playful brand word reveals and candy idents; with cloner-bed-ripple gives the full C4D-ident look in the browser.
source: mg-styles-15 04-3d-render 0.3-3.8 s, blender/sim.py bed_force / letter_track (MIT, Vincentwei1021) — technique after mg-styles-15

text.doc: the word (lowercase reads most candy-like, up to 10 letters)

beats.doc: drop time in seconds per letter (cycles if shorter than the word)

relift.doc: a late wave hops the letters again in reading order

seed.doc: unused variation seed (kept for spec compatibility)

title: Last object drop (engraved brass puck)
description: A single brass puck engraved with the final number falls with gravity into the centre of a walnut dial ringed by plate stacks, unwinds its yaw, lands with one tiny damped bounce while its shadow tightens; the room dims for a breath before the hit and an accent verdict settles.
useFor: Totals, ratios and "target met" endings for data films; the one heavy object that closes the argument.

value.doc: big engraved number on the puck face

topLine.doc: small engraved line above the number (e.g. a year)

material.doc: puck material: brass | copper | aluminium | stone | oak

dropAt.doc: frame the fall starts (lands 15 frames later)

stacks.doc: number of context stack pairs ringed around the dial (0 = bare dial)

caption.doc: accent verdict line that settles after the landing

introLine.doc: small spaced line at the top-left before the drop

title: Lidar canopy peel
description: A dense teal-to-pale point-cloud forest. A horizontal cut plane steps down on the beat; returns above it lift, glow white and vanish, a bright rim marks where the plane meets the crowns, and a height ruler with a canopy-height histogram tracks the cut. Bare-earth scan stripes remain at the end. Procedural seeded forest, slow orbit camera.
useFor: Archaeology / forestry / engineering reveals; "strip away the noise to find what matters" in product and brand stories.

cutKeys.doc: cut-plane heights in metres, one step per entry (30 → 0)

stepFrames.doc: frames per step (the move takes 45 % of it, then holds)

ramp.doc: three height-ramp colours low → mid → high

title: Light beam ribbon
description: A soft volumetric beam sweeps like a clock hand from a lighthouse lamp over a night sea: a camera-facing additive ribbon with a Gaussian profile, a root-bright core and a wide halo, tilted 7 degrees down, while the faceted water under it lights in a band with per-facet sparkles. An overlay mode draws only the beam.
useFor: Night scenes, "spotlight on X", searching / discovery / guidance metaphors, lighthouse and projector beats; overlay mode sweeps a beam across any host scene.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/lowpoly-island demo/world.js l.175-177 + sea.js beam-lit water (MIT, LemoLab)

bpm.doc: tempo used to time the sweep

beatsPerTurn.doc: beats for one full 360 degree turn (12 = a slow clock hand)

startAngle.doc: beam azimuth at frame 0 (degrees, ground plane)

tiltDeg.doc: degrees the beam points below horizontal

lighthouse.doc: draw the lighthouse the beam comes from

overlay.doc: draw only the beam on a transparent background (host scene shows through)

timeStart.doc: time of day at the start: dawn | day | dusk | night

timeEnd.doc: time of day at the end

elevation.doc: camera elevation (20-25 night shows more sky and stars)

title: Liminal office corridor (3D)
description: A handheld camcorder walks an endless, empty office of mustard wallpaper partitions on a 2.4 m grid under a drop ceiling of fluorescent troffers (a few dead, a few flickering), the far corridors fading into dark fog, one red EXIT sign far ahead and a REC / clock OSD.
useFor: Liminal / uncanny backdrops for horror-lite, mystery, "corporate dread" satire and found-footage openers.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/backrooms demo/world.js, tex.js, main.js handheld rig (MIT, LemoLab)

seed.doc: layout seed (partition placement, dead / flickering panels)

wallpaper.doc: wallpaper colour (pool tile #9fc7c0, school #b9c49a for alternatives)

fogDensity.doc: exponential fog density (higher = darker far corridors)

osd.doc: camcorder REC / battery / clock / date overlay

osdLabel.doc: camcorder on-screen-display label next to the red dot (osd: true)

title: Ocean surface 3D
description: A perspective sea built from Gerstner waves with analytic normals, fresnel sky reflection, sparkling sun glitter, crest foam and horizon fog under a gradient sky and sun glow; low-skim, high or drifting camera.
useFor: Travel, maritime and calm brand heroes, film openers, looping website backgrounds (put the words in HTML over it). For a stylised low-poly sea use faceted-sea instead.
source: prompt-corpus: awesome-opus5-5-videos (MIT) — Gerstner ocean cases (9), original implementation

skyZenith.doc: sky colour overhead (also what the sea reflects)

skyHorizon.doc: sky + fog colour at the horizon

sunElevation.doc: sun height above the horizon in degrees (low = long glitter path)

sunAzimuth.doc: sun direction in degrees (0 = straight ahead)

title.doc: optional serif title over the sea (empty = none)

title: Particle shape morph
description: A title glyph dissolves into ≈ 5 k sand-like particles that sweep (left first) into a rotating Fibonacci sphere around a red core, open into a tilted spinning torus, then collapse into a tiny glowing core with an orange bloom, while a mono caption tracks N and the stage.
useFor: "Ideas / data take shape" beats, logo-to-particle intros, tech-product hero loops; the collapse hands off to a shockwave or flash transition.

text.doc: word the particles start as (sampled from the rendered font)

shapes.doc: shape sequence: glyph | sphere | torus | ring | cube (glyph only makes sense first)

holdFrames.doc: frames each shape holds (the first glyph holds half of it)

morphFrames.doc: frames per morph (glyph → first shape is 20 % longer, swept left to right)

collapse.doc: end by collapsing everything into the glowing core

rotation.doc: rotation speed of the 3D shapes in degrees per second

captions.doc: show the mono "N = … · A → B" caption

title: Plan tilt to 3D
description: An ink floor plan draws on top-down, then the camera tilts to eye level as the walls extrude into a 3D line drawing, dollies through the front door, and cranes back up until it reads as the plan again.
useFor: Architecture, product or system explainers: show that the diagram and the 3D thing are the same; walk into a space.

walls.doc: wall segments [x1, z1, x2, z2] in metres (gaps = openings)

rooms.doc: floor labels {name, x, z, w, d} (w×d prints the area string)

furniture.doc: extruded blocks {x, z, w, d, h}

doors.doc: door swings {x, z, r, a0} (hinge point, radius, start angle)

entrance.doc: [x, z] of the front door the camera tilts to and walks through

wallHeight.doc: wall height in metres after extrusion

accent.doc: accent colour (last title line, construction line)

kicker.doc: small mono line above the headline

showTitle.doc: show the headline over the plan

walkIn.doc: dolly through the doorway before craning back up

mode.doc: 'tour' (default: tilt, walk in, crane back) or 'popup' (the flat line drawing rises off the page into a 3D ink model, camera tilts to an oblique and orbits)

popupFrames.doc: popup mode: frames each wall/object takes to rise (with paper-pop overshoot)

pageGhost.doc: popup mode: opacity of the flat wall footprints left on the page (0-1)

title: Plinth progress ring
description: A round matte studio plinth whose ~120-notch ring lights orange clockwise as a clay-voxel model is placed, stays lit while the model exists and drains grey while it lifts away: a progress / loading indicator that lives in the scene.
useFor: A loading / unlocking / onboarding-step indicator on a product pedestal; bind `progress` (0..1) to a counter, or leave it at -1 to auto-run fill, hold and drain.

progress.doc: ring fill 0..1 (model builds to this fraction); -1 = automatic fill, hold, drain

count.doc: number of notches on the ring

fillFrames.doc: frames to fill the ring (auto mode)

holdFrames.doc: frames the full ring is held before the lift

drain.doc: lift the model away and drain the ring at the end (loop seam)

percent.doc: show the small mono percentage readout

title: Point cloud orbit
description: An image (default: a procedural swordswoman) becomes a 3D cloud of coloured beads pushed forward by brightness; the camera orbits, beads extrude into voxel columns, then the figure disintegrates into white particles blown sideways.
useFor: Turn any still into a living 3D data sculpture; "Thanos snap" exits; tech/AI vision moments.
notes: Pass src for your own subject (a cut-out PNG works best).

src.doc: optional image in public/ (e.g. demo/owl.jpg); empty = procedural figure

depthScale.doc: how far brightness pushes beads toward the camera

beadSize.doc: bead diameter in world units (picture is 10 units tall)

extrusion.doc: 0..1 voxel column extrusion (0 = flat relief only)

disintegrate.doc: blow the cloud away at the end

direction.doc: +1 blow to the right, -1 to the left

speed.doc: particle drift speed (world units per second)

fringe.doc: RGB rim split on each bead (0 = off)

keyDark.doc: for images: luminance below this is keyed out (0 = keep all)

scan.doc: photo-to-points scan: a bright seam sweeps left to right; ahead of it the picture is a flat plate of beads, behind it the 3D relief stands up

scanFrames.doc: scan: frames the seam takes to cross (~3 s = 90)

craneTilt.doc: degrees the camera tilts up during the scan (0 = default gentle pitch); e.g. 44 for a nadir-to-oblique crane

title: Pop-up book spread
description: An open pop-up book on a walnut desk: flat cut-paper cards with die-cut borders flip up around their bottom edges with a springy overshoot — back row first, then forward — sway gently with soft contact shadows, and fold back down in the same order at the end. CSS-3D (no WebGL), so it is light enough for web heroes.
useFor: Children's stories, game trailers, feature-set 'unboxing', onboarding chapters, kids' edtech, playful website heroes.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/paper-popup (MIT code, CC BY 4.0 docs, LemoLab) — demo/sets.js popper/updatePops, DEMO.md motion numbers

title: Product turntable (3D hero shot)
description: A procedural can, bottle, box or phone (with your label image or a generated label) rises onto a seamless peach sweep lit by an image-based studio, orbits slowly 40 degrees while a key-light streak crosses its glossy surface, a soft contact shadow and floor reflection ground it, and a hero headline fades in beside it.
useFor: E-commerce, product launches, packaging reveals and hero sections: set `labelSrc` to your label artwork (for a phone, your screen), `colors` and the headline.
source: prompt corpus x15 (product on a seamless sweep, three-point light, slow orbit, light streak, reflection)

title: Shockwave flip field
description: A heavy chrome ball glides in, hangs for a beat, then slams into a bed of two-tone candy capsules: a shock front races outward and every pill it reaches leaps, tumbles half a turn and lands showing its other colour — the whole field recolours as the ring passes, nearby pills fly off frame, the camera kicks and the moment plays in brief slow motion.
useFor: A hero "state change" beat: brand colour takeover, before/after, launch moments; strong for idents and thumbnails.

title: Stack of plates (data physicalization)
description: Data series as stacks of real thin plates — brushed aluminium and milky acrylic with a brass ruler plate every 10th — assembling piece by piece on a walnut base in a warm studio, then the newest increase feeds in plate by plate while pinned readings roll with the landings.

title: Studio plinth stage

title: Sun shadow measure
description: A low winter sun swings across a white massing model while a clock readout runs; shadow sides go deep projected blue. Then one tower's shadow is traced as a cool fill with a bright edge while a range line with 100 m ticks grows from its base to the tip and a counter lands; the roofs inside the shadow ping on one by one.
useFor: Shadow-impact stories for a new building, solar-panel roof ranking, "daylight in a courtyard", sundial / education pieces, any measured "how far does it reach" beat.

own NOAA solar-position + analytic prism shadows

title: Voxel burst swirl
description: Clay-studio three.js scene: an original voxel creature on a round plinth shatters into ~1.1 k tumbling cubes that fly into a thick ring, orbit the plinth with the black eye voxels still readable, then fly back and reassemble into the creature so the clip ends on a finished, loopable frame (exit=lift sends the cloud up and out leaving the empty stage; also fall / scatter).

description: A voxel island with beach, grass, rock, block trees and a little hut builds itself as cubes drop in waves (low and central first, decorations last) in a sea of bobbing water cubes on a slab, under drifting cube clouds, with a slow orbiting camera, soft shadows and a cube-count caption.

description: Clay-studio three.js scene: ~1.1 k rounded orange cubes rain from above the frame and stack bottom-up into an original voxel creature on a round white plinth, while the plinth notch ring fills and a mono HUD counts the voxels; the creature then blinks and looks around.

title: White model projection (data as light)
description: A white massing model of a city on a dark plinth in a dark room. House lights snap off, a projector strikes with a flicker and a warm wash spreads from its axis lighting one set of buildings amber; a second layer pops buildings on one by one with a white flash, a rising level of light colours every facade by height, and a final pick-out lights one tower alone. The model never changes, only the light.
useFor: Data-as-light hero for urban planning, real-estate portfolios ("our sites by year"), campus plans, flood/height studies, infra and B2B brands; any "data on a physical model" museum-style piece.

own procedural city + SVG orbit renderer

title: Wireframe build

title: Auto-frame camera
description: Self-framing camera for build-up diagrams: as blocks are added the isometric scene pans and zooms (0.7 s easeInOutCubic) so the current assembly always fills the viewport with a constant margin, while the header and readouts never move. Dashed guides show the margin box and the content bounds.
useFor: Keeps any multi-step build-up diagram readable without hand-keyed cameras; the same `fitCamera` / `autoFrameAt` helpers (src/core/r2-x58-kit.tsx) drive any step-based motion.

steps.doc: array of {title, blocks:[{id,label,x,y,w,d,h,color}], links:[{from,to}]}; blocks are diffed by id between steps

margin.doc: margin around the content as a fraction of the viewport

guides.doc: show the dashed margin box and content bounds

zoomLabel.doc: word before the zoom value in the readout pill

boundsLabel.doc: legend text for the teal content-bounds guide ("- - " is prefixed)

title: Board camera (one huge board, one long dolly)
description: A very large board holds every idea in its own region; the camera dollies between regions with log-zoom weighting and small rolls, pushes into one symbol, then pulls back past the board edge to show the whole lesson hanging on a wall in an aluminium frame with a pen tray. Directional motion blur appears when the camera moves fast.
useFor: Turns hand-drawn motions into one continuous explainer: course intros, "how it works" product videos, onboarding; the full-board pull-back is a natural recap / end card. Regions can host any library motion via `layers`.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/whiteboard demo/engine/wb.js Camera / applyCam / Board.render (MIT, LemoLab) — own implementation

title: Canvas flythrough
description: One tall layout holding every section; a virtual camera flies between stations with a van Wijk smooth zoom (zooming out slightly while travelling, settling on a long ease, speed-proportional camera blur) and at the end pulls all the way out to reveal the whole canvas was a phone screen.
useFor: Explainers, product tours and pitch one-shot infographics: lay out sections as one canvas, list the stations, and let the camera do the storytelling.

title: Orbit parallax
description: 2.5D camera orbit around a cut-out subject: depth layers slide against each other while the subject turns slightly.

title: Rack focus
description: Focus pulls between a foreground, a subject and a background layer: blur follows depth, bokeh blooms, lens breathes.

title: Time remap clock
description: Explains and demonstrates the punctuation-hold clock: two balls on a track, one on the constant timeline, one on the remapped clock that eases to a full stop on each hold, then runs up to ~2x to catch back up; a live speed graph shows the dip, the stop and the sin² catch-up. The same pure remap (buildTimeRemap in src/core/r2-mg1b-kit.tsx) can drive any motion for musical breaths.
useFor: Visualising or tuning holds / slow-mo on beats; template for retiming any library motion without drifting off the timeline.

title: Flat person at desk
description: A geometric flat-vector person with round glasses works at a laptop in a cosy sunflower room (window with skyline and sun, framed print, swaying pendant lamp, plant, steaming mug); the room pops in with springs, they type and blink, the phone pings with a bell bubble, their head snaps round with an "!" mark, they reach for the phone and break into a smile, bobbing on the beat.

title: Sign drop & swing
description: A neon, comic banner or wooden sign drops in on ropes with a springy bounce, swings on a damped pendulum and settles into a gentle sway; neon flickers on after landing.

title: Silhouette runner (cut-paper chase)
description: A flat black cut-paper agent with a streaming red tie sprints on twos across red rooftops under a paper moon, leaping the gaps, chased by a taller villain in a wide brim whose red coat lining flashes as he runs.

title: Stickman rig
description: Round-capped stick figures with circle heads walk, run, punch, kick, fall, cheer, moonwalk, wave and dance from a joint-angle pose library with 2-bone IK legs; lines boil on twos and strikes trigger impact frames (flash, burst, hit-stop shake).

title: Toon object character
description: An everyday object (mug, box, bottle, can) becomes a 1930s rubber-hose cartoon character: pie eyes and a big mouth on its front, black noodle arms and legs, white four-finger gloves, huge round shoes, boiling ink outlines and a steam carrier that shows the mood; it walks in, hops with squash and stretch, points, waves and cheers.

boil.doc: ink boil amplitude in character units (0 = off)

title: Atom electron cloud builder
description: Dark blue space: a nucleus of protons and neutrons grows one proton per beat with a counter and an element symbol/name card updating (H, He, Li ...) while each new electron is a seeded particle swarm that spreads into its shell, expanding the electron cloud.

caption.doc: mono sub-line

protonNote.doc: floating note when a proton is added

title: Axis ratchet rescale
description: A pencil chart draws calmly until one value pierces the top frame line — torn red scar, 2-frame punch-in, decaying shake — holds the break for a beat, then the y-axis rescales in 4 ratchet clicks with every tick and mark sliding to its new position.
useFor: "Record-breaking" moments — a viral spike, price bubble, flood level, heat record — in any chart story; pairs with number-counter.

values.doc: the series; one value should exceed domainBefore

spikeIndex.doc: index of the record value (-1 = third from last)

domainBefore.doc: y domain before the rescale (the spike must overshoot it)

domainAfter.doc: y domain after the 4 ratchet clicks

subtitle.default: DAILY VISITS, THOUSANDS · ONE MARK PER DAY

note.doc: handwritten red note at the spike

title: Accelerating beat montage
description: Hard-cut image montage whose cuts accelerate 12 f -> 6 f -> 3 f, a persistent centre dot, breathing sonar rings on the beat, per-shot micro push and beat-synced style swaps.
useFor: Recaps, "so many examples" sequences, showreels, building energy before a reveal.

images.doc: public/ image paths cycled through the shots (empty = procedural scenes)

steps.doc: frames per cut for each block (accelerating)

counts.doc: number of shots in each block

bpm.doc: beat tempo: sets the sonar ring period and the dot pulse (150 bpm = 12 f)

shuffle.doc: 0..1 chance that a shot after the first block is restyled

styles.doc: styles to shuffle between: duotone | dot | invert

pingBeats.doc: insert 6-frame paper ping beats between blocks

mode.doc: images (default) | shapes (graphic match cuts: one circle keeps its centre and size while it becomes a wheel, roulette, pupil, moon, keyhole, target; steps [10,8,6,4] + dotColor as accent)

reverse.doc: replay the shots in reverse order with contracting rings (rewind / flashback; combine with steps [4,2])

shapePalette.doc: shapes mode: background colours cycled per shot

title: Cause and effect chain
description: Step boxes linked by dashed arrows; each arrow fills with a travelling pulse and the next box lights up, the colour sliding from the cause colour to the effect colour, ending with a pulse ring on the last box.
useFor: Domino-effect explainers, "how X leads to Y" chains, root-cause stories, economics / science / news cause chains — pass `steps` (2-7 short strings).

steps.doc: chain step texts, in order (up to 7)

title: Chip stack bars
description: Horizontal bars built from labelled unit chips, one chip per item: each row has a tiny tracked label above and a rolling count at the end, rows grow left to right chip by chip (about one chip per frame), and the highlighted row uses the accent colour with a gentle wave once complete.
useFor: A unit-chart (isotype) alternative to bar charts for counts of things that have names: parts per system, features per tier, ingredients per category.

rows.doc: rows[{label, items: string[] (chip texts), accent?: true}]

subtitle.doc: small tracked line under the headline

chipFrames.doc: frames per chip (1 = one chip per frame)

title: Crowd tracks
description: A locked-off concourse plate darkens and desaturates while every walker becomes a glowing sodium-orange dot trailing a decaying polyline of where it just was, linked to its nearest neighbour — people as data — with a lock-digit footfall count.
useFor: Footfall / mobility / network-activity explainers, smart-city and retail-analytics films, "everyone is connected" beats; drop a crowd still into `src`.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/city-symphony (MIT, LemoLab) — render.py Trails, lock_digits; poster docs/frames/city-symphony.jpg

revealAt.doc: frame where the plate starts darkening and the tracks appear

number.doc: counter value (digits lock left→right one per sixteenth); empty = no text

caption.doc: tracked line under the rule

src.doc: optional public/ crowd still used as the plate (procedural concourse otherwise)

title: DNA helix unzip
description: A rotating DNA double helix draws on, coloured A-T / G-C base-pair rungs fill in, then a zipper point runs along the axis and the two strands peel apart into half-rungs with letter tags.
useFor: Biology / genetics explainers, "copying the code" or "unlocking" metaphors, biotech and health intros.

unzipFrames.doc: length of the unzip in frames

letters.doc: show base letters on the separated half-rungs

seed.doc: seed for bases when sequence is empty

title: Dot tally (people as dots)
description: One dot per person in labelled groups; selected dots turn one by one from filled cream discs into open red rings while a huge counter runs; the total and a two-symbol legend land at the end.
useFor: Casualties, survey answers ("37 of 100 said…"), seats won, users affected, failure rates — a restrained alternative to a bar chart an agent can generate from two numbers.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/visual-investigation demo sPeople() (MIT, LemoLab) — idea, own SVG build

groups.doc: [{label, count, marked}] one grid per group; `marked` dots turn

ink.doc: colour of the filled dots and text

total.doc: text for the final big figure (default: number of marked dots)

title: Dot-to-stripes morph
description: A hand-drawn pencil dot chart on cream paper sweeps mark by mark into a full-height warming-stripes band: each dot falls to the band centre, stretches into its coloured stripe and loses its ink ring, while the graphite line fades and a handwritten note returns as a tiny pencil tick.
useFor: Climate / finance / health "the whole century in one band" reveals; the ramp centre, span and colours are props so it stays brand-safe.

orbitDeg.doc: camera orbit over the clip, degrees

description: A glowing gas-discharge tube sends light through a slit and a prism; a dark spectrum panel with an nm axis draws bright emission lines at element-specific wavelengths (hydrogen, helium, neon) as a scanner sweeps across, then swaps to the next gas.
useFor: Physics and chemistry explainers on atomic spectra, "how we know what stars are made of", element fingerprints, astronomy intros.

spectrumLabel.doc: caption after the gas name above the spectrum panel

labels.doc: show the paper label cards with handwritten values

yaw.doc: 3/4 view yaw in degrees (drifts +7° over the clip)

title: Flame test colours
description: A Bunsen-style burner on a lab bench: a wire loop dips into the flame, which turns crimson, yellow, lilac, green, red and orange for Li, Na, K, Cu, Sr and Ca with sparks, a label pill and the matching sample bottle lighting up.

title: Flow diagram (packets on edges)
description: Rounded boxes with icons joined by arrows that draw on in sequence (14 f each, 5 f stagger); glowing packets or labelled chips travel the edges, each receiving node pulses 1 -> 1.08 -> 1 and a highlight ring follows the active step. Auto-lays out left-to-right (top-to-bottom on portrait) from the edge graph; blueprint / paper / dark themes.

title: Function plot (curve, tangent, area)

title: Grid exception (the one that breaks out)
description: Swiss grid poster where everything moves in exact eased snaps and one red circle hesitates, then breaks out in the only linear move, growing and pausing mid-flight before landing off the grid; a mono readout flips from on grid to red off grid, the other elements re-flow nearest-first and the grid lines extend to fill the frame.

title: Ground-plane ruler
description: A measuring tape is laid on the ground of a photograph in true one-point perspective, its ticks crowding toward the horizon, while a big mono counter runs and lands on the measured distance.

title: Isometric bar-chart staircase
description: Data-driven clay-isometric bar chart on a tiled floor; a white eyed blob hops down it on the beat painting each cap orange (squash, confetti), the paint cascades, the floor ripples, and it rides a pillar back up — a seamless loop.

description: Isotype statistic: identical flat icons pop in with a back-ease overshoot into a grid, bar, row or heart silhouette, accelerating from quarter notes to 16ths while a big count-up number runs in sync; a highlighted subset turns accent and a legend reads "icon = N".

it was checked against the harbour charts held in the archive.

can be built while the existing crossing remains in service.

squeegee.doc: show the squeegee blade on each pull

title: Textbook energy lab
description: An open physics textbook on a sage desk under window-light shadows. The right-page pencil apparatus stands up: a ball rolls a U-track while three beakers (gravitational, kinetic, thermal) trade liquid levels, joined by glowing transfer arcs.
useFor: Explaining energy conservation, or any interactive-textbook look: a lesson page with a live diagram beside the formula.

default: A ball high on a track stores energy
in its height. Let it go, and that store
drains into motion at the bottom.
Climbing again, motion refills the store.
A little is always lost as heat.
bodyLines.doc: lines of body text on the left page

caption.default: Lift the flap to see the answer.
caption.doc: handwritten note in the answer box

friction.doc: energy lost to heat per frame (0 = none)

formulaNote.doc: handwritten note under the pendulum diagram

figLabel.doc: figure label in the bottom corner of the right page

title: Aurora curtain
description: Undulating teal-green aurora curtains shimmer over a navy starry sky, snowy mountains and an icy sea, with an optional pixel-art (pixelate + dither) look. Overlay-capable.
useFor: Polar / night / wonder / title-card backdrops; transparent overlay for any night sky.

backdrop.doc: paint sky, stars, mountains and ice

topColor.doc: faint tint at the curtain tops

strips.doc: broad soft strips behind the curtains (8-14 in source)

height.doc: curtain height as a fraction of frame height

pixelSize.doc: pixel-art block size at 1080p; 0 = smooth (6 = video21 look)

title: Iridescent bubbles
description: A packed foam of soap bubbles on a steel sink: rotating rainbow thin-film rims, jiggle, occasional pops and re-growth; "rising" mode sends bubbles up through deep water. Overlay-capable.
useFor: Clean / fresh / soap / fizz / bubbly-mood beats, underwater ambience; overlay bubbles on footage.

mode.doc: "cluster" (packed foam with pops) or "rising" (bubbles rising through water)

backdrop.doc: paint the steel sink (cluster) or deep-water gradient (rising)

hueSpeed.doc: thin-film rainbow rotation in degrees per second

foam.doc: tiny foam bubbles around the cluster

title: Caustics & god-rays
description: Underwater: a rippling caustic web at the surface, swaying light shafts and drifting motes; "pool" = full-frame scrolling caustic texture; "beam" = warm window light shaft with dust. Overlay-capable.
useFor: Ocean / underwater openers, pool or summer textures, quiet interiors with a single light shaft; layer over footage as light.
notes: Excellent calm web hero background for water / health / science brands.

mode.doc: "underwater" (surface web + god-rays), "pool" (full-frame caustic texture), "beam" (window light shaft + dust), "floor" (dark glossy floor: dancing RGB-fringed filaments, lens ring, coloured beat rings)

background.doc: CSS background; "transparent" = overlay (only light elements are drawn)

backdrop.doc: paint the procedural water / room

rayColor.doc: light shaft colour; empty = #E6FBFF underwater, #FFDC96 beam

fadeDepth.doc: fraction of height the surface caustics reach before fading (underwater)

intro.doc: pool mode: open on a wire grid that switches to caustics in 3 frames

rgbSplit.doc: floor mode: chromatic fringe strength of the filaments (0 = single colour)

lensRing.doc: floor mode: ring-shaped lens caustic around the centre

waveEvents.doc: floor mode: frames at which a coloured ring spreads out (empty = every ~36 frames)

accentA.doc: floor mode: ring colour near the centre

accentB.doc: floor mode: ring colour at the outer radius

title: City skyline (window flicker, dusk to night)
description: Seeded procedural city: three depth rows of buildings with setbacks, water tanks, antennas and window grids that flicker on and off; the sky goes from dusk to night as more windows light up, with traffic on the street and an optional aerial crane pull-back from one window to the whole skyline. Sketch style gives the hatched pencil-on-paper look.
useFor: Urban establishing shots, "the city at night", time passing, ending pull-backs, backdrops behind titles.

pullback.doc: start close on one window and crane back to the whole city

toNight.doc: sky grades from dusk to night while windows switch on (flat style)

litRatio.doc: share of windows lit at full night

stepFrames.doc: frames between window flicker steps (5 = 0.17 s)

traffic.doc: cars with head/tail lights on the street

lightsMode.doc: 'flicker' (default, windows toggle randomly) | 'sequence' (every window lights once, one by one on the cadence, with a white bloom pop, until the city glows)

lightsStart.doc: sequence: first frame a window can light

lightsSpan.doc: sequence: frames over which all windows have lit

cadence.doc: sequence: lighting steps every N frames (2-4 = steady cadence; match the beat)

glowColor.doc: sequence: lit window / glow colour (empty = windowColor)

title: Conveyor flow
description: Storybook workshop doors swing open and identical products (cassettes, boxes, cards or your image) roll out one after another on a wooden perspective belt toward the lower right, growing with depth at an even spacing while slats scroll and rollers turn.
useFor: "Output / production / shipping" metaphors: many generated items (videos, orders, builds) leaving a system; pass itemSrc for your own product.

background.doc: 'scene' = procedural gouache street + workshop, or a CSS colour (belt + items only)

itemSrc.doc: optional image (public/ path or URL) used as the item instead

startAt.doc: frame the first item leaves the doors

travelFrames.doc: frames for an item to ride the whole belt (≈ 3 s)

itemSize.doc: item width at the near end, in u

openDoors.doc: swing the workshop doors open at the start

sign.doc: text on the plaque above the door (empty = blank)

ticks.doc: small action ticks over the door as each item appears

title: Curl-flow swirl
description: Hundreds of coloured ribbons stream through a turbulent curl-noise vortex around a dark spiky pupil, inside a red magnifier lens on cream paper (or full-frame). Overlay-capable.
useFor: Inspection / insight / chaos-under-the-lens beats, psychedelic or hypnotic transitions, "looking closer" moments.

backdrop.doc: paper texture, iris lines, magnifier handle and boiling sketch arcs

lens.doc: clip the flow inside a magnifier lens circle; false = full frame

pupil.doc: dark spiky pupil at the vortex centre

title: Deep-sea depth descent
description: Underwater descent infographic: a bobbing brass bathysphere hangs on its cable while the world scrolls up past it — surface god-rays, a fish school, glowing jellyfish, a trench wall and the seafloor — the water darkens with depth, marine snow drifts, the headlamp beam rises as light falls, a depth counter with pressure/light/temperature counts top-left, a log-scale depth ruler with landmark ticks scrolls on the right and zone titles blur in letter by letter.
useFor: Scale explainers ("how deep / how far / how big"), descending through levels or eras, any ranked list read as depth.
source: video23 0:00-1:30 depth-descent-scroll, depth-counter-hud, log-depth-ruler, bathysphere-idle-bob, headlamp-beam, marine-snow-particles, zone-title-blur-swap

landmarks.doc: ruler ticks + zone titles: [{depth, label, note}] (depth in metres)

maxDepth.doc: depth reached at the end (counter stops here)

holdFrames.doc: frames held at the bottom at the end

scrollSpeed.doc: world scroll speed in px per frame at 1080 (constant, decoupled from the counter)

heroSrc.doc: optional public/ image to replace the procedural bathysphere

hud.doc: show the counter and zone titles

background.doc: colour behind the water (normally fully covered)

waterTop.doc: water colour at the top of the frame per depth, 8 hex colours for depths 0/100/300/800/1500/3000/4500/6000 m; [] = default ocean ramp

waterBottom.doc: water colour at the bottom of the frame per depth (8 hex colours), [] = default ocean ramp

ruleColor.doc: underline rule colour under the zone title

title: Embers & gold flecks
description: Golden additive sparks rising and twinkling over a fire glow; "motes" = slow soft glowing ember dots, "gold" = spinning Klimt gold flecks with sparkle pulses. Overlay-capable.
useFor: Warmth, fire, magic, craft/forge or luxury beats; drop over any dark scene as an additive ambience layer.
notes: mode motes + low count is the classic subtle accent over any dark scene (blend screen).

mode.doc: "sparks" (fast golden sparks), "motes" (slow glowing dots), "gold" (spinning gold flecks), "fireflies" (40-60 warm dots wandering on smooth noise paths, each with a short comet tail, blinking at its own rate)

background.doc: CSS background; "transparent" = overlay (particles use screen blend)

backdrop.doc: paint the procedural dark fire-glow (or Klimt) backdrop

glow.doc: soft glow halos and fire glow

tail.doc: fireflies: number of trail dots behind each firefly (6)

blink.doc: fireflies: average blink period in seconds (1.5-3)

band.doc: fireflies: [top, bottom] vertical band 0..1 the swarm wanders in

title: Falling petals / leaves / papers
description: Petals (or autumn leaves, or paper sheets) sway, spin and flip in 3D as they fall in three depth layers past a blossom branch over a soft meadow. Overlay-capable.
useFor: Spring / romance / seasons / time passing; papers for office chaos, letters, bureaucracy; overlay on any scene.

mode.doc: "petals", "leaves" or "papers"

backdrop.doc: paint the procedural sky / meadow / branch

branch.doc: draw the blossom (or autumn) branch in the top-left

title: Fireworks
description: Staggered fireworks over a night city: a faint launch streak climbs, a white flash ball holds for a few frames, then a peony of sparks expands with an ease-out-cubic, droops under gravity, fades from the core out and twinkles away, while a warm global light pulse briefly lifts the whole scene.
useFor: Celebrations, launches, milestones, "it worked!" beats, festive end cards.
notes: scene:false = transparent bursts over your own scene (use blend screen).

radius.doc: burst radius in u (195 = 18 % of a 1080 frame)

flashFrames.doc: frames the white flash ball holds

fadeFrames.doc: extra frames for the sparks to fade and twinkle out

lightPulse.doc: peak opacity of the warm global light pulse

scene.doc: paint the night sky + city (false = transparent overlay)

title: Fish school + jellyfish
description: Underwater scene: a loose school of fish sweeps across the frame along an eased Bézier S-curve, each fish trailing at its own lag with tail wobble, depth-faded colour and gentle wander, past pulsing glowing jellyfish, swaying kelp, god-rays and drifting particles.
useFor: Ocean / nature beats, "moving together" or crowd metaphors, calm ambient backgrounds.

count.doc: number of fish in the school

path.doc: cubic Bézier control points [[x,y] x4] as fractions of the frame; the school travels it over the clip (ease in-out)

spread.doc: half-width of the school across its path (u)

title: V-formation flock
description: A V-formation of red-crowned cranes flies right-to-left over snowy peaks: birds shrink with depth along each arm, flap on twos with offset phases (white down-strokes, grey-blue up-strokes) and bob against their wings, while a lone paper crane swoops in from the lower right and takes the last slot.
useFor: Migration / journey / teamwork beats, "joining the group" metaphors, sky interludes.

count.doc: number of real cranes (including the leader)

angleDeg.doc: angle of the V arms (degrees from horizontal)

scaleFalloff.doc: size factor per bird toward the back (depth)

period.doc: flap cycle in frames (25 = 0.833 s, drawn on twos)

paperCrane.doc: a paper crane flies in and joins the formation

joinFrames.doc: frames it takes to reach its slot

mountains.doc: snowy peaks, cloud banks and conifers below

title: Flow lines (wind / heat / steam / waves)
description: Wavy streamlines: wind lines with end curls across a sky, rising heat wiggles over a desert road, soft steam wisps from a bowl, or braided pencil wave rows on paper. Overlay-capable.
useFor: Show air, heat, smell, sound or time: breeze over a landscape, a hot day, a hot meal, a ripple/time wipe.
notes: mode waves on paper makes a good section divider band.

mode.doc: "wind", "heat", "steam", "waves" or "ink-curls" (wind drawn as ~@ ink curls spawning behind a moving object that draw on, then erase from the tail, with falling leaf dabs)

backdrop.doc: paint the mode scene (sky / desert road / kitchen bowl / paper)

color.doc: line colour; empty = mode default (#5A6FAE / white / white / ink #2B2622)

count.doc: lines per frame; 0 = mode default (7 / 16 / 8 per source / 16)

curlProbability.doc: wind: chance a line ends in a curl

sources.doc: steam: [[x, y], ...] emitter positions as frame fractions (default bowl at [0.5, 0.66])

fade.doc: waves: 0.35 s fade in at the start and out at the end (wipe use)

followPath.doc: ink-curls: [[x, y], ...] frame fractions the hero object travels along (empty = a gentle wave left to right)

spawnEvery.doc: ink-curls: frames between curl spawns (one per beat, e.g. 12)

drawFrames.doc: ink-curls: frames a curl takes to draw on (0.4 s = 12)

life.doc: ink-curls: frames before a curl has erased itself from its tail

dabs.doc: ink-curls: number of leaf-shaped wash dabs tumbling after the hero

dabColors.doc: ink-curls: foliage colours for the dabs (empty = greens / ochre)

title: Fog and clouds (parallax)
description: Three parallax layers of drifting noise-built clouds (lit white cumulus with soft grey undersides), low ground fog over dark ridges, or a wide soft mist; layer speeds run 1 : 2 : 4, blur grows toward the front and a screen-blended sun glow scatters through them.
useFor: Skies for heroes, passing through clouds, mood and ambience; overlay-capable (`background: "transparent"`) over any scene or website hero.
source: prompt corpus x23 (layered drifting clouds / ground fog, parallax, light scattering)

colors.doc: [light, shade] cloud colours (fog / mist use the light colour only)
