sunPos.doc: [x, y] of the sun as fractions of the frame

background.doc: 'auto' (sky gradient for the style) | 'transparent' | any CSS background

ridge.doc: dark ridge silhouettes behind fog / mist (auto background only)

title: Grass field (teal blades + golden leaves)
description: Procedural tapered teal grass blades grow up from the bottom edge in a staggered wave, golden pointed leaves pop up behind, and the whole field sways with travelling wind gusts under a starry night sky.
useFor: A living foreground for night/sunrise scenes, an opening or end-card ground plane, a calm nature beat.

horizon.doc: sky colour at the bottom edge

bladeBase.doc: front blade colour at the base

bladeTip.doc: front blade colour at the tip

golden.doc: add the row of golden pointed leaves behind the teal blades

goldenAt.doc: frame the golden leaves start popping up

growAt.doc: frame the teal blades start growing (-1 = already grown)

swayAmp.doc: base sway in degrees (2.5 s period)

gust.doc: extra lean of the travelling wind gust (degrees)

windSpeed.doc: speed multiplier for sway and gusts

motes.doc: floating pollen motes drifting on the wind

title: Insect dart flight (dragonflies / fireflies)
description: Red dragonflies zig-zag over a sunny lotus pond in fast expo-eased darts separated by jittery hovers, their translucent wings flickering every frame, and one lands on a lotus bud and folds its wings; firefly mode fills a night meadow with glowing, blinking fireflies drifting between waypoints.
useFor: Nature ambience, "a small idea arrives / lands" beats, summer or night atmosphere.

dartFrames.doc: frames per dart (dragonfly; fireflies are slower)

holdFrames.doc: hover frames between darts

land.doc: the first dragonfly lands on the lotus bud

scene.doc: paint the pond / meadow background (false = transparent overlay)

title: Lamp screen (shadow-theatre cloth)
description: A warm cotton shadow-theatre screen in a lacquered stage frame (optional blurred audience heads) lit from behind by flickering oil lamps; the pierced subject is transmitted light: dyes glow, holes shine, overlaps darken. More lamps bleach the cloth, snuffing steps it back to gold.
useFor: The light is the world: lights switching on one by one (servers, city, a fever), folklore and heritage explainers, festival openers; turns any silhouette or icon set into a warm theatre scene.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/shadow-puppet demo/gl.js, demo/main.js (lamps, exposure), DEMO.md "Rendering constants" (MIT, LemoLab)

lamps.doc: lamp positions [{x,y}] as fractions of the frame

snuffAt.doc: frame each lamp is snuffed (-1 = never; 0.35 s gutter + smoke)

src.doc: optional image used as the transmission layer (dark = shadow)

subjectAt.doc: frame the subject is pressed onto the cloth

stage.doc: lacquered lintel, pillars and gold cloud curls

audience.doc: blurred audience heads along the bottom

title: Light-band stained-glass window
description: A tall leaded window with four lancets and a rose in a dark ashlar wall: a soft band of coloured sunlight travels across it (dawn, noon, afternoon, dusk, moon) so the lit lancet glows jewel-bright with a shaft, dust and a floor patch while the others go dark and milky and freeze their figures.
useFor: Light as time: recipe steps, the seasons of a farm, factory shifts, chapters of a biography, a product line-up lit in turn; strong heritage or holiday look.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/stained-glass demo/comp.js, window.js, scene.js (MIT, LemoLab)

panes.doc: one object per lancet: caption, sky, sky2, sun, hill, accent colours (2-5 lancets)

schedule.doc: sun path keys: at (frame), sunU (0..1 across the window), colour, intensity

bandWidth.doc: extra band width beyond a lancet, in u

rose.doc: show the rose window (dark at night)

shafts.doc: light shafts, dust and floor patch

dust.doc: number of dust motes in each shaft

background.doc: page colour behind the wall (normally covered)

recess.doc: dark window recess colour (behind the glass)

titleColor.doc: carved title colour (tinted by the sun colour)

captionColor.doc: pane caption colour when unlit (tinted by the sun colour)

dustColor.doc: dust mote colour in the shafts

title: Paper-cut lightbox (纸雕灯)
description: A glowing paper-cut lamp scene in eight stacked sheets: starry pulp sky, a moon with halo, auspicious clouds with carved spirals, two mountain ranges, a village whose warm windows switch on one by one, a river with a broken moon trail, a dark tree and reeds, and blurred hanging lanterns that flicker — each sheet casting a soft shadow on the one behind while the lamp turns on back-to-front and the camera creeps in.
useFor: Festival greetings (Mid-Autumn, Diwali, holidays), gift and brand stories, cosy website hero backgrounds (reduced-motion still = lamp fully on).
source: lemo-opuscar styles/paper-lantern (MIT code, CC BY 4.0 docs, LemoLab) — demo/src/paper.js, stage.js, art.js, shots/s01_night.js

light.doc: backlight point {x, y (0..1), color ("" = ladder default), radius}

windows.doc: how many village windows switch on

lampOnAt.doc: frame the lamp starts turning on (moon first)

lampOnStagger.doc: frames between each sheet lighting, back to front

windowsAt.doc: frame the first window switches on

title: Lightning flash relight
description: A rainy night house scene is relit by lightning: a forked bolt draws on, the frame flashes to a pink storm-lit plate for 2 frames and decays back to night in ~0.3 s; repeatable, with double strikes. Overlay-capable.
useFor: Drama, shock, revelation or horror punctuation; a storm establishing shot; overlay the flash + bolt on any night footage.

background.doc: CSS background; "transparent" = overlay (bolt + screen flash + rain only)

backdrop.doc: paint the night house scene and its lit plate

sheetFlashes.doc: frames of distant cloud-only flickers (no bolt, ~0.35 intensity)

holdFrames.doc: frames the flash holds at full brightness

decay.doc: exponential decay time constant in seconds (0.1 = source)

doubleStrike.doc: second flash 3 frames after the hold at 0.6 intensity

shake.doc: camera jolt in px on strike frames

title: Mesh gradient backdrop
description: Big soft pools of violet, blue, cyan and magenta light drifting slowly over an indigo-black base, gently breathing, with an optional ripple of light and fine grain: the 2025-26 tech-brand backdrop.
useFor: Hero sections, AI product pages, keynote slides and any video that needs a calm premium moving backdrop. Cheap CSS mode: safe as a website MotionBackground (overlay=true for transparent base).

speed.doc: drift speed multiplier (1 = 24-40 s loops, default 2.2 so an 8 s clip visibly moves)

rippleAt.doc: frame of a light ripple that pushes the pools outward (-1 = none)

overlay.doc: transparent base so it layers over host content

title: Mode-7 lobby floor
description: An art-deco lobby in true one-point perspective: a checkered marble floor with a burgundy runner slides under a dollying camera, with depth darkening, gold pilasters and glowing sconces receding on both walls, warm mirrored glow pools and a sunburst door at the end of the hall.
useFor: Instant lobby / stage / hallway depth behind titles or characters: hotels, galas, luxury, theatre, "walk into the event" openers.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/art-deco demo/scenes/lobby.js mode-7 floor (MIT, LemoLab)

speed.doc: dolly speed in tiles per second

camY.doc: camera eye height in tiles (lower = more floor drama)

sway.doc: gentle lateral camera sway in tiles

endDoor.doc: show the glowing sunburst door at the end of the hall

title: Outrun grid
description: One-point-perspective neon floor grid scrolling toward the camera to a hot horizon, a banded retro sun with scrolling cut-out stripes, ridged wireframe mountains, palm silhouettes and reflector posts whipping past, a starry sky with a shooting star and a tail-lit car; beats fire a bright shock line across the floor and pump the sun.
useFor: Retro / synthwave backdrop for music, gaming and 80s-themed promos, or a website hero loop (export to webm on mobile).

speed.doc: floor travel speed in world units per second (it ramps in over the first second)

sunRise.doc: frames for the sun to rise

pulses.doc: frames of kick hits: shock line across the floor + sun pump

horizonY.doc: horizon height as a fraction of the frame

title: Paper cut-out layers (stop-motion)
description: A scene built from flat coloured paper layers with deckled edges and soft drop shadows that grow with depth, fibre grain over everything: layers slide up with a 4-8 degree rotation that settles to 0, a sun, clouds, three hills, a paper sea and a sailboat bob and drift in parallax, a paper-cut title lands last, all stepped on twos (12 fps stop-motion).
useFor: Kids / education explainers, festive greetings, charity stories and warm brand films: pass your own `layers` (shapes or text) and `palette`; reuse `paperShape` / `DeckleFilter` / `paperShadow` from r2-pr1-kit to give any SVG scene the paper look. For a fixed pop-up landscape see paper-diorama.

layers.doc: [{kind:'rect'|'circle'|'hill'|'wave'|'cloud'|'tree'|'star'|'blob'|'sail'|'ring'|'text', color: hex | palette index, x, y (centre, % of frame), w (bands: % of frame width; objects: % of the short side; text: % of frame width), h? (bands: % of frame height), depth 0-4, delay?, rot?, text?}]

palette.doc: colours that layers can reference by index

step.doc: hold each drawing for n frames (2 = 12 fps stop-motion)

title: Paper diorama
description: A pop-up-book landscape of 8 cut-paper layers with fibre texture, torn light rims and soft inter-layer shadows; a slow multiplane dolly, a walking paper critter on a stone bridge, a flowing stream and a golden guide star that ignites and leaves a trail.
useFor: Storybook / brand-journey openers, children’s education, calm website hero loops and chapter backgrounds with a title in the sky band.
source: video x5 0:00-0:06 (alpine sunset scene, measured dolly 6.5-11 s)
video x5 every scene (layer stack, palette)

showHero.doc: show the paper critter on the bridge

heroSrc.doc: optional public/ image (transparent PNG) to stand on the bridge instead of the critter

heroX.doc: hero x as a fraction of width (keep it on the left third, eye line to the star)

starAt.doc: frame the guide star ignites (bloom + sparkle spray + trail)

dolly.doc: push-in rate in %/s at depth 1 (far layers move 40 %)

pan.doc: lateral truck in px/s at depth 1 (0 = pure push-in)

dof.doc: blur (px at 1080p) on the nearest foreground layer

title.doc: optional title set in the sky band (Fraunces)

title: Parallax landscape truck / speed-run
description: Layered flat-vector landscape (sky and clouds, two mountain ranges, distant fields with a village, a hill, a tree row, foreground and whizzing near blades) trucking sideways at depth-proportional speeds with a flapping paper crane; speed-run mode ramps to a gallop-speed rush over a savanna with a fixed giant sun, horizontal streak blur on the near layers and light streaks.
useFor: Travel and progress beats, establishing shots, "moving fast" moments behind a hero character.

mode.doc: "truck" (slow camera truck) or "speedrun" (ramp up to a rush, blur streaks, ramp down)

speed.doc: truck mode foreground speed in px per frame at 1080

peakSpeed.doc: speed-run peak foreground speed in px per frame (123 = 3700 px/s)

layerFactors.doc: speed factors for [far mtn, near mtn, fields, hill, trees, ground, front blades]; [] = auto per mode

finish.doc: 'flat' (default) | 'papercut' (flat paper sheets from a tonal ladder, back sheets glowing and light, front near-black, each casting a soft shadow on the next; grass and tufts are dropped)

shadow.doc: papercut: shadow strength multiplier (1 = 2.6 / 3.6 px blur 5)

title: Pop-up layer rise
description: A cut-paper landscape assembles like a pop-up book: over the existing sky each paper layer slides up into place, far layers first and the nearest last from furthest down (easeOutCubic, no overshoot), then holds with a slow dolly and drops back out near-first with motion blur.
useFor: "Opening the book" intros for any layered illustration, chapter openers, exploded-view build-ins and slide build-ins.
source: video x5 47.6-48.3 s (reversed inside the layer swap)

direction.doc: 'up' = layers rise from below (pop-up book) | 'down' = layers drop in from above

duration.doc: frames each layer takes to land (easeOutCubic)

riseBase.doc: travel of the farthest layer as a fraction of height

risePerDepth.doc: extra travel per unit depth (the nearest layer travels riseBase + risePerDepth)

exitAt.doc: frame the layers drop back out near-first (0 = no exit)

exitFrames.doc: frames each layer takes to drop out (easeInCubic)

guideStar.doc: golden guide star ignites once the scene has landed

title.doc: optional title in the sky band (fades in after the build)

title: Print wave
description: An original woodblock-style wave: a tall wall of water in bokashi blues (pale crest → Prussian → deep trough) with offset banding and grouped broken white flow lines along the back slope, a hollow shaded under the curling lip, a scalloped foam rim, fractal claws (each splits into three fingers that split again, tips hooking inward) over a pale back layer, spray in clusters, and a background sea of banded curls. It swells, curls and hangs with jitter ×0.25; nature steps at 8 fps. Paper, double border, ink outlines.
useFor: Dramatic climax or backdrop for Japanese-themed content, "a wave of …" metaphors (sales surge, data flood, demand spike); pairs with frame-breakout.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/ukiyoe/demo/wave.js + DEMO.md (MIT, LemoLab) — original composition, not the Great Wave

crestAt.doc: frame the swell reaches its crest

clawDepth.doc: claw recursion 1–3 (each level splits into 3 fingers)

border.doc: draw the paper margin + double border (off for a full-bleed layer)

title: Rain
description: Night street in the rain: 3 parallax layers of slanted streaks, lamp-lit cone, ground ripples; optional glass droplets and trickles. Works as a transparent overlay.
useFor: Moody/rainy ambience under any scene; set background "transparent" to lay rain over footage, glass: true for a window POV.

background.doc: CSS background; "transparent" = overlay mode (no painted street)

backdrop.doc: paint the procedural night street (sky, blocks, wet road, lamp)

density.doc: streak + ripple count multiplier (1 = 150/300/600 per 1080p frame)

angle.doc: degrees from vertical; positive falls to the right

ripples.doc: expanding ripple ellipses on the ground band

groundY.doc: fraction of height where the ground / ripple band starts

glass.doc: window-glass POV: droplets with highlights, slow trickles, backdrop blurred

glassDrops.doc: number of static droplets per 1080p frame

lamp.doc: street lamp with volumetric cone that lights the streaks

reflection.doc: wet-ground reflection of the lights: none | streaks (neon-noir: blurred flipped streaks + ripple bands) | dabs (painterly stacked knife dabs, shimmering on twos)

reflectionColors.doc: colours of the extra reflected neon lights (each adds one column)

title: Rocket launch
description: Countdown on a dusk launch pad, ignition with billowing ground smoke and a flickering plume, an ease-in lift-off and a camera that tilts up to follow the rocket as the sky turns to space, leaving a smoke trail.
useFor: Launch metaphors for product releases, "we shipped" reveals, space / science education; pair with number-counter or a title for the label.
source: prompt-corpus: awesome-opus5-5-videos (MIT) — rocket launch metaphor cases (8), original implementation

countdown.doc: seconds counted down before ignition (0 = no countdown)

sublabel.doc: small mono line under the label

seed.doc: seed for smoke, clouds and stars

skyTop.doc: sky colour at the zenith while still on the ground

skyHorizon.doc: sky colour at the horizon (dusk glow)

space.doc: colour the sky fades to at altitude

countdownLabel.doc: small mono label under the big countdown number

title: Segmented worm breach
description: A giant panelled mechanical worm with a toothed circular mouth bursts out of a cream line-art desert in a dust plume, arcs toward camera and dives back; optional translucent cyan x-ray pass.
useFor: Hero reveal of a colossal machine/creature, desert or sand worlds, sci-fi cold opens, product-as-monster metaphors.

xrayColor.doc: cyan used in the x-ray pass

xray.doc: turn the worm translucent cyan x-ray for the middle of the clip

seed.doc: seed for panels, dunes and dust

title: Snowfall
description: Layered snow drifting diagonally over a dusk snowy landscape; blizzard mode streams pixel snow and streaks sideways through a blue-grey white-out. Overlay-capable.
useFor: Winter / cold / quiet beats; blizzard for harsh weather, isolation or a white-out scene change; set background "transparent" to snow over anything.

mode.doc: "drift" (soft layered snow), "blizzard" (horizontal pixel snow + white-out) or "stab" (woodcut teardrop flecks on black; background "#3A5D80" default becomes near-black)

backdrop.doc: paint the procedural landscape / white-out

density.doc: flake count multiplier (drift 520/240/60, blizzard 600 per 1080p frame)

streaks.doc: extra fast wind streak lines in drift mode (video2 hydrant look), e.g. 120

pixelSize.doc: blizzard pixel size in px at 1080p (6 = source)

freezeAt.doc: stab: frame at which the flecks freeze mid-air (-1 = never)

reinkFrom.doc: stab: frame the flecks start being inked back in one by one (-1 = off)

angle.doc: stab: shared fall angle in degrees

sizeRange.doc: stab: [min, max] fleck radius in px at 1080p

title: Starfield night
description: Dark teal night sky with twinkling cream stars, a grainy crescent moon that fades in, swaying teal grass and a shooting star. Overlay-capable.
useFor: Calm night / sleep / dream / wish beats, end cards and quiet intros; transparent overlay for stars over any sky.

background.doc: CSS background; "transparent" = overlay (stars, moon, shooting star only)

backdrop.doc: paint the teal sky gradient, grass and print grain

moonPos.doc: [x, y] moon centre as fractions of the frame

moonPhase.doc: crescent thickness: inner-circle offset as a fraction of the radius (0.42 = source)

shootingAt.doc: when the shooting star starts, as a fraction of the duration

grass.doc: swaying teal grass silhouette along the bottom

grain.doc: static print speckle over the frame

ripple.doc: {x, y, at}: a wave of brightened twinkles spreads from that point (0..1 fractions) starting at that frame - a "star arriving home" / payoff accent; null = off

title: Studio sweep (graphite seamless backdrop)
description: A dark graphite photographic seamless: a soft radial gradient with the floor implied only by a blurred contact shadow beneath a glossy subject, and a slow narrow softbox light sweep gliding across the set.
useFor: Instant premium packshot background for product cut-outs (src PNG with alpha), logos and 3D motions; set `subject: "none"` for a bare backdrop.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/teardown STYLE.md §2–3, demo/src/main.js sweep light (MIT, LemoLab)

radius.doc: gradient radius as a fraction of the frame

sweepFrames.doc: length of the sweep in frames (4.2 s default)

src.doc: optional alpha PNG (public path) shown instead of the demo subject

title: Sun rise / sun set
description: Sunrise: a huge orange gradient disc rises from behind teal grass with an ease-out, grows a ring of spike rays and golden leaves pop up over a starry night. Sunset mode: stepped purple-to-peach sky bands, a cream sun with rotating dashed rays sinks behind the horizon and the sky darkens to dusk.
useFor: Openers, "a new day" beats, endings and time-passing; a giant backlight disc behind a hero.

mode.doc: "rise" (video15 sunrise disc) or "set" (video1 sunset descent)

rayCount.doc: number of rays (70 rise, try 36 for set)

rayLength.doc: ray length in u (rise) / ray length scale (set)

golden.doc: golden leaves pop up after the rise

moon.doc: crescent moon that sinks and fades as the sun rises

bands.doc: sunset sky band colours, top to horizon (set)

duskBands.doc: the same bands at full dusk (set)

bandStyle.doc: set mode: 'wobble' (default soft wobbly band tops) | 'thinning' (flat colour stepping into the next via thinning stripes — instant screen-print sky, no gradients)

sunRings.doc: set mode: concentric rings around the sun disc (0 = none, 2-3 = print look)

stripes.doc: set mode, bandStyle 'thinning': stripes per band transition (5)

land.doc: land layer colours far to near (set)

title: Time-of-day grade (day to night)
description: A simple procedural hillside village whose sky gradient and colour grade keyframe from day through golden hour, dusk pink and mauve to night: the sun arcs down and sets behind the hills, clouds pick up the sunset, a multiply night grade cools everything, the moon and stars come out and the house windows switch on one by one.
useFor: Time passing, "by the end of the day", before/after moods, calm transitions between story beats.

stops.doc: grade keyframes [{t 0..1, skyTop, skyBottom, sun, grade}] (grade = multiply wash colour)

holdStart.doc: frames held at the first stop

holdEnd.doc: frames held at the last stop

lights.doc: house windows switch on as it gets dark

lightsAt.doc: darkness (0..1) at which the first windows light

nightGrade.doc: strength of the #0C1A2E night multiply layer (video16 uses 0.75)

sun.doc: sun disc that sets behind the hills

hills.doc: hill colours far, mid, near (before grading)

roofColor.doc: roof colour A (houses alternate randomly with B)

season.doc: off (day to night) | cycle (spring -> summer -> autumn -> winter with petals, leaves, snow) | spring | summer | autumn | winter (one fixed season)

seasonFrames.doc: cycle: frames per season (0 = split the duration in four; 2-4 s each is typical)

seasonFade.doc: cycle: crossfade frames between seasons (≈30 in the source)

title: Top-down terrain scroll
description: Bird’s-eye view: a fixed paper crane (with hatched cast shadow and streaming dashed trail) flies over seeded top-down terrain — fields, river and town roofs, ocean with a whale breach, desert dunes, snowy peaks, night city, autumn forest — that scrolls diagonally with a speed ramp and hard-cuts between biomes.
useFor: Journeys and "around the world" montages, travel/progress beats, map-like transitions under a hero.

biomes.doc: list of biomes: farmland | ocean | desert | snow | city | forest

montage.doc: hard-cut through all biomes (true) or scroll only the first one (false)

speed.doc: ground speed in px per frame at 1080 (8 = source farmland speed)

speedRamp.doc: speed multiplier reached at the end (1.96 = 8 -> 15.7 px/f as in the source)

angle.doc: flight heading in degrees clockwise from up (terrain moves the opposite way)

heroSrc.doc: optional public/ image path used as the hero instead of the crane

shadow.doc: hatched cast shadow under the hero

trail.doc: dashed flight trail behind the hero

title: Toy-town traffic
description: A seeded miniature city seen from a high oblique angle: blocks of low-rise buildings with coloured roofs and blue shadows, parks with round bright trees and ponds, crosswalks, and dozens of little cars that flow, queue at red lights and surge on green (IDM car-following simulated deterministically), pedestrians gathering at corners. Actors step at 8 / 12 Hz under the time-lapse while the camera rotates smoothly, a tilt-shift focus band follows the red hero car, and a time-lapse clock ramps from ×6 down to ×1 real time.
useFor: Mobility / logistics / smart-city / real-estate explainers, "rush hour" metaphors for queues and load, satisfying looping backgrounds; nothing else in the library animates a traffic system.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/tilt-shift/demo/traffic.js, story.js, main.js stepT (MIT, LemoLab)

blocks.doc: [columns, rows] of city blocks (swapped automatically in portrait)

rate.doc: time-lapse rate keyframes [[seconds, rate]] — ≥6 steps at 8 Hz, 2–6 at 12 Hz, <2 smooth; drop to ~1 for the real-time detail

rotation.doc: camera rotation in degrees per second

follow.doc: tilt-shift band follows the red hero car

band.doc: tilt-shift band: centre (when not following), width, falloff (fractions of height), maxBlur px at 1080p

carColors.doc: colour pool for the other cars

title: Window glow sequence
description: A storybook brick workshop powers up: its arched windows turn golden one after another with a warm bloom and one flicker, action ticks flicker over the roof hopper, the tower cog speeds up and smoke puffs rise as a giant hand withdraws.
useFor: "It's alive / powering up / open for business" beats; light the windows of any building image (src + windows) — factories, shops, houses, city shots.

background.doc: 'scene' = procedural gouache street + workshop, 'transparent' = glow overlay only, or a CSS colour

src.doc: optional building picture (public/ path or URL); then list its windows in `windows`

windows.doc: normalised frame rects [{x, y, w, h, shape: arch|round|rect}] to light; empty = the procedural workshop windows

order.doc: lighting order: ltr | rtl | random | center-out

flicker.doc: index of the window that flickers once after lighting (-1 = none)

hand.doc: show the giant creator hand withdrawing at the top

ticks.doc: flicker action ticks over the hopper (or at tickAt)

tickAt.doc: normalised [x, y] for the action ticks (empty = above the hopper)

sign.doc: text on the blank plaque above the door (empty = blank)

push.doc: slow camera push-in amount over the shot

title: Backlit paper cut-out (holes are light)
description: In a dark paper night scene a hanging cut-out — a rosette window flower, a lantern or a word — lights up from behind: the paper glows deep red, every cut hole burns warm white with a two-level bloom and soft rays, and the hole pattern is projected across the ground as squashed light, with a candle flicker.
useFor: Night reveals, "an idea shines through", lantern / Diwali / Lunar New Year moments, a word or emblem projected as light; overlay over dark scenes with background "transparent".
source: lemo-opuscar styles/papercut-red (MIT code, CC BY 4.0 docs, LemoLab) — demo/light.js glowWindow/bloom/rays/lightMasked

shape.doc: "rosette" (8-fold window flower), "lantern" or "text" (word cut out of a red card)

text.doc: the word when shape is "text"

project.doc: project the hole pattern onto the ground

title: Beam clash
description: Two fighters fire white-core energy beams in their own colours that meet mid-frame in a jittering four-point star flare spraying spark streaks, with a blurred reflection on the glossy neon floor, a "DEAD EVEN!" pop and a white-out bloom at the end.
useFor: "Two forces are equal / competing" metaphors, head-to-head finales, energy-transfer diagrams.
source: video x7 21.25-23.55 s (beam clash, contact jitter, white-out) — original fighters

contact.doc: where the beams meet between the fighters (0..1)

jitter.doc: contact jitter as a fraction of width

text.doc: exclamation that pops in above ("" = none)

bloomAt.doc: frame of the 3-frame white-out bloom (0 = none)

fighters.doc: draw the two original fighters at the beam ends

title: Beat punch zoom
description: Music-synced camera kick: the whole frame punches a few percent toward a chosen point on every accent (ticks, hits, slams at different amplitudes, summed and capped) and relaxes in ~5 frames. Demo: a candy sunburst stage where a toy star squashes on each slam with a star-ring-lines burst; or feed any image with src.
useFor: Universal music-energy layer for promos, recaps and social cuts; wrap any footage, image or composition in beat punches.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/game-show (MIT, LemoLab) — demo/main_v1.js punch(), main_b.js camera; also used by halftone-dossier

bpm.doc: tempo of the accent grid

pattern.doc: one char per eighth note, looped: 'S' slam, 'h' hit, 't' tick, '.' rest

cap.doc: cap on summed simultaneous punches (frame edges never show)

src.doc: optional image (public/ path or URL) that receives the punches instead of the demo stage

overlayDemo.doc: draw the candy demo stage when src is empty

title: Circuit traces
description: A faint glowing PCB pattern — thin traces with 45° bends ending in round pads — draws itself over the ground (flat or squashed onto the iso plane), then breathes at low opacity under the scene.
useFor: "AI / tech layer over the real world" overlay on maps, photos and product shots; background texture that says "computed".
source: video x6 2.57 s, 9.2-9.5 s (draw-on), 16-46 s (breathing under the armies)

drawFrames.doc: frames each trace takes to draw on

pulse.doc: breathe at 0.3 Hz after the draw-on

label.doc: optional mono caption under the pattern

demoScene.doc: paint the painterly battlefield behind (preview only; turn off as an overlay)

title: Confetti burst
description: Flat circles, rings, squares and capsules explode radially from a point with drag, gravity, spin and 3D flutter; fill mode tiles the whole frame (video17). Overlay-ready: background "transparent".
useFor: Celebrations, completions, level-ups, "chaos" beats; small counts make an impact puff on a landing or tap.
notes: As a web overlay: <MotionPlayer motion="confetti-burst" overlay loop="once"/> over your success screen.

x.doc: burst origin x (0..1 of frame width)

y.doc: burst origin y (0..1 of frame height)

delay.doc: local frame the burst fires (the hero ball winds up during the frames before it)

weights.doc: relative weight of each palette colour (same length as palette, else uniform)

shapes.doc: any of circle, ring, square, capsule, dot, triangle

power.doc: launch speed multiplier (0.15 = tiny landing puff, 1 = fills the frame)

spread.doc: launch cone in degrees, centred upward (360 = all directions)

upBias.doc: extra upward launch speed in px/s (v14 -150..-500)

flutter.doc: sway + 3D flip amount while falling (0 = rigid)

fill.doc: true = v17 mode: pieces fly to a jittered grid that tiles the whole frame, float, then drop out

life.doc: seconds before a piece fades (burst mode)

ringRadius.doc: spawn ring radius in u (v14 spawns on a 60-120 px ring)

ghosts.doc: draw motion-blur ghost copies while pieces move fast

showSubject.doc: draw the hero ball that pops (scene mode only)

title: Copper proof pull
description: ECU of polished warm copper with hairline scratches and a blurred four-pane window reflection: a burin cuts glinting grooves (dark trough, bright burr) with a curling swarf ribbon while the camera pulls back over the mirrored plate; then a paper sheet sweeps across with a curled edge and the image is revealed printed true, with an engraved title.
useFor: "The secret comes out / draft becomes final / die and strike" reveals: stamps, coins, certificates, heritage brands, craft stories.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/engraving (MIT, LemoLab) — demo/engine/copper.js drawCopper, copperLight, drawGrooves, drawBurin, drawSwarf

title.doc: roman caption cut on the proof

cutDuration.doc: seconds of burin cutting on the copper

peelAt.doc: second the paper starts to sweep across

push.doc: extra loupe zoom at the start

title: Crayon wax shader
description: Wax-crayon-on-toothy-paper look as a layer: a picture-book garden (sun, cloud, flowers, grass) is outlined, coloured lightly so the wax only catches the paper tooth, then coloured over hard until near-solid; embossed paper, fibre grooves, 12 fps boil. With src, any picture is coloured in by big zig-zag strokes through the same filter.
useFor: A hand-made crayon style layer for kids content, picture books, greeting cards; turn a photo into a crayon drawing.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/crayon-book (MIT, LemoLab) — demo/gl.js tooth / wax adhesion / emboss, demo/crayon.js

src.doc: optional picture (public/ path or URL) rendered as wax crayon; empty = the procedural garden

caption.doc: printed words, written letter by letter at the bottom

colors.doc: [sun, petals, leaves, flower centre, cloud] crayon colours

title: Cyanotype water bloom
description: Water drops fall onto a cyanotype blueprint and bloom into deeper, more saturated blue stains with pale tide-line rims; the white line work inside each stain goes soft, and a drop on the signature makes the ink bleed.
useFor: Rain / flood / emotion beats on any paper-based motion; a melancholy turn in a blueprint or patent story.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/blueprint demo/paper.js wet branch (MIT, LemoLab)

drops.doc: [{x, y, at, r}] drop positions (0..1), landing frames and stain radii in px at 1080; empty = four default drops, the last on the signature

signature.doc: signature that bleeds when the last drop hits it

note.default: FIG. 2 · WORKS BEAUTIFULLY. NO CLOUDS YET.

title: Data view flash
description: Beat-synced 1–5-frame "data" flashes: the painterly army close-up cuts to the same units as flat glyphs on near-black noise (with an occasional RGB-split frame) and straight back, hiding each faction change inside a flash.
useFor: Rhythmic "under the hood / what the AI sees" accents; hiding hard cuts on music beats.
source: video x6 13.8-26.4 s (12 flashes at ≈ 92 BPM, 1-5 frames each)

bpm.doc: flash tempo (one flash per beat)

flashFrames.doc: flash lengths in frames, cycled per beat (1–5)

rgbSplit.doc: add a ±8 px red/blue split on the second flash frame

factions.doc: armies to cut between (shot changes every 4 beats, hidden in a flash)

push.doc: camera push during each 4-beat shot in %/s

title: Drop splash crown
description: A glossy drop falls stretched onto a polished floor, squashes into a lens and throws a crown of tapered tendrils; the tips bead up and pinch off as secondary droplets that fly and land as small beads or melt into the puddle while the stubs recoil, all mirrored in the floor; a second smaller drop lands in the puddle.
useFor: Drink, food and cosmetics ads, logo openers, "drop" product launches and loader hits.

drops.doc: list of {t: impact frame, x: 0..1 across the frame, size, hue 0-360}

secondaries.doc: tips pinch off into flying droplets

floorY.doc: floor line as a fraction of the frame height

reflection.doc: mirror strength in the floor 0..1 (0 = none)

cameraMacro.doc: macro framing: bigger drop and crown

title: Electric arcs
description: Jagged white-core lightning arcs with violet glow, re-randomised every 1-2 frames with drop-outs and brightness flashes, radiating from a plasma orb, jumping between two electrodes or crawling around an object. Overlay-ready: background "transparent".
useFor: Energy, power, surges, sci-fi, "electrifying" ideas; around mode electrifies a logo or product.

x.doc: arc origin x (0..1) — orb centre or first electrode

mode.doc: radial (out of an object edge) | between (x,y) and (x2,y2) | around (crawling over the object surface)

reach.doc: radial mode: max arc length as a fraction of the short side

radius.doc: object radius in u (arcs start at its edge)

holdFrames.doc: regenerate every N frames (1-2)

branches.doc: add short forks off the arcs

rampOut.doc: frames to power down at the end

showSubject.doc: draw the plasma orb / electrodes (scene mode only)

title: Emote pop
description: Doodle reaction icons (! ? lightbulb hearts sweat-drop music notes) pop in over a point in 1-2 frames, boil, bob and fade, chained one after another above a box-bot. Overlay-ready: background "transparent".
useFor: Quick reactions over any character, face or UI element: surprise, confusion, idea, love, stress, joy.

background.doc: scene paper colour; 'transparent' = overlay (no bot, no paper)

x.doc: emote anchor x (0..1) — the point the icons pop over

icons.doc: sequence of icons: '!', '?', '!?', 'bulb', 'heart', 'sweat', 'note' + round-2 set: 'ticks' (flickering manga action strokes), 'anger' (vein), 'steam' (rising puffs), 'zzz', 'dots' (typing bubble), 'stars' (orbiting), 'spark', 'cloud' (personal rain cloud); each starts the frame after the previous ends

showSubject.doc: draw the reacting box-bot under the icons (scene mode only)

title: Eraser rewind (undo wipe)
description: A charcoal felt eraser slides along a zig-zag path at constant speed and wipes a wide band of hand-drawn ink, leaving a faint ghost; then a corrected line is written in. Reads as "undo / rewind time" or a clean whiteboard wipe.
useFor: Undo / rewind beats, "what if we hadn't…" storytelling, clean wipes between whiteboard sections, correcting a wrong answer on screen.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/whiteboard demo engine (MIT, LemoLab) — Timeline.erase / zigzag / drawEraser, own SVG mask build

ink.doc: ink colour of the drawing that gets erased

text.doc: handwritten line(s) under the chart, \n for more lines

after.doc: text written after the wipe (empty = none)

strength.doc: how much ink is removed (0.9 leaves a 10 % ghost)

box.doc: [x, y, w, h] erase area as frame fractions

title: Explosion burst
description: Two-frame flash, a fireball that swells in 12 frames and then rolls while cooling yellow to red to soot with turbulent edges, rising smoke puffs, a shockwave ring that outruns the frame in about 10 frames, glowing debris with streaks, drifting embers and a decaying camera shake; or a cartoon version with a spiky flash, scalloped ink-outlined clouds, chunky debris on twos and optional comic text.
useFor: Game trailers, dramatic reveals, comedy beats, history / battle stories, "blow up the old way" transitions.
source: prompt-corpus research: explosion-burst (21 cases, ideas only; original implementation)

text.doc: cartoon only: comic word above the blast (e.g. a sound effect)

background.doc: scene colour behind the blast; use a dark base or composite with screen blending

title: Eyes blink & look
description: A pair of cartoon eyes on a red ball blinks, darts between look targets and switches to happy ^ ^ arcs with a squash hop; watching variant fills dark negative space with staggered glowing green eye pairs. Overlay-ready: background "transparent".
useFor: Give any shape, logo or object a personality; suspense / "being watched" beats in dark scenes.

background.doc: 'auto' = cream (character) or near-black (watching); any colour; 'transparent' = overlay

variant.doc: character (one pair that blinks / looks / smiles) | watching (field of glowing eye pairs in the dark)

delay.doc: frame offset for the whole timeline

eyeStyle.doc: oval (v17 black ovals) | sclera (v2 white eyes with moving pupils and lids) | round-2 eye library: happy closed sleepy narrow angry determined sad teary cry heart x swirl spark shades scared dot

eyes.doc: [left, right] eye styles for mismatched pairs, e.g. ['oval','x'] or ['heart','heart']; [] = both use eyeStyle

spacing.doc: distance between the two eyes multiplier

blinks.doc: frames (after delay) at which the eyes blink

looks.doc: saccade schedule [{at, x, y}] with x,y in -1..1 of maxOffset

maxOffset.doc: look offset in u at x/y = 1

happyAt.doc: frame the eyes switch to happy arcs (-1 = never)

showSubject.doc: draw the ball (character) or the fog, wind and lantern figure (watching) — scene mode only

subjectColor.doc: ball colour (also lid colour for sclera eyes)

stagger.doc: watching: frames between pairs appearing (~0.4 s)

region.doc: watching: [x0, y0, x1, y1] area (0..1) the pairs scatter in

title: Fire flames (cartoon / real / lava)
description: A fire bed that licks upward with 6-10 Hz flicker and 15 % height variance: flat layered red / orange / yellow tongues (cartoon), soft additive gradient layers with heat glow and embers (real), or dark crust with pulsing glowing cracks and gooey rising lava blobs. Overlay-capable.
useFor: Hearths and campfire ambience, danger beats, hot deals, forge / craft stories, lava worlds; drop over a dark scene with overlay=true.
source: prompt-corpus research: fire-flames (20 cases, ideas only; original implementation)

width.doc: fraction of the frame width the fire spans

tongues.doc: number of flame tongues (lava: blob density follows it)

overlay.doc: true = transparent background so it can sit over any scene

title: Focus desaturate
description: At the key moment the whole scene greys toward warm cream (mix with luma and #E9DFCB) while one subject keeps full colour and gets a dashed ring and label. Default scene is a flat isometric town with one red-roofed house as the subject; with src it greys an image except a kept circle.
useFor: "This one" moments — one user, one store, one product, one data point in a busy scene.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/iso-infographic (MIT, LemoLab) — engine.js colour pipeline (desat + keep flag)

src.doc: optional image in public/ — greyed except the keep circle

keep.doc: image mode: kept circle [x, y, r] as fractions (r of the short side)

subjectColor.doc: procedural mode: the subject roof colour

title: Frame-blend time-lapse
description: A keyed speed ramp (1x to 70x and a hard brake to 0.3x) integrated to source time, each frame an average of blended sub-frames: headlights become continuous lines, clouds turn to water, the sky runs through the day, then everything snaps sharp.
useFor: Hyperlapse and time-lapse looks, "time flies" beats, light-trail backgrounds; the same speed-integration + sub-frame-average recipe applies to any procedural child.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/city-symphony/demo/tools/prep.py (MIT, LemoLab); STYLE.md sections 5 and 8

speedKeys.doc: speed keyframes [[seconds, multiplier], ...] — smoothstep (log-space) between keys; 0.3 - 75

blend.doc: cap on sub-frames averaged per output frame (8 - 30)

shutter.doc: fraction of the frame interval that is sampled (1 = 360 degrees; ~0.4 for noon clouds)

lanes.doc: road lanes (even number, half each way)

hourStart.doc: clock hour at source time zero (the sky and window lights follow it)

src.doc: optional still image (public/) used as the sky + skyline plate behind the road

seed.doc: seed for buildings, clouds and cars

speedLine.doc: HUD line; {n} = sub-frames blended, {s} = "S" when more than one

clockLabel.doc: caption under the source clock readout

title: Frame breakout
description: A framed woodblock-style print sits on a tan mount; the red koi inside grows, leaps and pushes out past the top border while the rest of the picture stays clipped to the frame — the camera tilts up into the mount and widens to follow, holds the almost-frozen crest outside the frame, then falls toward the lens with a camera push and small roll, bursts into foam that fills the screen and fades to bare paper. Clip is bound left/right/bottom but open on the break edge.
useFor: Thumbnail-style "pop out of the frame" moments for any framed media: a product leaving a phone screen, a character leaping from a comic panel, a chart line breaking its axis box; dramatic climaxes.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/ukiyoe/DEMO.md climax beats; STYLE.md §6 §8 (MIT, LemoLab) — original koi + print

src.doc: optional subject image in public/ (transparent PNG) instead of the built-in koi

breakEdge.doc: which border the subject escapes: top or right

growAt.doc: frame when the subject starts growing

riseAt.doc: frame when it starts to rise and the camera tilts

hangAt.doc: frame the crest hangs outside the frame (near frozen)

fallAt.doc: frame it falls toward the lens

endWash.doc: fade the foam to bare paper at the end

title: Freeze-frame brackets
description: The footage stops dead with a white flash, a small punch-in and colour draining to 45 %; yellow corner brackets close in on the subject and a timecode chip with a red pause mark slides in top-right.
useFor: "Wait — look at this" moments in reaction videos, tutorials, sports, news and explainers.

src.doc: public/ photo (empty = procedural footage with a crossing bird)

focus.doc: [x, y] 0..1 bracket centre for a supplied photo (procedural footage tracks the bird)

label.doc: bold caption under the brackets (empty = none)

subject.doc: draw the moving subject on procedural footage

title: Giant eye reveal
description: In darkness a huge reptilian eye opens from a cyan slit through an almond lid mask, with a glowing fibrous iris, contracting slit pupil and lit scales; ends with an exponential push into the pupil (or an eyelid close). Overlay-ready: background "transparent".
useFor: Creature reveals, "you are being watched" twists, dramatic awakenings, zoom-through-the-pupil transitions.

size.doc: eye size multiplier (1 = ~72 % of frame width in landscape)

holdFrames.doc: frames the open eye holds (pupil contracts, iris sparkles)

ending.doc: push (exponential zoom into the pupil -> endColor) | close (lids squash shut) | hold

endColor.doc: colour the push lands on (match-cut into the next scene)

src.doc: optional public/ image shown inside the lids instead of the procedural iris

scales.doc: draw lit scales around the eye

title: Glass crack and mend (re-leading)
description: A leaded stained-glass pane takes a blow: nine white-hot jagged cracks race out from the impact in a quarter second with a flash and a 2-frame shake, then groups of glass slide along the leads into a new arrangement, one group per beat with a weld spark, and the cracks turn into dark mending lead lines.
useFor: Turning points: reinvention, injury and recovery, a restored building, a before/after pivot; works over any image via `src`.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/stained-glass demo/story.js (CRACKS, WELDS, crackAfter) + STYLE.md (MIT, LemoLab)

impact.doc: impact point as 0..1 of the window

groupAt.doc: start frame of each re-lead group (one slide per entry)

mend.doc: turn the cracks into lead lines

src.doc: optional image shown through the glass (public path); empty = coloured glass

title: Grease pencil marks
description: Hand-made telestration: a warm-white grease pencil draws a wobbly overshooting ring around a detail, quick arrows with barbs, crosses and soft-lead underlines — each stroke doubled by a thinner offset pass so it reads waxy; optionally freezes an image with a short jolt first. Transparent overlay by default.
useFor: "Look here" evidence circles for documentaries, sports telestration on stills, tutorial screenshots, annotated archive photos.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/newsreel (MIT code, CC BY 4.0 docs, LemoLab) — demo/index.html pencil/ring/lineP/pencilDark

marks.doc: annotations [{type: ring|arrow|underline|cross, at: [x,y] 0..1, to? (arrow), rx/ry (size), rot, start (frame), dur?, label?}]

color.doc: pencil colour (warm white; use a dark tone on paper)

freezeSrc.doc: optional image to freeze and jolt under the marks

title: Impact frame (flash, shake, punch)
description: On each hit: one inverted frame, one white frame, a decaying camera shake, a 1.06 to 1 zoom punch, a chromatic RGB split and a burst of speed lines with a shock ring; the default scene slams one giant word per hit (READY / SET / GO) on a new colour with an anticipation ring closing before every beat.
useFor: Beat drops, fight and comedy shorts, stat slams, game trailers. Set `scene: false` and `background: "transparent"` to lay the flash + speed lines over other layers; pairs with comic-burst and speed-lines.
source: prompt corpus x18 (hit: inverted/white frames, decaying shake, zoom punch, chroma split)

scene.doc: draw the built-in word scene (false = effect layers only, for overlaying)

strength.doc: overall hit strength (1 = shake 2% of the frame, flash, 1.06 punch)

ramp.doc: extra strength added per successive hit

lines.doc: draw the speed-line burst

chroma.doc: chromatic RGB split on the hit

background.doc: backdrop when `scene` is off ("transparent" to overlay)

title: Ink blot (pen stop)
description: Where the pen stops, ink soaks into the paper as a growing teardrop: the tip stays at the nib, the belly sags downward, the rim is irregular with a darker tide line; several blots with their own timing and optional handwritten words. Transparent overlay by default.
useFor: A hesitation / loss / signature beat in ink, pencil, ink-wash or woodcut styles; punctuation in hand-drawn explainers.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/one-line (MIT code, CC BY 4.0 docs, LemoLab) — demo/ink.js drawBlots

blots.doc: blots [{x, y (0..1), start (frame), dur?, size? (1 = small), label?}]

lineWidth.doc: the stopped line's width in u (sets the initial dot)

title: Ink brush boil
description: A doodle (light bulb, mug, star, heart or your own strokes) inks itself on warm paper with real brush lines — tapered ends, pressure wobble, heavier on the shadow side — then flat fills drop in off-register, a hatched shadow scratches in, a hand-lettered caption writes on, and every line keeps breathing (re-drawn each exposure).
useFor: Hand-made, craft or "drawn for you" moments: ideas (bulb), coffee breaks, ratings, love/likes, or any line art you feed as strokes; the kit upgrades any doodle to brush ink.
source: mg-styles-15 05-cel-boil engine.js boil/outline/inkW/inkLoop/hatch (MIT, Vincentwei1021) — technique after mg-styles-15

strokes.doc: custom: list of strokes, each a list of [x,y] in 0..1; a stroke whose last point equals its first is a filled loop

caption.doc: hand-lettered caption under the drawing ("" to hide)

fillColors.doc: flat fill colours (subject parts pick by index; first is also the underline)

inkWidth.doc: brush width multiplier (6 px base at 1080p)

boilScale.doc: boil noise scale multiplier (70 px base; bigger = smoother wobble)

boilEvery.doc: frames per drawing (2 = on twos, 3 = on threes)

taper.doc: taper length multiplier (14 px in / 26 px out)

heavySide.doc: extra weight on the lower-right shadow side (0–1)

drawDuration.doc: frames to ink the whole drawing

title: Long-exposure trails
description: Dusk city with a road bending to the horizon: moving lights leave long glowing streaks like a long-exposure photograph — warm white headlights streaming toward the viewer and red tail-lights streaming away, each trail a tapered additive-glow line that fades toward its tail and grows with perspective, plus a brighter hero car. Overlay-capable: set background transparent (or give a src plate) and your own light paths.
useFor: Night-city intros, logistics / delivery routes, "data packets" metaphors, festive lantern scenes, traffic and motion energy over any dark plate.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/tilt-shift/STYLE.md §8 long-exposure light; DEMO.md dawn car trail (MIT, LemoLab)

paths.doc: light paths: {pts:[[x,y]…] (0-1 of the frame), color, count, speed (path fractions/s), offset (px), delay, perspective, reverse, hero}

trail.doc: trail length in seconds of world time (1–4)

width.doc: light core width in px at 1080p

glow.doc: additive glow radius in px at 1080p

background.doc: plate colour, or "transparent" to overlay on a host scene

src.doc: optional plate image in public/ (replaces the procedural dusk city)

title: Loupe magnify (light table)
description: A black-rimmed magnifier with a bevel highlight and clear acrylic skirt drops onto a document on a backlit light table, reads a line at 2.5× with colour fringing at the rim, glides to the key figure (underlined and ringed in the signal colour), then the camera pushes through the lens.
useFor: The "look closer" beat in an explainer or evidence film: a contract clause, a receipt, a product detail, a screenshot or a map.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/archive-lighttable demo/film.js lens branch (MIT, LemoLab)

src.doc: optional public/ image to inspect instead of the procedural document (fills the page area)

meta.default: Ref. NH-2041 · Filed 14 March · Page 3 of 12
meta.doc: reference / date line under the title

default: The survey team walked the full length of the channel on four
separate mornings and recorded every reading by hand before
it was checked against the harbour charts held in the archive.
Ships now entering the port are wider and taller than any that
the old bridge was designed for, and pilots report that the
clearance at high water leaves almost no margin for error.
The measured clear span required for safe passage is 1,208 metres,
more than twice the distance the present structure can offer.
A cable-stayed design meets this figure with room to spare and
can be built while the existing crossing remains in service.
Costs and timings are set out in the tables that follow, with
every figure traced to its original source document.
lines.doc: body lines of the document (one string per printed line)

keyLine.doc: index of the line that holds the key figure (underlined after the glide)

keyNumber.doc: text inside the key line that gets ringed (e.g. "1,208")

focus.doc: lens stops as [[x,y],[x,y]] in 0..1 page coordinates; empty = meta line then the key figure

fringe.doc: lateral colour fringe strength (0 = none, 1 = ±1.1 % per channel)

landAt.doc: frame the loupe lands (0.4 s drop, scale 1.35 → 1)

glideAt.doc: frame it lifts and glides to the second stop

pushAt.doc: frame the camera starts pushing through the lens

pushThrough.doc: end by pushing through the lens until the rim leaves frame

accent.doc: signal colour for the underline and ring (use sparingly)

title: Magnifier reading loupe
description: A thin round glass lens wanders across textbook text like a reading cursor, magnifying it 1.6× with a slight barrel bulge, a prismatic orange/magenta rim fringe with tinted ghost text, a white edge highlight and a small magnifier icon; it follows its path with a soft critically damped lag. Works over any `src` image, or as glass only over host content (backdrop "none").
useFor: Drawing attention to fine print, a definition, a UI detail or a chart value; "look closer" and "read along" beats in explainers and product tours.

src.doc: image to read over (public/ path or URL); empty = procedural textbook page

backdrop.doc: "book" procedural textbook | "none" = transparent overlay: only the glass is drawn (no magnified copy)

path.doc: lens path as [x, y, travelFrames] in 0..1 of the reading area (left page, or the whole frame with src)

bulge.doc: barrel bulge: extra magnification at the centre (0 = flat)

icon.doc: show the small magnifier icon at the centre

drift.doc: slow camera push on the backdrop over the clip

background.doc: colour behind the glass in overlay mode ("transparent")

title: Marker ring and arrow
description: Broadcast-telestrator annotations drawn live without a freeze: glowing fluorescent marker arrows (solid for what happened, dashed with an open chevron for what was intended), a perspective ring with rotating dashes, a translucent dashed area, and a comet with a fading tapered trail behind a moving point — every stroke has a dark outline, colour glow, colour core and white highlight. Overlay-capable: set background to transparent and scene to none.
useFor: Annotating any video, map, chart or UI capture; sports analysis, "what happened vs what should have", callouts and pointers; a punchy alternative to pencil / blueprint annotation looks.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/telestrator/demo/index.html — marker, partial, ring, comet, trail (MIT, LemoLab)

items.doc: annotations: {type:"arrow"|"ring"|"comet"|"area", pts:[[x,y]…] (0-1 of the frame) or x,y,r, color (role name or hex), at (s), dur (s), dash, wobble}

palette.doc: colour roles: did = what happened, plan = intended (dashed), alert, focus

weight.doc: marker core width in px at 1080p (6-9)

scene.doc: demo backdrop: pitch, grid or none (use none + transparent background to overlay)

background.doc: backdrop colour, or "transparent" for a pure overlay

ringSquash.doc: ring height / width — lower = flatter perspective ring

title: Palette re-ink (squeegee recolour)
description: A finished screen-print poster of a lake under mountains is pulled again: a wide tilted squeegee crosses the sheet in about a third of a second and behind it every ink has changed (noon, golden hour, dusk), geometry identical; the big number swaps with the palette.
useFor: Time passing (day/night hours), seasons, product colourways, A/B variants — any "same thing, new palette" beat.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/silkscreen-poster STYLE.md §5/§8 + DEMO.md "7 h" swap (MIT, LemoLab)

palettes.doc: palette names (dawn, noon, golden, dusk, harbour, winter) or inline objects; one per re-ink + the first

at.doc: frame each re-ink starts (one per palette after the first)

frames.doc: frames the blade takes to cross the sheet

tail.doc: depth of the ragged ink front in poster units

header.doc: tracked line at the top of the poster

name.doc: big name in the info band

title: Physics pile (falling, stacking shapes)
description: Colourful circles, rounded boxes and triangles (or letter tiles from a word) drop in one after another, bounce, tumble, stack and settle in a box, bowl or on the floor; a deterministic pre-simulated 2D rigid-body sim at 120 Hz sampled per frame, with small impact marks and exported collision frames for sound effects.
useFor: Playful product demos, logos or words that fall into a heap, music-from-collisions, data drops (one body per item), toy / game stories.
source: prompt-corpus research: physics-pile (18 cases, ideas only; original implementation)

count.doc: number of bodies (ignored when text is set)

text.doc: letters that fall as tiles instead of shapes (e.g. a brand name)

size.doc: body size in u (1u = 1px at 1080 on the short side)

impacts.doc: draw small impact bursts at hard collisions

title: Portal glow
description: A golden ring between paper-stone ruins with a four-point star at its centre, slowly rotating light rays, a pulsing glow, a shimmering basin pool, winking glints and rising motes, ending in a warm white-out bloom.
useFor: "The goal / destination / unlock" beat, level-ups and launches; ends in a white-out you can cut on.

size.doc: ring diameter as a fraction of the short side

rays.doc: number of light rays behind the star (16–24)

raySpeed.doc: ray rotation in degrees per second

bloomAt.doc: frame the light blooms into a white-out (0 = never)

ruins.doc: draw the stone pillars, carvings and glints

title: Practical light shadow jump
description: A cold, dim room with two figures beside an unlit lantern. On the switch-on beat the light ignites (0 to 1 in ~.3 s with a flicker overshoot), the glow blooms, the figures turn toward it and their shadows swing out across the floor from their feet while the mood flips from cold blue to warm. Source can be lantern, lamp or screen.
useFor: "Switching on" moments: product power-on, store opening, an idea lighting up, a story turning from dark to hopeful.

warm.doc: light colour (ignored for screen, which is cool white-blue)

cold.doc: colour of the unlit room darkness

title: Registration snap (loose print layers clamp)
description: A crane down a screen-print: the ink layers hang loose as separate paper sheets with paper-white gaps, thickness shadows and depth parallax, then clamp into perfect register on one loud hit (2-frame shake and flash) before the key facts print in.
useFor: The "everything locks into place" beat before a date, price or launch fact; multi-plane parallax that does not look like moving mountains.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/silkscreen-poster DEMO.md climb shot + STYLE.md §5/§8 (MIT, LemoLab)

planes.doc: how many ink layers hang loose (2-7)

loosenFrom.doc: frame the sheets start to hang loose

gap.doc: paper gap between planes in poster units

shadow.doc: thickness shadow size in poster units

stats.doc: info-band stat blocks printed after the snap

title: Scribble ball
description: A boiling tangle of open ink loops, regenerated every 2 frames, floats over an upset box-bot linked by a red steam squiggle; storm variant swaps in a boiling doodle cloud with a lightning scribble and rain. Overlay-ready: background "transparent".
useFor: Frustration, confusion, overthinking, "problem" states, bad moods.

background.doc: scene paper colour; 'transparent' = overlay (no bot, no paper)

delay.doc: frame the scribble fades in (it fades out at the end of the clip)

variant.doc: tangle (v20 frustration ball) | storm (doodle storm cloud with lightning scribble)

boilEvery.doc: regenerate the drawing every N frames (1-2 = line boil)

steamColor.doc: colour of the steam squiggle to the head

steam.doc: draw the red steam squiggle (tangle variant)

showSubject.doc: draw the upset box-bot underneath (scene mode only)

elementBoil.doc: per-element line boil: each ink loop keeps its own random stream and re-draws only on its own staggered beat (no all-over shimmer)

title: SDF liquid shade
description: Coloured metaballs orbit and fuse into thick glossy jelly: smooth necks that blend their colours, dome-shaped diffuse shading from a key light, a hard specular highlight, a broad softbox sheen, a saturated translucent rim and a fading floor reflection.
useFor: The shading look under liquid motions: drops, logo melts, blob loaders, liquid buttons and transitions; also a standalone glossy-goo background.

colors.doc: ball colours (hex), cycled over the balls

light.doc: key light azimuth in degrees (225 = upper left)

blur.doc: merge softness in px at 1080 (bigger = longer necks)

title: Smear frame
description: Hand-animation smears: a red ink ball (or the flame mascot, or a star) holds on twos, anticipates, then whips to its next spot in one stretched dry-brush smear drawing followed by one "multiples" drawing of overlapping copies, landing with squash, trailing speed lines and an impact star on the slam.
useFor: Instant "animator craft" accents on hits, whooshes and logo slams; the multiples / smear grammar for any fast move in a hand-drawn piece.
source: mg-styles-15 05-cel-boil 0.29-0.46 s, scene.js drawStrikeSmear / smearUp (MIT, Vincentwei1021) — technique after mg-styles-15

stretch.doc: smear length as a fraction of the move (1 ≈ 90 %)

holdFrames.doc: frames held (on twos) at each station before the next whip

ground.doc: ink ground line and contact shadow

title: Smoke puffs
description: Clusters of open doodle ink circles (or soft blurred circles) rise from a vent, grow and fade, then shrink away when fixed; flash mode fires a 2-frame muzzle flash and a forward-drifting smoke puff. Overlay-ready: background "transparent".
useFor: Broken machines, steam, thinking, engines; with flash: cannon / gun / launch / explosion beats.

background.doc: scene colour; 'auto' = cream paper (doodle) or dusk navy (soft); 'transparent' = overlay

delay.doc: frame the first puff (or shot) fires

style.doc: doodle (v20 open ink circles) | soft (v3 blurred grey-white smoke)

flash.doc: true = cannon mode: muzzle flash + one big puff per shot

shotEvery.doc: flash mode: frames between shots (0.25 s)

rate.doc: continuous mode: frames between new clusters (0.3 s)

rise.doc: rise distance as a fraction of frame height

grow.doc: scale reached at end of life

direction.doc: flash mode: barrel / blast direction in degrees (0 = right, -90 = up)

drift.doc: sideways wind in u per second

stopAt.doc: continuous mode: local frame spawning stops and puffs shrink away (-1 = 22 frames before the end)

showSubject.doc: draw the broken machine (doodle) or cannon (flash) — scene mode only

title: Sparkle burst
description: Four-point doodle sparkles burst from a contact point and twinkle out (tool-tap repair), or gold stars fly out of a jittering scuffle cloud, or twinkle around a cheering character. Overlay-ready: background "transparent".
useFor: Success / fixed / done accents, comic fights and replacements, celebration beats.

background.doc: scene paper colour; 'transparent' = overlay (no subject, no paper)

delay.doc: repair: frame of the final tap (sparkles fire here); scuffle/cheer: start frame

variant.doc: repair (4-point colour sparkles + impact ticks) | scuffle (dust cloud + gold stars) | cheer (twinkling gold stars around a bouncing bot)

radius.doc: scatter radius in u (~1.2 body widths)

ticks.doc: flash radial ink impact ticks for 3 frames on each tap

taps.doc: repair scene: number of hammer taps (sparkles on the last)

scuffleFrames.doc: scuffle variant: length of the jittering cloud window

showSubject.doc: draw the scene subject (hammer + cracked pipe / bouncing bot); ignored in overlay mode

title: Star glint flare
description: A six-spike specular "ting" with soft bloom flashes on a blade tip, shimmers through a hold and slowly decays; can slide along an edge, or fire as a quick 4-point twinkle. Overlay-ready: background "transparent".
useFor: Specular highlight on a logo, product edge, blade, badge or coin; "shiny / new / premium" accents.
notes: The 'shiny / premium' accent on a logo, badge or number.

background.doc: scene colour (lavender sky); 'transparent' = overlay (no blade scene)

style.doc: flare (v5 6-spike flare with hold) | twinkle (v2 quick 4-point star, repeated)

hold.doc: frames the flare holds with shimmer (v5 ~48)

spikeAngles.doc: spike angles in degrees; first two are the long X diagonals, a vertical (0) is mid-length, others short

to.doc: [x, y] (0..1) to slide the glint along an edge during the hold; [] = stays put

showSubject.doc: draw the etched sword-and-army scene (scene mode only)

ink.doc: etching ink colour for the scene

trail.doc: guide-star trail: number of tiny shrinking stars popping on one by one behind the glint, then twinkling (0 = none; try 6 with spikeAngles [0,90,180,270], style flare, color #D6B65D, bloomColor #FFF3C4)

trailSpacing.doc: trail: spacing between trail stars as a fraction of width

trailAngle.doc: trail: direction in degrees the trail leaves the glint (90 = straight down)

trailCurve.doc: trail: arc bend (degrees per star x30)

trailStagger.doc: trail: frames between stars popping on

lens.doc: anamorphic lens flare 0..1: horizontal streak + 5 hexagonal ghosts along the line through the frame centre

title: Sticker cut-out (die-cut border)
description: Paper-sticker finish for any subject: a thick rounded off-white die-cut border, a thin grey cardboard edge peeking out below, paper grain and a soft cut-out-shaped shadow; icons, words and transparent images slap down one by one with a back-ease and sway gently.
useFor: Kids / game / social sticker moments, scrapbook explainers, craft-made icon sets; wrap a product PNG to make it a sticker.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/paper-popup (MIT code, CC BY 4.0 docs, LemoLab) — demo/paper.js finishCut, cutmesh.js

items.doc: stickers [{kind: icon|text|src, icon? (FlatIcon kind: heart, star, coffee, leaf, sun, moon, bolt, gear, chat, check, flame…), text?, src?, color?, x, y (0..1), size (fraction of short side), rot (deg), at (frame)}]

title: Swirl portal (goo-rim toon hole)
description: A vertical oval hole in the world with a lumpy thickly outlined goo rim, five spiral arms in two alternating tints rotating inside, a pale hot core, orbiting sparks, drips off the bottom and flat rings of glow; pops open with an overshoot and boils on threes.
useFor: A "jump" device: a product teleporting between use cases, a meanwhile-in-another-universe beat, a doorway reveal for a picture (src inside the core), a playful CTA hole. Pairs with portal-wipe. Overlay-capable.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/scifi-toon demo/worlds.js (portal), demo/main.js (popOpen), DEMO.md "The portal" (MIT, LemoLab)

radius.doc: radius in u (1u = 1px of a 1080 short side)

openAt.doc: frame the pop-open starts (-1 = use `open` directly, 0..1, for a transition driver)

colors.doc: {rim, armA, armB, core, glow} (non-green by default)

drips.doc: drips off the bottom once open

wash.doc: full-frame flat tint alpha while open

src.doc: optional image shown through the hole instead of the arms

background.doc: backdrop colour; empty string = transparent overlay

title: Tape stutter
description: The picture behaves like worn tape: it steps down to 15 fps while tracking, jolts two or three frames backwards, drags at 15 fps into the drop and winds down at half speed; a cassette demo with a source-time curve and OSD makes each skipped frame visible.
useFor: Pre-drop tension, retro / found-tape feel and rhythm edits: wrap any motion in `TapeRemap` with the same segments, or reuse the remap curve for a tape-stop ending.

segments.doc: list of {from,to,mode} in frames; mode = normal | step (hold every Nth frame) | reverse (rewind blip) | half (half speed)

stepEvery.doc: frames held per step in step / half modes (2 = 15 fps at 30)

jitter.doc: horizontal picture jitter in px while the tape misbehaves

showGraph.doc: show the source-time curve and playhead

graphLabel.doc: caption under the time graph (showGraph: true)

title: Theatre gate (framed film print)
description: Frames any picture or motion as a film being shown: a 4:3 print in a rounded aperture with a soft dark rim, flanked by deep red-brown velvet drapes lit by the screen spill and footlights, with curtains that part at the start and close at the end.
useFor: Frames any motion as "a film being shown": retro launches, the-story-so-far, nostalgia pieces; solves 4:3 content inside 16:9 frames; wraps other motions via `layers`.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/silent-film demo/engine/cards.js (theatre), DEMO.md "Frame", poster.jpg (MIT, LemoLab)

layers.doc: motions to show inside the aperture [{motion, props, from, duration, ...}] (rendered full-frame and clipped)

src.doc: image for the print (public path or URL); empty + no layers = procedural plate

openAt.doc: frame the curtains start to part

closeAt.doc: frame the curtains start to close (-1 = stay open)

footlights.doc: warm footlight glow along the bottom

title: VHS CRT pass
description: Soft VHS-on-CRT playback over a night scene: smeared chroma with the red shifted right, scanlines, RGB grille, phosphor glow, dark corners, noise, a power-on opening and tracking-noise tears.
useFor: Retro, 80s, found-footage and synthwave looks over any picture; use overlay:true for a scanline/grille/corner/noise finish over other layers; the power-on and tracking bursts double as a tape transition.

src.doc: optional image path (public/) to put through the tape pass instead of the demo scene

subtitle.doc: cream-yellow subtitle composited inside the pass (empty = none)

bleed.doc: chroma horizontal smear width in px (at 1080)

rshift.doc: red-chroma shift to the right in px

powerOn.doc: [startFrame, endFrame] of the CRT power-on opening (equal = off)

overlay.doc: true = transparent finish only (grille, scanlines, corners, noise, bursts) to layer over other motions

seed.doc: seed for the demo scene and tear offsets

title: Wash bloom colour
description: A copperplate print of a pear is cut in black line, then transparent watercolour blooms region by region from where the brush touched — ragged wet front, spill past the line, off-register, darker tide-line, backruns and granulation — multiplied under the ink, with an engraved title and a script note.
useFor: "Colour arrives" climax for line art: botanical / natural-history plates, maps, product sketches, heritage brands.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/engraving (MIT, LemoLab) — demo/engine/wash.js Wash, burin.js, plate.js

note.default: Coloured by hand, after the print.
note.doc: copperplate script note, written left to right after the colour

printDuration.doc: seconds for the black line print to cut itself

colourAt.doc: second the first region starts to bloom

title: Wax resist reveal
description: Crayon picture-book page (hills, lighthouse, moon) drawn on toothy paper; a broad ultramarine watercolour wash sweeps across with bristle streaks and a dark wet front, and hundreds of white-wax stars plus a hidden hand-lettered message appear exactly where it passes, each uncovered star glinting.
useFor: Reveal a hidden message, thank-you names or a feature: greeting cards, kids brands, bedtime stories, education.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/crayon-book (MIT, LemoLab) — demo/gl.js FS_WASH wax resist, demo/crayon.js

message.doc: the hidden message written in white wax (short)

washColor.doc: watercolour colour (ultramarine default; try rose #9B3B5A or sap green #2F5A3A)

direction.doc: wash sweep direction: right or down

hillColors.doc: two crayon colours for the hills

scene.doc: draw the picture-book scene (false = only paper, wax and wash)

beam.doc: the lighthouse beam is coloured in after the wash

title: Army formation
description: A painterly isometric battlefield with four faction armies of tiny unit sprites around banner shields: they spawn as white placeholders, flood with faction colour, bob, march inwards and trade arcing arrow volleys, with a selection ring on one army and a centre-out "initialised" title in red brackets.
useFor: "AI models / teams / products compete" stories, strategy explainers, market-share battles, game trailers.

title: Candy set backdrop
description: Full-bleed game-show set: one saturated candy hue with a same-hue lighter pattern — slowly scrolling diagonal stripes, offset polka dots or a rotating sunburst — plus a darker floor band with an ink line, a hopping "GAME 1" pill, star bursts and beat punches; the hue hard-cuts with a white flash every two bars.
useFor: Instant loud backdrop for quizzes, kids content, sales promos, chapter cards; pairs with kinetic-captions, comic-burst and bean mascots.

title: Fuse beat timer
description: A rope fuse along the bottom with one knot per beat; a sparkling spark spawning star particles travels along it so it passes every knot exactly on the beat, charring the rope, toward a rocket (that launches) or a bomb (that bursts). A big beats-left numeral pops on every beat over a violet sunburst stage.
useFor: Countdowns for quizzes, challenges and limited-time offers; on-beat timers; game-show / microgame formats; set stage=false to overlay the fuse on any scene.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/microgame demo/hud.js (MIT, LemoLab) — fuse timer, hard-shadow toon parts

doneText.doc: word shown when the fuse reaches the icon

title: Lit pixel sprites
description: Flat low-res pixel characters with 1-px selout outlines step through 4-frame walk cycles and 2-frame idles on a dusk plaza. Two practical lamps and a drifting lantern tint their colours as they pass, posterised light pools band across the floor, and each sprite casts sheared shadows away from every nearby light while the camera drifts smoothly.
useFor: Retro-game storytelling, pixel mascots in a lit set, HD-2D mood; pairs with pixel-dither.

title: Lives counter
description: A dark rounded toon panel (ink outline, hard shadow) with hero-head icons: on a loss one icon cracks in five frames, shards fly, it shakes and greys while a slam caption announces it; the last life blinks at 2 Hz under a top-spot light; a gain re-lights an icon with a pop.
useFor: Battery / retries / chances metaphors, gamified explainers, quiz shows, "you only get three tries" beats.
