description: Dark blueprint: a blue dot pings, the camera snaps back to a seeded circular library plan with a glowing hub, blue paths and flowing nodes, then spokes shoot out to category labels.
useFor: Hero background for systems / knowledge / network stories; reveal 3-8 categories around a hub.
notes: At 30-40 % opacity with categories [] it is a premium tech texture behind a logo.

categories.doc: labels the blue spokes shoot out to (first fires alone, then in pairs)

centerLabel.doc: small tracked label under the hub ("" to hide)

accentPaths.doc: thick blue paths entering from outside

networkSpokes.doc: thin blue spokes with flowing nodes

pullFrom.doc: starting zoom of the pull-back reveal

rotateSpeed.doc: plan rotation in degrees per second

title: Spec chip rail
description: Hologram spec sheet: each value rolls from garbage glyphs into the real number on a big card (locks right-to-left, turns amber with a 1-frame flash), then the card shrinks into a compact chip that slides into a side rail and stays; chips accumulate, then a weight/price block and CTA box lock up. A cyan drone wireframe turns on a projector pad behind.
useFor: Spec sheets, feature checklists, pricing summaries — keeps every fact on screen long enough to read.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/hologram-hud (MIT, LemoLab) — hud.js chip/rollText, DEMO.md structure, poster

items.doc: specs in order: {label, value, unit, detail, part?} — part highlights the holo drone part (battery|camera|body|rotorFL|rotorFR|rotorBL|rotorBR)

every.doc: frames per spec (card in, roll, hold, dock)

lockup.doc: final block: two label/value/unit pairs and a CTA line

showModel.doc: show the hologram drone wireframe behind

background.doc: stage colour, or "transparent" for an overlay

title: Sync grid (evidence on one clock)
description: Three evidence columns (report log / dashcam / CCTV) side by side under one huge monospaced stopwatch; each column cuts in with a flash only when its source starts on the event clock, so the grid fills as time runs. At the sync point everything freezes, the key column gets a red border and a word, a red dashed line runs across the pictures and the stopwatch becomes a big red verdict.
useFor: Dashcam + CCTV + log comparisons, "which happened first", sports replays, launch/telemetry reconstructions, A/B latency demos (three apps responding to one tap), product race comparisons.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/visual-investigation demo sRun() / playhead() (MIT, LemoLab) — idea, own build

default.text:
unit 4 dispatched
caller confirms location
alarm silenced remotely
second call received
unit 4 on scene

clock.doc: [[frame, eventSeconds]] piecewise-linear event clock (can run faster than real time)

syncAt.doc: event second at which everything freezes

syncColumn.doc: index of the column that gets the red border and word

verdict.doc: big red text that replaces the stopwatch

startClock.doc: wall clock at event second 0 (format hh:mm:ss)

camLabel.doc: on-screen label inside the dashcam-style panel

title: Target lock box
description: Sci-fi target lock: an oversized faint square rotated 45° snaps onto a part in .22 s, flashes white for 3 frames, drops an anchor ring and a "TGT 01 · LOCK" mono tag; the camera whips to the next target. Default subject is a cyan hologram drone wireframe on a projector pad; works over images or as a transparent overlay.
useFor: "Look here now" pointers for product features, UI walkthroughs, sports/video analysis and spec explainers.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/hologram-hud (MIT, LemoLab) — hud.js target box, DEMO.md motion numbers

targets.doc: locks in order: {label, part (holo part: body|battery|camera|rotorFL|rotorFR|rotorBL|rotorBR) or rect [x,y,w,h] in 0..1 frame fractions, at (lock frame)}

subject.doc: 'holo' = built-in hologram drone wireframe, 'image' = show src, 'none' = boxes only (use rect targets)

src.doc: image in public/ for subject 'image' (targets then need rect)

background.doc: stage colour, or "transparent" to overlay the boxes on your own footage

title.doc: product name in the HUD header

whip.doc: 0..0.6 how far the camera whips toward each target

title: Target lock
description: Candidate boxes with ids and rising MATCH % appear over a scene half a second apart; four L-brackets fly in from the frame corners, close in and snap onto the target (1.4 to 1.0 scale), a lock ratchet ring fills, then a "TARGET LOCKED" banner opens from the centre with coordinates typing below. Works over a built-in crate scene, your image, or transparent as an overlay.
useFor: Gaming edits, tech reviews ("found the bug") and product highlights on a screenshot, face or map; pairs with target-lock-box (different 45-degree style).

target.doc: lock target {x, y as fractions of the frame, size in px at 1080p}

candidates.doc: candidate boxes [{x, y, size, id, match}] shown 0.5 s apart; match >= 90 uses the accent colour

src.doc: optional image (public/ path) used as the backdrop instead of the crate scene

background.doc: scene colour; 'transparent' renders only the HUD for use as an overlay

lockAt.doc: frame the brackets snap on (they start 13 frames earlier)

title: Zoom-through tunnel
description: Blueprint radar target opens into a tunnel of outlined capsule rings; the camera accelerates through it and a hero word punches in as the tunnel slows, with an optional arc subtitle.
useFor: "Entering the system" / hyperspace beats that land on a single key word.

word.doc: hero word that punches in at the end

subtitle.doc: text typed along an arc above the word ("" to hide)

rings.doc: number of capsule rings in depth

spin.doc: tunnel spin in radians per second

popFrame.doc: frame where the word pops (the zoom accelerates for ~2.4 s before it)

title: ASCII image grid (phosphor CRT)
description: An image or procedural scene rebuilt as amber phosphor glyphs on a strict monospace grid: brightness becomes glyph ink density and dim/normal/bold attributes, dark areas stay empty; rows type in, then the sample window slowly pushes in under constant-size glyphs.
useFor: A logo, product or photo in a terminal aesthetic for dev tools, hacker, retro-computing and data brands.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/ascii-crt demo/term.js makeRamp, pick, cellsFromImage (MIT, LemoLab)

src.doc: public/ image to convert (empty = procedural plate)

charset.doc: restrict glyphs to these characters, e.g. a sentence ("a picture made only of these words"); empty = full density ramp

reveal.doc: rows = typed top to bottom, random = cells pop in, none = already on

push.doc: grid-camera push over the whole duration (1 = none)

dither.doc: Bayer + hash dither amount (0.6–0.7 in the source)

title.doc: typed terminal title top-left with block cursor (empty = none)

title: Autofocus hunt
description: Camcorder autofocus hunting on a liminal office corridor (or any image): blur → snaps sharp → slips → locks, then a zoom from 52° to 27° and a second hunt; a far figure is visible only inside the first sharp window. REC / AF / zoom OSD and focus brackets.
useFor: Suspense reveals, "did you see that?" beats, found-footage openers, product reveals with a lens feel.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/backrooms demo/story.js focus curve + core/three/post.js CoC (MIT, LemoLab)

src.doc: public/ image to focus-hunt (empty = procedural corridor)

focusKeys.doc: [[frame, focusDistance]] with 1 = the subject in focus; overshoot past 1 and back for a hunt

fovFrom.doc: start field of view in degrees

fovTo.doc: end field of view in degrees (zoom = tan(from/2)/tan(to/2))

reveal.doc: show the far figure only while sharp between revealFrom and revealTo

revealFrom.doc: first frame the hidden figure may appear

revealTo.doc: last frame the hidden figure may appear

notice.doc: printed notice on the wall: title line then rules

signal.doc: EXIT sign colour (the only signal colour)

osd.doc: camcorder REC / AF / zoom overlay and focus brackets

osdLabel.doc: camcorder on-screen-display label next to the red dot

title: Brush-stroke reveal
description: A picture is uncovered by thick brush strokes sweeping across the frame (zigzag rows, a spiral or diagonal passes): each stroke leads with a wet ink fringe, its edge breaks into dry-brush bristle streaks, and ink pools at the stroke ends; the revealed image (or a painted sunrise) drifts in slowly and a title lands when the last stroke ends.
useFor: Ink / painterly titles, heritage and cultural stories, festival greetings, art-brand reveals: pass `src` and `title`, or your own `strokes` as 0-1 coordinates.
source: prompt corpus x24 (brush strokes reveal shapes and images, ink pooling)

src.doc: image to reveal (public/ path or URL); empty = painted sunrise

mode.doc: auto strokes: 'zigzag' | 'spiral' | 'diagonal' (ignored when `strokes` is given)

strokes.doc: [{pts:[[x,y]...] (0-1 of frame), width? (fraction of short side), at?, frames?}] custom stroke paths

title.doc: title revealed with the picture ("" = none)

subtitle.doc: small caps line above the title

strokeFrames.doc: frames one stroke takes to sweep (8-14 feels like a real stroke)

width.doc: stroke width as a fraction of the short side (0.06-0.18)

zoom.doc: slow push-in scale applied to the revealed image

palette.doc: painted-sunrise colours: [sky top, sky low, sun, ridge 1, ridge 2, lake]

title: Comic halftone post FX
description: Print-comic finish over an image: posterised toon colour, 45° halftone ink dots in the midtones and shadows, ink outlines, colour misregistration and vignette, animated on twos.
useFor: Comic / pop-art stylisation of any still or render, playful explainers, a stylised hold before comic SFX overlays.

src.doc: public/ image path; empty = procedural plate

palette.doc: procedural plate palette: dusk | night | dawn

dotPitch.doc: halftone cell size in px at 1080p (5 in the source)

dotBand.doc: [lo, hi] luminance band that gets ink dots (0.2–0.75); outside it colours stay flat

outline.doc: ink outline width in px at 1080p (3–4)

step.doc: hold every drawing for N frames (2 = on twos, 1 = smooth)

push.doc: slow push-in in %/s

registrationKick.doc: opt-in: colour plates jolt apart and ring back into register on each kick frame; amplitude in px (8-14 typical, 0 = off)

kickFrames.doc: frames the registration kicks land on (e.g. on the beats)

registrationDrift.doc: opt-in: plates slowly drift apart up to N px (about 25) over driftRange, then snap back with a click (0 = off)

driftRange.doc: [from, to] frames of the drift; the snap lands on `to`

tint.doc: opt-in mono mode: paper tint colour (e.g. #efe3c2); picture becomes ink-to-paper tones under the halftone dots (empty = full colour)

spotInks.doc: opt-in flat spot inks, dark to light (e.g. ["#1b2a6b","#e8452c"]); picture split into flat bands of these inks plus the paper tint

offsetShadow.doc: opt-in misregistered offset shadow: outlines and deep shadows re-printed in shadowInk, shifted N px, multiplied (0 = off)

shadowInk.doc: colour of the offset shadow ink

shadowAngle.doc: direction of the offset shadow in degrees (0 = right, 90 = down)

cutout.doc: opt-in scissor cut-out: a transparent-PNG src gets a faceted paper rim + drop shadow on a flat background; opaque images are cut to a hand-cut ellipse

rim.doc: cut-out rim width in px at 1080p

facets.doc: cut-out polygon tolerance in px (higher = fewer, more angular scissor facets)

cutoutBg.doc: flat background colour behind the cut-out

title: Crayon pressure pass
description: A child's crayon drawing draws itself: waxy strokes skip over a procedural paper tooth (light pressure leaves gaps, heavy fills in), zig-zag hatching overshoots the lines, the paper grain is embossed from the top-left and the indigo wobbly outlines boil on twos.
useFor: Kids / edu / family brands, "hand-drawn by a child" moments, playful onboarding and recap drawings; the wax filter idea works on any stroke art.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/microgame demo/glpass.js crayon (MIT, LemoLab) — deposit = tooth > 1 - 1.22*pressure, SVG feTurbulence approximation

text.doc: handwritten word written in magenta crayon

crayons.doc: nine hex colours: yellow, orange, red, green, dark green, blue, light blue, brown, magenta

boil.doc: line-boil steps per second (8 = on twos at 30 fps)

emboss.doc: strength of the embossed paper grain 0-1

title: Dot matrix / halftone / particle image
description: Image resampled to a grid of dots — LED billboard, print halftone duotone, glowing luma particles or pointillist dabs — with a stepped resolution ramp from abstract to legible and back.
useFor: Music-video stylisation, beat-synced reveals of a picture, retro LED signage, print/poster looks.

src.doc: public/ image path; empty = procedural plate (sampled analytically)

palette.doc: procedural plate palette: dusk | night | dawn

style.doc: led | halftone | glow | pointillism | field (analytic Ben-Day density field) | tiles (flipping mosaic tiles with grout) | text (words spelled by a cell grid)

pitch.doc: legible dot pitch in px at 1080p (led 26, halftone 13–29, glow 12–18); auto-raised to keep ≤ 5000 dots

ramp.doc: coarser pitches stepped through before the legible one ([] = no ramp)

rampStart.doc: frame of the first ramp step

rampOut.doc: reverse ramp (coarser and coarser) over the last steps

push.doc: slow push-in of the sampled image in %/s (keeps the dots alive)

holdFrames.doc: refresh the mosaic every N frames (LED low-fps feel)

matte.doc: led: cells darker than this luma become background dots (0 = off)

invert.doc: halftone: light ink on dark paper (dot size grows with brightness)

body.doc: glow: particle body colour (gold #FFC861, violet #D88BFF, white)

maxRadius.doc: glow: max particle radius in px at 1080p

field.doc: style 'field' (Ben-Day density field, no image): radial halo | edge (dots crowd the frame border) | ramp (left to right)

fieldLayers.doc: style 'field': overprinted layers [{color, angle deg, step px at 1080p, k dot size 0..1}] (multiply on paper)

fieldRadius.doc: field: halo radius / edge band, relative (0.8)

fieldSwell.doc: field: breathing amplitude of the halo (dots swell = emotion), 0 = static

tileSize.doc: style 'tiles': tile size in % of the short side

grout.doc: tiles: grout width px at 1080p (bgDot colour shows on the unflipped back of each tile)

flipFrames.doc: tiles: frames a tile flip takes

flipOrder.doc: tiles: radial (from the centre) | random | sweep (left to right)

flipSpan.doc: tiles: frames over which the flips are staggered

text.doc: style 'text': words spelled out by lit cells (panel colour is the floor)

textWave.doc: text: speed of the lattice flicker waves

zoomFrom.doc: text: camera crane start zoom (1 = none, 6 = macro to wide)

title: Duotone recolour
description: A full-colour image cross-fades into a 2–3 colour brand ramp (blue, pink-violet, ink etching with cross-hatch, madness green flash or a day-to-night grade).
useFor: Brand-colour unification of mixed stills, mood switches (calm -> panic, day -> night), print-style looks.

src.doc: public/ image path; empty = procedural plate

palette.doc: procedural plate palette: dusk | night | dawn

colors.doc: custom ramp dark -> light (2–3 hex colours) overriding the preset

push.doc: slow push-in in %/s

hatch.doc: ink-etching: cross-hatch opacity in the darks (0.25 in the source)

word.doc: madness: word that flickers on (+0.30 s for 2 f, off 3 f, then steady), e.g. 狂気

sCurve.doc: S-curve contrast strength for the ramp (0 = preset; 0.32 print grade, 0.18 documents)

paperFibre.doc: paper-fibre texture multiplied over the print 0..1 (0.5 = print grade)

redOverlay.doc: spot-colour layer multiplied over the recolour (e.g. #D23A2A constructivist red); empty = none

title: Film finishing stack
description: Cinematic finish over an image: bloom on highlights, radial chromatic fringe, grain, vignette, gate weave, a flickering blue anamorphic flare streak and optional 2.39:1 bars (or overlay-only mode).
useFor: Making any still or scene feel shot on film; a final pass over composites; a flare accent on a light source.
notes: overlay:true (+ flare:false, letterbox:'off') is the finishing frame layer on top of any mix.

src.doc: public/ image path; empty = procedural plate

palette.doc: procedural plate palette: dusk | night | dawn

overlay.doc: true = transparent background, only grain / vignette / flare / bars (layer over another scene)

fringe.doc: chromatic fringe at the frame edge in px at 1080p

flareLength.doc: streak length as a fraction of the width (0.8)

push.doc: slow push-in in %/s

look.doc: preset on top of untouched props: film (default) | print (damaged nitrate print: scratches, dust, hair, burn, sepia, flicker) | crt (scanlines, roll band, slice glitch, fringe) | projector (rounded 1.37 gate, flicker, scratches)

hair.doc: a hair that lives in the gate for a few frames now and then

burn.doc: brown burn creeping in from the edges 0..1

phosphor.doc: monochrome phosphor tint colour (e.g. #33ff66); empty = off

impactFlashAt.doc: frame of a white-hot impact flash (-1 = none)

gate.doc: projector gate aspect (1.37 = academy); 0 = off. Black surround with rounded corners

title: Mondrian glass pane grid
description: A black-leaded Mondrian grid draws on over an image; each glass pane offsets, scales and tints its piece of the picture and keeps drifting, like looking through stained glass.
useFor: Fractured / multiple-perspective beats, art-history or design references, stylish holds on a hero image.

src.doc: public/ image path; empty = procedural plate

palette.doc: procedural plate palette: dusk | night | dawn

depth.doc: subdivision depth (3 = few big panes, 5 = many)

barWidth.doc: leading bar width in px at 1080p (10–12 measured at 720p, ≈14 at 1080p)

maxOffset.doc: max pane offset as a fraction of the frame width (0.03–0.06)

driftDuration.doc: frames for the refraction offsets to ease in (easeInQuad), then a slow drift continues

start.doc: frame the leading starts drawing on

mode.doc: 'panes' (Mondrian refraction grid) | 'leaded' (stained-glass panel: lozenge lattice of jewel pieces, dark lead with solder blobs, streaky glass, backlight band)

cellSize.doc: leaded: piece size in px at 1080p (30-80)

lead.doc: leaded: lead came width in px at 1080p

jewels.doc: leaded: jewel colour palette the pieces cycle through

backlight.doc: leaded: strength of the backlight band sweeping across

bandAt.doc: leaded: frame the backlight band starts (-1 = start + 30)

title: Glitch image bursts
description: An image hit by timed digital-glitch bursts: RGB-split band displacement, datamosh column smear, stage-rewind bands with black slivers, 1–2 frame CMY silhouette flashes and a rainbow chroma echo trail.
useFor: Beat hits, "system error" / hacked moments, energetic transitions between stills, music-video accents.

src.doc: public/ image path; empty = procedural plate

palette.doc: procedural plate palette: dusk | night | dawn

bursts.doc: list of {at, frames, kind: bands|smear|rewind|flash|echo, strength} — the intensity envelope

maxShift.doc: max band shift as a fraction of the width (0.02–0.08)

rgbSplit.doc: R/B channel offset in px at 1080p inside glitched bands

tint.doc: teal tint for some bands / smear edge

smearColumn.doc: [x0, x1] 0..1 column of the datamosh smear (≈25 % W)

smearY.doc: source row (0..1) of the smear, i.e. the top of the subject

push.doc: slow push-in in %/s

look.doc: 'clean' (default) | 'vhs' (1990s camcorder tape: chroma shifted + smeared, edge halos, lifted blacks, streaky noise, wobble, head-switching band, dropouts, 4:3 pillarbox)

chromaShift.doc: vhs: chroma shift to the right in px

dropouts.doc: vhs: white dropout streak density multiplier

trackingTearAt.doc: vhs: frames at which a tracking-tear band slips sideways

mode.doc: 'glitch' (default, burst toolkit) | 'silhouette' (a solid colour silhouette filled with scrolling code, stepping through poses, glitch-tile bursts, typed caption on black)

textFill.doc: silhouette: colour of the scrolling code text in the fill

silBursts.doc: silhouette: frames at which tile bursts spray out

poses.doc: silhouette: [{rot, sx, sy, dx}] stepped every ~3.5 frames (empty = seeded micro-poses)

caption.doc: silhouette: mono caption typed beside the silhouette with a "_" cursor

title: Grid multiply
description: The frame splits 1×2 → 2×2 → 3×3 → 4×4 on the beat; each stage lights its cells in a scattered order over the previous stage (never black), the last beat re-cuts every cell every sixteenth, then it slams back to one picture.
useFor: Montage climaxes, "everything at once" beats, product-range / UGC / location walls synced to music; pass your own `images`.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/city-symphony (MIT, LemoLab) — render.py grid_plate, ORDER9/ORDER16

images.doc: public/ image paths cycled through the cells (empty = procedural scenes)

stages.doc: [{at: frame, cols, rows}] — one stage per half bar or bar; cols/rows swap in portrait

bpm.doc: tempo: the 1×2 halves light half a beat apart, cells fill on sixteenths (≤ 0.3 s per stage)

frantic.doc: on the last beat re-cut every cell every sixteenth

franticAt.doc: frame where the frantic re-cutting starts

endFullAt.doc: frame where it slams back to one full picture (0 = never)

push.doc: slow zoom per second inside each cell

grade.doc: release-print finish: contrast, desaturation, grain, vignette and 1.85 matte

title: Handscroll reveal
description: A long ink-wash landscape pans right-to-left like an unrolling Chinese handscroll (procedural mountains, pines, a lone boat — or your images printed on the paper), then the camera pulls back to the whole scroll mounted on silk with wooden rollers on a dark table, and a vermilion seal stamps the end.
useFor: Timelines, histories, journeys, supply chains — any linear story shown as one continuous artwork.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/ink-wash (MIT, LemoLab) — STYLE.md §6/§8, DEMO.md ending

images.doc: optional public/ images, one per panel (printed into the scroll); empty slots paint procedural ink landscapes

panels.doc: number of panels in the scroll

title.doc: vertical title column on the first panel

pullbackAt.doc: frame the pull-back to the mounted scroll starts

mountColor.doc: sheen colour behind the mounted scroll

title: Ken Burns push / pull / tilt
description: Slow push, pull, pan or tall tilt-up across a still plate with handheld noise, an optional punch-in cut, rain and print grain.
useFor: Turning any still (AI art, photo, illustration) into a living shot; emphasis punch-ins on a caption beat; cold-open tilt reveals of tall images.
avoid: Do not use ken-burns as the only motion of a piece: add type + an accent, or pick a richer image look (film-look, light-sweep, duotone).

src.doc: public/ image path (e.g. "demo/owl.jpg"); empty = procedural dusk plate

images.doc: several public/ images: the duration is split into hard-cut shots alternating push / pull

palette.doc: procedural plate palette: dusk | night | dawn

mode.doc: push | pull | pan | tall-tilt (tilts bottom -> top over a tall image)

rate.doc: scale change in %/s (ambient 0.6–2, emotional 3–5, warm push 8–9)

focus.doc: [x, y] 0..1 point the push moves toward (subject / eyes)

pan.doc: [dx, dy] lateral drift in px/s at 1080p

handheld.doc: handheld noise amplitude in px (0 = locked off)

punchAt.doc: frame of the punch-in hard cut (-1 = off)

punchFocus.doc: [x, y] subject the punch-in re-centres on

drift.doc: tall-tilt horizontal drift in px/s (camera pans right for positive)

fadeIn.doc: fade from black over this many frames (tall-tilt source: 18)

punches.doc: stepped beat punch-ins [{at: frame, zoom}] e.g. [{at:60,zoom:1.4},{at:75,zoom:2},{at:90,zoom:2.9}]

kick.doc: damped kick shakes on hits [{at: frame, amp: px}]

rig.doc: handheld camcorder rig amount (0 = off, 1 = documentary): gait bob, sway, roll, breathing, tremor

fear.doc: rig: fear keys 0..1 spread across the duration; tremor grows with fear

holdBreath.doc: rig: [[fromFrame, toFrame]] ranges where bob and breathing freeze

layers.doc: multi-plane dolly: [{src, depth 0..1}] full-frame (transparent png) layers, far to near; near layers push faster

depthRate.doc: multi-plane: %/s zoom at depth 1 (far layers move 40 % of it)

title: Knife colour relay
description: A cool-grey, wet-looking palette-knife painting is re-laid in colour stroke by stroke by a wave spreading from a point: each stroke sweeps from grey to colour along its own length. Strokes in exceptionMask (default: the red umbrella) stay in colour from the start, the one-colour exception. Set revealSpeed 0 for exception-only, exceptionMask [] for a pure wave.
useFor: "The world wakes up", rebrand, recovery, season turning — a story beat; or "everything grey except this one thing".

src.doc: optional image in public/ — grey copy with a colour wave (procedural landscape when empty)

revealOrigin.doc: wave origin [x, y] as fractions of the frame

revealSpeed.doc: wave speed in u per frame (0 = never reveal, exception only)

revDur.doc: frames each stroke takes to turn to colour

exceptionMask.doc: scene groups kept in colour: umbrella, house, tree, river, sun, sky, hills, field

title: Knife paint plate
description: An illustration becomes a palette-knife oil painting: a slanted mosaic of flat paint planes (coarse underpainting, then detail strokes only where the picture needs it) with lit ridges from a raking light and canvas weave showing through. Strokes paint on in a diagonal sweep, each growing along its own length; the raking light drifts afterwards. Default plate is a procedural river landscape; with src the picture is knife-filtered with ridge texture.
useFor: Premium oil-painting look for heroes, art/culture brands and emotional ads; a paint-on reveal for any image.

src.doc: optional image in public/ — knife-filtered with ridge overlay (the procedural landscape is used when empty)

lightAngle.doc: raking-light direction in degrees (225 = from upper left)

grey.doc: 0..1 how much of the colour is replaced by cool grey

appearDur.doc: frames the sweep takes to cross the plate

palette.doc: override scene colours: {skyTop, skyLow, sun, hillFar, hillNear, field, river, leaf, leafHi, wall, roof, door, umbrella …}

canvas.doc: bare canvas colour showing between strokes

lightKeys.doc: raking-light elevation keyframes [[frame, 0..1], ...]; a LOW elevation = grazing light = stronger ridge glints (peak beat)

rakingAt.doc: frame of a raking-light peak: the light drops to a grazing angle so every ridge glints, then settles (0 = off)

rakingLow.doc: elevation at the bottom of the dip (0.15)

rakingDur.doc: frames the dip takes in total (~2 s = 60)

title: Night light sweep
description: Cinematic night lighting: headlights sweep across a rain-streaked window, sodium street lamps flicker on with volumetric cones through rain, or a door opens and floods a corridor floor with light and a long shadow.
useFor: Mood beats in night scenes: a car passing, arriving somewhere at night, a reveal of someone at the door.

src.doc: public/ image for the outside view (window / street / doorway); empty = procedural night (dawn for door)

mode.doc: headlight | streetlamp | door | reveal (dim picture lit by a passing soft diagonal band of light) | neon (bands of coloured light slide across a held picture)

figure.doc: door: a figure steps into the doorway and casts a long shadow

push.doc: slow push-in in %/s

sweepFrames.doc: reveal: frames the sweep takes (~1.3 s = 39)

base.doc: reveal: brightness of the unlit picture (0.07)

soft.doc: reveal: band softness as a fraction of the sweep (0.26)

glint.doc: reveal: glint riding the front, 0 = none (<= 0.2)

keep.doc: reveal: stay lit after the band passes (false = the band lights only what it covers)

bandFrames.doc: neon: frames one band takes to cross

bandWidth.doc: neon: band width as a fraction of the frame diagonal

palette.doc: procedural plate palette when no src (dusk | night | dawn)

title: Negative develop reveal
description: A photo lies on a backlit light table as a warm amber glass negative; a circular develop front with a thin orange edge spreads from one point and turns it into a silver-gelatin (or colour) positive.
useFor: Before/after reveals: archive photos, "the real picture" moments, X-ray → product, a teaser image coming into view.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/archive-lighttable demo/film.js negative() + lens develop front (MIT, LemoLab)

src.doc: public/ image to develop (empty = procedural city plate)

origin.doc: [x, y] 0..1 inside the photo where the develop front starts

mode.doc: fullframe = the whole plate develops; lens = only a loupe-sized disc develops

mono.doc: true = silver-gelatin greys (archive), false = keep the colour of the photo

edgeColor.doc: colour of the warm ring riding the front

label.doc: mono caption under the plate (empty = none)

title: Perspective flatten
description: An oblique broadcast-style photo of a pitch un-tilts smoothly (a true homography, ease-in-out) into a straight top-down chalk board — the photo fades as a dark board with chalk lines and a faint grid takes over, the players become ring marks at their real positions, and shot markers drop onto the board one after another. Give it src + imagePoints + boardPoints to flatten your own photo of a pitch, court, floor, desk or whiteboard.
useFor: Turning any oblique photo into a map or plan: sports shot maps, floor plans from a room photo, a whiteboard photo straightened into a clean diagram, real-estate site plans. A strong "how did they do that" moment.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/telestrator/demo/index.html — shotMap / flatten mesh (MIT, LemoLab)

src.doc: optional photo in public/ — flattened with the homography from imagePoints → boardPoints (default: the built-in oblique pitch)

board.doc: chalk board preset: pitch (105×68 m), court (28×15 m) or floor (12×8 m plan)

imagePoints.doc: photo control points as [x,y] fractions of the frame (≥ 4, same order as boardPoints); empty = built-in camera

boardPoints.doc: the same points in board units (metres for the presets); empty = corners, mid-line and quarter points

markers.doc: dots that drop on the board: {board:[u,v] | img:[x,y], color, size (m), at (s), label}

showPlayers.doc: ring marks at the photo's player positions after the flatten

title: Photomontage tower
description: Constructivist photomontage: print-graded photo strips slam in from alternate sides on 16th notes as the floors of a tower, an ink beam under each, paper-bordered cut-out figures land on every other floor; the camera climbs, a big floor counter runs and turns red while it rests on dated anchors with captions, a deco crown tops it, then the camera pulls back to the whole tower.
useFor: "People built this" — company growth, team milestones, user photos stacked into a product, building or logo.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/kino-montage (MIT, LemoLab) — STYLE.md §6 photomontage tower, DEMO.md shot 14

floors.doc: number of floors (strips) in the tower

images.doc: optional photos in public/ used for the strips in turn (print-graded); empty = procedural archive scenes

default.label: Week 4
default.caption: The frame passes the old water tower

default.label: Week 7
default.caption: Steel tops out at the setback

anchors.doc: counter rests: {floor, label, caption} — building pauses while the caption is up

bpm.doc: beat grid (floors on 16ths, then 8ths)

crown.doc: deco crown and red flag on top

title: Pixelate + Bayer dither look
description: Image rendered as chunky 6 px pixel art with 2x2 Bayer ordered dither, a 5–8 colour hue ramp, 2.34:1 letterbox, grain and vignette, slowly tilting.
useFor: Retro game / pixel-art cinematics, moody cold opens, unifying mixed stills into one pixel style.

src.doc: public/ image path; empty = procedural plate

palette.doc: procedural plate palette: dusk | night | dawn

pixelSize.doc: virtual pixel size in px at 1080p (source: 6)

colors.doc: luminance ramp dark -> light (3–8 colours); [] keeps source colours, posterised

dither.doc: 2x2 Bayer dither strength in palette steps (0 = none, 1 = classic)

tilt.doc: slow vertical tilt in px/s (+ = tilt up)

push.doc: slow push-in in %/s

letterbox.doc: auto (landscape only) | on | off — hard black bars

aspect.doc: active picture aspect (2.34 in the source)

embers.doc: number of rising pixel embers (0 = none)

fadeIn.doc: fade from black over this many frames

ladder.doc: palette collapse: colour-depth steps, one per stepFrames after collapseAt, e.g. ['c16','c8','gb4','c2','faded'] (presets full 24 steps | c16 | c8 resampled from colors | gb4 | c2 | faded fixed blue-greys, or a hex ramp string '#000,#445,#aab'); [] = off

stepFrames.doc: palette collapse: frames per step (a beat, 15 = 0.5 s)

collapseAt.doc: palette collapse: frame of the first step

title: Press and lift (entrance / exit preset)
description: Arrivals come in large and blurry, as if held near the lamp, then snap sharp onto the screen with a thud; exits grow, blur and fade into light like lifting a puppet away. Shown on three paper tags over a lamp-lit cloth.
useFor: A universal comes-into-focus / fades-into-memory entrance for any layer: a rumour growing, a deadline pressing in, forgotten items lifting away. Copy the numbers (scale 2.6 -> 1, blur 34 -> 0, 0.55 s; lift 1 -> 1.9, 0.9 s) onto any wrapper.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/shadow-puppet demo/main.js (sun pieces), STYLE.md §5 (MIT, LemoLab)

items.doc: tag texts (one tag per item)

images.doc: optional image per tag (public path or URL)

maxBlur.doc: blur in u at the far end

firstInAt.doc: frame the first tag starts to press on

liftAt.doc: frame the first tag starts to lift off

thud.doc: small squash and ring at the snap

title: Proportion sweep
description: A bright honey bar sweeps across live footage to X % of the width; everything it has passed turns grey and dark, the percentage slams in on the dark side, then a caption chunk lands with its keyword on a yellow block.
useFor: Any "X % of …" statistic over a photo or video — share lost, churn, coverage — instantly readable with the sound off.

src.doc: public/ photo (empty = procedural footage plate)

percent.doc: share of the width that goes dark (0–100)

direction.doc: fromRight = the bar sweeps in from the right edge, fromLeft = from the left

caption.default: Two in five homes are still dark
caption.doc: caption line slammed in after the number

keyword.doc: substring of the caption shown on the accent block

darkFilter.doc: CSS filter for the passed side

title: Riso plate reveal
description: A risograph print inked one colour at a time: first only the blue plate exists; then a roller sweeps across and the yellow plate inks in left to right with a heavier band at its edge (the blank-paper scarf lights up); later the pink plate arrives and the overprint colours appear. Registration offsets and a kick on each arrival.
useFor: Brand / product reveals where a new colour is a new feature, history timelines (one ink per era), "colour returning" recoveries, zine and indie title intros. Pass `src` to print any image in three plates.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/risograph demo/riso.js (uGate, uSweep, band), STYLE.md §8 "Plates as narrative" (MIT / CC BY 4.0, LemoLab); original implementation

inks.doc: plate colours in print order (up to 3)

arrivals.doc: [{plate, at, sweepFrames, from:'left'|'right'}] frame each plate arrives and how long the roller sweep takes (0 = fades in)

src.doc: optional image (public path) to print in three plates instead of the built-in poster

title.doc: title printed in the third plate of the built-in poster

kick.doc: px kick of a plate on arrival

band.doc: extra ink density of the roller edge band (0..1)

thresholds.doc: image mode: per-plate darkness thresholds (0..1; defaults 0.58 / 0.95 / 0.74 for blue / yellow / pink)

title: Spinning headline (newsreel paper)
description: A newspaper spins out of the dark desk into the lens — growing and decelerating through 2.5 turns with faint motion-blur ghosts — slams flat with a jolt, pushes toward the headline, punches in on a beat, and a warm-white grease-pencil ring is drawn around the detail; all inside a flickering 1.37:1 projector gate.
useFor: "The headline said…" beats in history, PR, legal, true-crime and news explainers; works with your own front-page image.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/newsreel (MIT code, CC BY 4.0 docs, LemoLab) — demo/index.html scenePaper

src.doc: optional newspaper / telegram / poster image (replaces the procedural front page)

subhead.default: Ten thousand turn out for the first crossing

focus.doc: push target [x, y] 0..1 of the paper

damage.doc: projector damage amount 0..1 (flicker, scratches, dust, grain)

title: Split-grid countdown
description: One shot splits into 2, then 4, then a 3×3 wall of synced cameras (chips + LIVE SYNC badges) around a big T− clock as zero approaches — new cells pop from dashed STANDBY slots — and at zero every cell slides to its tile and fuses into one full-screen picture with a warm flash.
useFor: Launches, product drops, election / sports / score countdowns, multi-camera event recaps and "many sources agree" evidence beats; pass your own `images`.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/countdown (MIT, LemoLab) — demo/index.html LAY/layoutAt/render merge, chip, syncBadge, drawClock

images.doc: public/ image paths for the camera feeds (cycled; empty = procedural scenes)

mergeSrc.doc: the full-screen shot everything fuses into at zero (default: the third image)

cams.doc: [{code, name, sub, sync: live|window|retimed}] chip + honest sync badge per feed

zeroFrame.doc: frame of T−0: cells merge (0.42 s) and the clock inverts

wallAt.doc: frame of the 3×3 wall (clock moves to the centre cell)

popEvery.doc: frames between new wall cells connecting

accent.doc: accent colour (T−, synced dots, landing flash)

standbyLabel.doc: text in a camera cell that has no feed yet

title: Sticker cutout burst
description: A subject cut-out becomes a die-cut sticker with a jagged white border and dark keyline, slammed onto spinning pink and yellow radial rays with boiling shiver marks and puffs, while a yellow spiky burst with a pink back-burst pops a shock caption character by character; on the freeze it turns into a tilted photo card on a cyan stripe board.
useFor: Meme / reaction freeze-frame moments, product hero stickers and thumbnails in motion; give it a transparent PNG as `src`.
source: mg-styles-15 demos/18-hanazi burstD, raysD, focusD, puff, card + assets/prep*.py matte (MIT)

src.doc: transparent PNG cut-out (public/ path); empty = a drawn peach

caption.doc: shock word inside the burst (short)

marks.doc: shiver marks and puffs around the sticker

freezeToCard.doc: freeze, then turn the sticker into a photo card on a stripe board

seed.doc: seed for burst jitter and the sticker edge

title: Sticker slap
description: Photo or icon cut-outs with a thick white outline drop onto the page from above the camera: large, tilted and blurred with a wide soft shadow, then land flat with a tiny squash and a two-cycle wobble while the shadow tightens on contact and the whole page jolts a few pixels.
useFor: The universal photo-to-sticker treatment for explainers, social posts and product callouts. Give transparent PNG cut-outs as src; overlay-capable with background transparent.
source: mg-styles-15 demos/19-paperclip slap() / shadow(), tools/stickers.py cutout(), 06-collage rimmed() (MIT)

items.doc: stickers[{kind: cup|bolt|flower|camera (procedural fallback), src: transparent PNG path (optional), x,y: offset from centre as fraction of width/height, size, at: landing frame, rot: resting degrees}]

background.doc: page colour ('transparent' to use as an overlay)

title.doc: big faint word behind the stickers

outline.doc: white outline thickness in px at 1080p (8-12)

jolt.doc: page jolt in px at each landing (4-8)

title: Telestrator freeze (analysis board)
description: Footage, a still or the built-in demo pitch freezes with a white flash and a small zoom punch, colour drains and cools and everything outside a focus ellipse darkens; a yellow ring draws clockwise under the subject with a rotating dashed outer ring and light beam, a glowing marker arrow draws along a path, a red space patch fades in and a black label card wipes open; then play resumes.
useFor: Sports and gameplay analysis, UX screen-recording teardowns ("freeze the recording and circle the button"), product demos, coaching, CCTV-style explainers over any footage or screenshot.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/telestrator demo/index.html (ring, marker, tag, grade, spot, flash) + STYLE.md §6, §9.1–9.2 (MIT / CC BY 4.0, LemoLab)

src.doc: optional still image (public path) to freeze on; empty = demo pitch

videoSrc.doc: optional video (public path): plays, freezes at freezeAt for holdFrames, then resumes

holdFrames.doc: frames the freeze lasts (1.8-2.4 s typical)

focus.doc: focus ellipse as 0..1 of the frame: cx, cy, rx, ry — outside it darkens

rings.doc: rings under subjects: x, y (0..1), r (fraction of height), color, at (frames after freeze), beam

arrows.doc: marker arrows: pts [[x,y]...] 0..1, color, at, dash, arrow

areas.doc: translucent space patches: poly [[x,y]...], at, color

labels.doc: label cards: x, y (0..1 top-left), title, sub, color, at

teamAColor.doc: demo pitch: team A shirt colour

teamBColor.doc: demo pitch: team B shirt colour

title: Tilt-shift diorama
description: A high three-quarter view of a little lit isometric town (cars, windows warming up, a train looping the track) where only a horizontal band is sharp and everything above and below melts into blur, with boosted saturation and vignette so it reads as a tabletop model. The sharp band follows the train. With src it applies the same tilt-shift to any picture.
useFor: Miniature look over any city / landscape plate, map overviews, "toy world" openers; overlay-capable as an image filter.

src.doc: optional image in public/ to tilt-shift instead of the built-in town

center.doc: band centre as a fraction of height (used when follow is false or with src)

width.doc: half-width of the fully sharp band (fraction of height, ~.1)

falloff.doc: distance from sharp to maximum blur (fraction of height, ~.3)

maxBlur.doc: maximum blur diameter in px at 1080p (16–18)

follow.doc: procedural scene only: band follows the train head (clamped .2–.8)

saturation.doc: colour boost that sells the miniature (1.15–1.4)

title: Torn-paper collage
description: Photos (procedural scenes by default), a circle, a star and a label strip with torn white edges, taped corners and halftone slap onto a kraft dotted board one by one with a one-frame overshoot, boil on twos with a little jitter, then a black torn headline strip stamps on.
useFor: Editorial explainers, music videos, zine-style social posts and recaps that show host photos: pass your images in pieces[].src and your words in headline.

pieces.doc: pieces [{kind:photo|circle|star|blob|note, src?(public path), scene?(procedural 0-3), x,y (0-1 landscape centre), px,py (portrait centre), w,h (px at 1080), rot, tape:top|corner|both|none, color?, label?(note), delay?}]

headline.doc: black torn strip text ("" for none)

step.doc: hold each drawing for N frames (2 = on twos)

tear.doc: torn edge displacement in px at 1080 (6-12)

title: Wash arrival
description: A hillside village by a lake sits as a pure ink sketch on cream paper; colour then floods outward from a little walker along the path and from the sunrise like watercolour on wet paper — an irregular cauliflower front with a darker pooled tide line just behind it, granulation, a brief wet sheen and a wash slightly off-register from the line. Whatever the sources touch becomes painted; the rest stays line until colour arrives (everything is flooded by floodAt). Give lineSrc / colorSrc to reveal your own picture.
useFor: "Colour follows the product / runner / sunrise" storytelling, sketch → finished-render reveals for architecture and real estate, onboarding illustrations that come alive.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/urban-sketch/demo/engine.js arrivalField + compositor; STYLE.md §8 (MIT, LemoLab)

lineSrc.doc: optional line-art image in public/ (dark lines on white) — used as the ink layer

colorSrc.doc: optional colour image in public/ — the paint layer (an ink layer is derived from its edges when lineSrc is empty)

sources.doc: colour sources in a 1000×620 design space: {x,y,t (s), v (units/s), R (reach), sy (vertical stretch), path:[[x,y]…] + t1 for a moving source}

amp.doc: front irregularity (noise offset in design units)

creep.doc: seconds per unit beyond the reach radius

floodAt.doc: seconds by which any unpainted area is flooded

walker.doc: draw the little walker that rides the path source

title: Woodblock print reveal
description: On a blank washi sheet an original ukiyo-e harbour print is "printed": the black key-line block lands first, then each colour block (blues, sea bands, green, ochre, vermilion) is revealed by a ragged diagonal baren-sweep in 12 quantised steps, sliding a few pixels into slightly imperfect register, with woodgrain, baren unevenness and goma-zuri specks in every block; a double border draws, the title cartouche drops in and a chipped red seal stamps. Nature moves on eights. With src the photo is posterised into luminance blocks and printed the same way.
useFor: "Printing" a logo, illustration, map or product shot into existence; heritage / craft / Japanese-themed openers; any multi-layer reveal (riso, screen-print).
source: lemo-opuscar styles/ukiyoe/demo/print.js, STYLE.md §5 §8 (MIT, LemoLab) — original composition, not a famous print

src.doc: optional image in public/ — posterised into 5 luminance blocks and printed instead of the built-in harbour

start.doc: seconds before the first block prints

speed.doc: print pace multiplier (1 = ~0.35 s per block)

misregister.doc: block registration offset multiplier (0 = perfect register)

push.doc: slow camera push over the clip (0.04 = 4 %)

title: Woodcut carve (form-following knife cuts)
description: A picture turns into a white-line woodcut: thousands of separate knife cuts that wrap around forms (along the isophotes), wide where the image is bright and absent where it is dark, carved in live from highlights to shadows, then printed on paper with a ragged block edge, ink speckle and an optional copper colour plate glowing out of the brightest cuts. Default is a procedural moonlit-hills picture; pass `src` for any image.
useFor: A very crafted treatment for book trailers, folk / heritage brands, history explainers and editorial portraits: give it any still and it carves it live. Pairs with ken-burns for a push.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/woodcut demo/engine filter.js, hatch.js, knife.js, print.js (MIT, LemoLab) — own SVG implementation

src.doc: image path (public/ or URL); empty = built-in moonlit-hills picture

sp.doc: spacing between cuts in px at 1080 (5 = fine, 10 = bold)

black.doc: tone below which nothing is cut (0-1)

white.doc: tone at which cuts reach full width (0-1)

a0.doc: fallback cut angle in radians where the picture has no direction

paper.doc: paper colour (also the colour of the cuts)

plateColor.doc: colour plate printed in the brightest cuts ("" = none)

plateAbove.doc: tone above which cuts take the colour plate (0-1)

plateFrames.doc: [from, to] frames the colour plate fades in

margin.doc: paper margin as a fraction of the short side

maxCuts.doc: cap on the number of cuts (performance)

title: X-ray scan reveal
description: A glowing vertical scan beam (or an inky organic blob / hatched hole) sweeps across an image, revealing a glowing x-ray / blueprint line-art version in its wake.
useFor: Showing what is inside / how it works, scanning or analysing beats, tech and science explainers.

src.doc: public/ image path (edge-detected into an x-ray); empty = procedural plate drawn as line art

palette.doc: procedural plate palette: dusk | night | dawn

mode.doc: beam | blob | hole | cutaway (half-section drawing of an object: hatched cut walls around a glowing core)

look.doc: blueprint (lavender on navy) | xray (cyan on deep blue)

speed.doc: beam speed in frame-widths per second (0.75 measured)

passes.doc: beam passes: 1 = reveal only, 2 = reveal then sweep back to colour

glowWidth.doc: beam glow half-width in px at 1080p (40–60)

reticle.doc: draw construction circles / reticle over the x-ray

push.doc: slow push-in in %/s

words.doc: beam mode karaoke cursor: [{text, at}] words laid across the frame; the beam's leading edge advances on each word's `at` frame, revealing the word cut into the x-ray layer

orbitDeg.doc: cutaway: slow camera drift in degrees over the shot

cutAngle.doc: cutaway: cut extent in degrees (180 = half section)

title: Choropleth fill (tile map + legend)
description: An abstract hex/square tile territory fills region by region with a colour ramp driven by values, with labels, count-ups, a gradient legend and a highest-region callout. Regions are generic tiles, not real borders.
useFor: Regional comparisons (sales by state, scores by team, adoption by country) when you just need the pattern, not exact geography. Name tiles with `labels`; for real borders use painted-choropleth or a map image.

values.doc: one number per region (also sets how many tiles there are)

labels.doc: one short label per region (same order as values)

colors.doc: colour ramp low -> high (2+ hex colours)

order.doc: fill order: "wave" (left to right), "value" (low to high), "index"

showValues.doc: print the value on every tile

highlight.doc: outline + legend marker for the highest region at the end

title: City zoom + label card
description: A world map zooms (expo ease, graticule re-scaling) down to a lat/lon, a pin pings, and a label card with name, subtitle and coordinates slides in.
useFor: "We are here" / location reveals, store or event locators, travel and news establishing shots, any beat that goes from the world to one place. Set `lat`, `lon`, `label`.

tag.doc: small caps line above the name

zoom.doc: final zoom in px per degree at 1080 scale (world view is ~5; 110 = a region; the baked coastline is simplified, so above ~250 it looks faceted)

showCoords.doc: print the lat/lon on the card

landStroke.doc: coastline, grid and card border colour

monoFamily.doc: CSS font-family for the coordinates line

title: Coverage route (floor plan)
description: Top-down mid-century floor plan: a robot route draws itself region by region — a wall-follow loop, then back-and-forth lanes that flow around furniture without crossing, curls at every U-turn, stars and dots popping between lanes, a dotted return to the dock — while the camera pulls back and counter-rotates to reveal a patterned whole.
useFor: Robot vacuums / mowers, delivery rounds, sprinkler or cleaning coverage, "how the algorithm covers the space" payoffs.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/midcentury-toon (MIT code, CC BY 4.0 docs, LemoLab) — demo/film.js laneY/buildPath/planProgress

zones.doc: regions drawn one per beat [{x0, x1 (0..1 of room width), color, label}]

items.doc: furniture obstacles [{shape: round|sofa|plant|rect, x, y (0..1), rx, ry (fraction of room), color}]

dock.doc: dock position [x, y] 0..1 of the room

curl.doc: curl radius at U-turns in u (0 = none)

returnFrames.doc: frames for the dotted return home

routeEdge.doc: darker off-register edge under the route

decor.doc: stars and dots revealed between lanes

caption.doc: caption card after the return ("" to hide)

title: Elevation profile
description: A route elevation line draws left to right, coloured by steepness, with a moving marker and live distance / total gain / grade readouts and a peak flag.
useFor: Hike, ride, run and race route explainers, stage profiles, any height-versus-distance story. Pass `data` (heights, evenly spaced along the route) and `distance`.

data.doc: elevation samples along the route (any unit, evenly spaced, 2+ numbers)

distance.doc: total route length, shown on the x axis and distance readout

colorByGrade.doc: colour the line by steepness (accent = steep up, accent2 = flat/down)

accent.doc: steep climbs, area glow, gain readout

title: Flight arcs (great-circle routes)
description: Great-circle arcs fly between lat/lon cities on a flat map: planes (or dots) travel with a glowing trail, cities ping on arrival, a distance counter adds up.
useFor: Global reach, shipping and travel routes, network/hub-and-spoke stories, "from here to there" beats; swap `routes` for any lat/lon pairs.

routes.doc: array of {from:{lat,lon,label?}, to:{lat,lon,label?}}; the camera fits them all

subtitle.default: Hub to hub, around the map

lift.doc: arc height as a fraction of the route length on screen (0 = flat)

trail.doc: glowing trail length as a fraction of the route

title: Hairline feature trace
description: On a dark raking-lit survey surface, 1-px amber hairlines light up along traced features in order (compound walls, a sinuous road, a pipe run, a boundary loop). Each line has a bright head glow at the drawing front and a faint halo behind, stays crisp at any distance, and is draped on the terrain while the camera drifts.
useFor: Route, network and boundary reveals on terrains and maps; complements map-route and topdown-terrain.

speed.doc: draw speed in plan units per frame (200-unit plot)

caption.doc: small caption at the bottom-left of the frame

surface.doc: low-ground colour of the lit surface

title: Iso diorama board
description: A floating flat-isometric diorama board (cream top, soil strata and a blue water corner on its front edges) builds up: stations drop in with a squash — farm, plant, port, city — trees pop, then a dashed ink route draws far-to-near with a red subject cube riding it; label pins with values pop at each stop and a legend card locks the total. Flat three-tone shading, no outlines.
useFor: Supply chains, onboarding flows, product journeys, "how X works" explainers as one premium map.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/iso-infographic (MIT, LemoLab) — engine.js projection/tri, world.js board, DEMO.md

title.doc: board title (top-left and on the legend)

stations.doc: route stops in order: {pos [x,y] 0..1 on the board, label, value, unit, kind farm|plant|port|city|shop}

bpm.doc: pace of the route (one leg ≈ 2.2 beats)

palette.doc: ground, boardTop, sea and subject (accent) colours

zoomOut.doc: pull back to the legend card at the end

footnote.doc: small caps footnote under the total ("" hides)

title: Map mask reveal
description: A choropleth map fills in west to east; one region is outlined in the accent with a leader label, the camera pushes into it, then a photo of the place grows out of the region's own outline until it fills the frame.
useFor: Location stories, store / branch reveals, travel and real-estate videos, regional news.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/caption-news demo/main.js shotMap(); tools/map_prep.py (MIT, LemoLab)

regionIndex.doc: index of the highlighted region (-1 = an inland default)

label.doc: region name (leader label and final caption)

src.doc: public/ photo of the place (empty = procedural plate)

pushAt.doc: frame the camera push starts (1.3 s)

maskAt.doc: frame the photo starts growing out of the outline

title: Painted choropleth map
description: A painted island map: the coastline is brushed in, then regions fill with quantised watercolour bands (wobbly wash edges, three-pass look) driven by station data; the field can morph through time (e.g. 50 Ma to today) with a radial fill reveal, a huge serif year label and a band legend.
useFor: Climate / data stories in a warm editorial look; election or survey maps for softer brands; "how X spread" maps. Pass your own `stations` and bands.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/watercolor demo/main.js map section (MIT, LemoLab) — own SVG build, procedural island

bands.doc: ascending thresholds; band k starts at bands[k]

stations.doc: [{x (0-1000), y (0-700), value}] data points; empty = built-in demo field

timeKeys.doc: [[frame, multiplier]] the field is scaled by this multiplier over time

yearFrom.doc: label number at the first time key

yearTo.doc: label number at the last time key

finalLabel.doc: label shown once the morph ends ("" = keep number)

title: Pin drop + clustering map
description: Map pins drop onto a map region, merge into numbered cluster bubbles, split into single pins as the camera zooms in, then merge again.
useFor: Store/user/event locators, "customers worldwide", coverage and density stories, any list of lat/lon points that needs to read as a map with counts.

points.doc: array of {lat, lon, label?}; the camera auto-fits them (labels show when a pin is single and zoomed in)

unit.doc: noun for the big counter (locations, stores, users)

clusterSize.doc: cluster radius in px (1080 scale): bigger merges more

zoom.doc: camera zoom-in factor for the split beat

onAccent.doc: text/dot colour drawn on accent shapes

title: Time rings (dated scan passes)
description: A locked top-down view where soft scan passes sweep down the frame, each swapping in an older or newer dated plate and leaving that date's outline as a thin white ring with a year label; the lost band flashes, a light runs the newest outline, the rest dims, and an amber reading rolls in and lands.
useFor: Before/after-over-time evidence on images: glacier retreat, city sprawl, construction progress, deforestation, a product growing on a map, a photo series of a building site.

title: Mix (layer motions together)

title: Icon draw, fill & glow (heart)
description: On warm sketch paper a pencil draws a red heart outline (or star / check / bolt), the hatched fill fades in, 4-point sparkles twinkle around it and a soft warm glow pulses while it hovers.

drawDur.doc: frames for the outline draw-on (36 measured)

glow.doc: warm glow fades in after the fill

pencil.doc: show the pencil that draws the outline

frame.doc: draw the torn deckle paper frame

title: Hex comb build
description: Cream wax hexagon edges grow segment by segment with node balls and compass-circle previews, cells fill with honey colours, wax caps spiral shut and the comb tilts into extruded prisms.
useFor: Building a system cell by cell, modular growth, teamwork / hive, filling a grid of slots.

cellColors.doc: fill colours picked per cell (honey, pollen...)

rings.doc: rings of cells built around the seed cell (1 = 7 cells, 2 = 19, 3 = 37)

framesPerEdge.doc: frames each wax edge takes to grow (easeOutQuad)

compassPreview.doc: lavender compass circles preview each next cell

caps.doc: fraction of filled cells that get a spiral wax cap

extrude.doc: end by tilting the comb into perspective and extruding prisms

title: Ink brush stroke
description: Sumi brushstrokes paint themselves on rice paper: a wet loaded body with a darker contour side, bristle tracks that break into flying white at the dry tail, soft edge bleed; presets for a decisive swoosh, an underline, an ensō circle and a bamboo sprig, or pass your own paths.
useFor: Hand-made accent strokes, underlines, logo swooshes, dividers; the foundation stroke for any brush or calligraphy look.

strokes.doc: custom strokes: {path [[x,y,pressure]..] in 0..1, width (u), dry 0–0.7, tone 0–1, at, dur, profile brush|tip|even|lens|fan|rise, darkSide -1|0|1, color?} — empty uses the preset

caption.doc: small italic serif line with a vermilion square ("" = none)

background.doc: 'paper' (warm rice paper), any colour, or 'transparent' for an overlay

title: Line-art draw-on
description: Line art constructs itself stroke by stroke with a pen nib riding each tip, then groups of lines recolour to a highlight; defaults to a blueprint building elevation.
useFor: Build any diagram, blueprint, wireframe, icon or logo line by line; highlight the part you are talking about.

paths.doc: SVG path strings in any coordinate space (auto-fitted); empty = built-in blueprint drawing

groups.doc: group index per path (for the highlight recolour)

highlightColor.doc: colour lines recolour to in the highlight pass

highlightGroups.doc: which groups recolour, in order, after everything is drawn

stagger.doc: frames between stroke starts (auto-tightened to fit 60% of the duration)

pen.doc: pen-nib dot on each stroke tip and a "+" flash where a stroke starts

engrave.doc: draw strokes as outlined double lines (video19 engraving)

fillOpacity.doc: highlighted closed shapes get a soft fill of the highlight colour

caption.doc: small mono title block typed after the drawing ("" to hide)

margin.doc: margin around the drawing as a fraction of the frame

medium.doc: stroke style: clean (default) | cable (thick outlined round cables with highlight + connector-cap pop; draws a breadboard demo when no paths) | crayon (wobbly tapered wax lines that keep boiling at boilFps) | fineliner (tapered pen, overshoot + skips)

surface.doc: blueprint (default) | whiteboard | chalkboard | paper — swaps background, ink and highlight colours, grid off

hand.doc: marker | pen | chalk — a hand holding the tool follows the active stroke tip and lifts between strokes (replaces the nib dot)

cables.doc: medium cable: [{from:[x,y], to:[x,y], color?, lift?}] in a 1000x640 space (lift = arc height as a fraction of 640)

wobble.doc: crayon / fineliner: line wobble in px

boilFps.doc: crayon: re-seed rate of the wobble (12 = hand-drawn boil)

taper.doc: crayon / fineliner: how much both stroke ends thin out (0..1)

overshoot.doc: fineliner: px the pen overshoots each stroke end

gapChance.doc: fineliner: 0..1 chance a stroke skips a small gap mid-way

retractAt.doc: frame to start removing the drawing (0 = never): cables split into pieces that shrink to nothing; crayon / fineliner erase from the tail

retractPieces.doc: cable pieces the stroke splits into when retracting

title: Logo reveal: liquid flood
description: Gooey two-colour liquid rises from the bottom edge with droplets lifting off the wavy surface until it floods the frame; a wobbly hole then opens in the middle and spreads out, revealing the logo inside it, followed by a ripple ring and the tagline.
useFor: Playful or organic logo intros and outros (drinks, wellness, kids, creative studios); your logo image or a wordmark.

text.doc: wordmark shown when no src is given (use \n for two lines)

tagline.doc: small tracked line under the logo ("" = none)

src.doc: logo image (public/ path or https URL); empty = wordmark text

background.doc: colour of the revealed frame the logo sits on, or "transparent"

ink.doc: wordmark / tagline colour (pick one that reads on `background`)

droplets.doc: droplets that lift off the surface (0-24)

wobble.doc: edge wobble of the hole (0 = perfect circle, 1 = default, 2 = very jelly)

fontFamily.doc: optional CSS font-family for the wordmark text

title: Metaball heat-map / goo
description: A liquid splat spreads and oozes, rendered as heat-map contour bands (maroon core to mint rim) on a starfield; or gooey dark blobs merge and swell with an RGB-split rim.
useFor: Heat maps, spills, thermal / density imagery, organic growth, liquid transitions, "it spreads".

colors.doc: heatmap: 5 bands rim->core; goo: [blob, rim A, rim B] ([] = source palette)

blur.doc: field softness in u (bigger = smoother, wider bands)

growth.doc: heatmap ooze rate (fraction per second the splat keeps spreading)

hopAt.doc: merge: frame the first puddle hops

hopFrames.doc: merge: frames one ballistic hop takes

leapHeight.doc: merge: leap height as a fraction of the short side

snapFrames.doc: merge: frame offset into the leap where the thread snaps

marble.doc: merge: original colours swirl inside the mass

wobble.doc: merge: wobble amplitude in % after each landing

title: Motif grid pattern (identity backdrop)
description: Brandable identity backdrop: square cells of big discs, half-discs and 14 small geometric motifs in five tones of one hue; whole rows slide against each other, breathe and jump a quarter cell on the beat, with a faint diagonal light sweep. One prop swaps the whole colour.
useFor: Event, sports and launch identity backgrounds, website hero sections, chapter colour cards; low spread under text, high spread for hero cards.

tones.doc: or five explicit tones [t0 darkest … t4 lightest] (overrides hue)

spread.doc: contrast of the pattern against the ground (0.42 under text, 0.95 hero)

cell.doc: cell size in u (180 = six rows at 1080p)

density.doc: share of cells with a small motif

motifs.doc: allow-list of motif kinds: quarter, fish, dots, tri, sunset, arcs, wheel, checker, crescent, swave, gradq, bars, half, ring

bpm.doc: tempo for the quarter-cell beat jumps

beatJump.doc: rows jump a quarter cell on each beat

title: One-line drawing, nib-follow camera
description: A single continuous ink line draws a whole scene with real pen dynamics — thin on fast travels, fat and pooled at slow corners, a soaked bleed, one red accent stretch, a soft pen shadow at the nib — while the camera glides after the drawing point with lag and anticipation and pulls back at the end to reveal the whole picture.
useFor: Minimal brand stories, signature / logo reveals, life-milestone films, "one continuous process" explainers; pass your own polyline for a custom picture.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/one-line (MIT code, CC BY 4.0 docs, LemoLab) — demo/cam.js camAt, ink.js prepare/drawLine, geom.js

paths.doc: JSON array of polylines [[[x,y],…],…] in a 1920×1080 world (smoothed through a spline); empty = built-in sailboat scene

accentRange.doc: accent stretch [from, to] as fractions of total line length

curvatureK.doc: how much sharp turns slow the pen (0 = constant speed)

penShadow.doc: soft shadow wedge at the nib

drawEnd.doc: frame it finishes (0 = auto: duration − reveal)

pool.doc: ink pools where the pen moves slowly

title: Oblique extrude drawing
description: On cyanotype blueprint paper, a flat line elevation draws on in drafting order, then turns into a thick oblique drawing as the depth animates 0 → 0.5 with hidden lines vanishing correctly; parts explode along the depth axis with hand-lettered labels, a dimension and a title block.
useFor: Plan → object reveals without three.js: flat-pack furniture, lamps, circuit boards, product diagrams, patents.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/blueprint demo/draw.js S(), solid() (MIT, LemoLab)

explodeAt.doc: frame parts fly apart along the depth axis (set past the duration to skip)

title: One-line journey
description: A single gold line with a glowing pen tip travels through a chain of figures (seed, plant, building, skyline, wave, ring) as one continuous path; a virtual camera rides the tip zoomed in and pulls back as the drawing grows, older parts dim to ~35 %, the clock breathes on each figure, and the finished drawing relights under a tracked title.
useFor: Luxury, architecture, finance and founder-story films; agents can feed brand-specific path pieces for a one-stroke story.

background.doc: centre colour of the backdrop gradient

lineWidth.doc: line width in screen px at 1080p

drawEnd.doc: clock second the last piece is finished

bank.doc: camera roll (radians) while drawing the wave piece

title.doc: tracked title that appears after the drawing

title: Onion-skin arc (straight ahead vs pose to pose)
description: Two panels compare animation methods: ghost circles drawn frame by frame along a wandering path vs keys, a breakdown and eased in-betweens filling an arc; or (mode drop) a bowling ball, ball and balloon fall the same height in different frame counts.
useFor: Explaining process vs planning, keyframes and in-betweens, timing and weight, any "same task, different approach" comparison.

mode.doc: 'compare' (straight-ahead vs pose-to-pose panels) | 'drop' (three objects, same height, different timing)

inbetweens.doc: number of eased in-between circles on the pose-to-pose arc

dropFrames.doc: drop mode: frames each object takes to fall (heavy, ball, light)

dropLabels.doc: drop mode: labels above the three columns

title: Origami fold sequence (paper crane)
description: A paper sheet in front of a sunny window: crease lines draw on, the sheet folds in snappy 2-3 frame flap rotations (excess strip falls away, pre-creases, diamond, 3/4 tilt, kite and narrowing folds, neck, tail, head) into a crane that flaps its wings; reversible (unfold).
useFor: Making / transformation / "step by step" stories, craft or paper themes, turning a plain idea into something that flies.

showArcGuides.doc: dotted arc guides along flap-corner paths in the 3/4 view

title: Pair field zoom-out
description: Dark violet field of hundreds of cyan+pink dot pairs pinging small rings; the camera pulls out 2.5x from a hero pair.

colors.doc: [dot A, dot B] colours (rings match their dot)

description: A square of red paper folds three times in snappy flaps down to a wedge, scissors trim a scalloped edge and cut saw-tooth bands, crescents, slits and coins out as holes, then the wedge unfolds in three quick snaps into an 8-fold round window flower that blooms with a warm flash, turns slowly and sheds fluttering red scraps.

title: Petal bloom (lotus / radial)
description: Layered petals unfold radially with spring overshoot into a lotus, or dense rings of spike petals sweep round a seed disk into a sunflower / fur ball.

description: A red ball swoops across a blue field trailing five lagging pastel ribbons; when it stops the ribbons whip past and settle hanging with a damped swing (or, style neon, two orbiting dots draw looping neon tube trails).

title: Scissor cut
description: A dashed "cut along the line" guide draws across an image, a pair of scissors travels it snipping five times, then the cut piece separates: it lifts away, flips over or falls, revealing a coloured panel beneath.

title: Shape morph chain
description: A solid flat icon (mug, sun, paper plane, pin, heart, star) morphs into the next through a circle, rotating and stretching on the way; its sub-parts (steam, rays, wing folds, highlights) morph in lockstep through constant-count slots, and the field colour changes with each shape. Any SVG outline can be fed in.

title: Sketch shade-in
description: Everyday objects drawn as bare black ink lines on a book page; an ink sun icon switches on and the shading arrives in a few tenths of a second — white clay fills, pen cross-hatching on the shadow sides and soft cast shadows — then the light drifts so the shadows swing.
