tagline.doc: small line that fades in at the end (empty = none)

gatherAt.doc: frame the beads start gathering into a capsule

burstAt.doc: frame the capsule erupts and morphs into letters

snapAt.doc: frame the first letter bridge snaps (one more every 2 frames)

drip.doc: {letter: index of the letter that drips, at: frame the drip starts forming}

title: Blur-in title card
description: Wide-tracked title whose letters sharpen out of a blur with a random stagger, tagline and rule below, then blur-swap to a second title.
useFor: Documentary title cards, chapter/zone names, place names and calm caption swaps.
avoid: Change title and subtitle (defaults ABYSSES / THE MIDNIGHT ZONE are sample text); set swapTo null for a single card.

title.doc: first title (use caps + wide tracking for the video23 look)

subtitle.default: less than five percent of the ocean has been explored

swapTo.doc: {title, subtitle} to blur-swap to at swapAt, or null for a single card

swapAt.doc: frame the first title starts blurring out

staggerFrames.doc: max random delay per letter (0.45 s = 14 f)

letterFrames.doc: frames each letter takes to sharpen (0.8 s = 24 f)

font.doc: font role: serif | sans | grotesk | display | instrument | mono | rounded …

underline.doc: thin rule under the subtitle that draws left→right and fades at its end

layout.doc: center | upper (video10 sky titles) | lower-left (video23 zone caption)

glow.doc: soft white glow opacity behind letters

backdrop.doc: ocean | ink | dusk | peaks | dunes | warm | none (plain background colour)

src.doc: optional public/ image behind the title

fadeOut.doc: blur-fade everything out over the last 16 frames

material.doc: 'plain' (default) | 'gold' (7-stop banded gold gradient letters; combine with a light backdrop / ink background)

sheenAt.doc: frame the specular band starts crossing the letters (-1 = right after the letters land)

sheenFrames.doc: frames the band takes to cross (~0.6 s)

glint.doc: {t0?, dur?, angle?} a white diagonal glint sweeping across the (plain-colour) letters; null = off. Pair with weight 200 and tracking ~0.5 for a thin launch-film title

kicker.doc: small tracked mono caps line above the title ("" = none)

title: Bouncing-ball singalong
description: Lyrics or a slogan on a period cinema title card: a white ball hops from word to word on the beat along parabolic arcs, squashing as it lands, and every word lights up (outline to solid) the moment the ball touches it.
useFor: Jingles, slogans, safety rhymes, karaoke captions, kids learning content; works over any backdrop motion (set `background` transparent-ish or pass `src`).
source: lemo-opuscar styles/rubber-hose/STYLE.md §8 "bouncing-ball singalong", §4 title cards (MIT / CC BY 4.0, LemoLab); original implementation

lines.doc: lyric lines (replace the sample words)

title.doc: small heading on the card (empty = none)

cues.doc: optional frame of each word touch; empty = one hop per beat from bpm

bpm.doc: beats per minute (one word per beat)

litColor.doc: colour a touched word fills with

background.doc: backdrop colour (period style darkens it to a vignette)

src.doc: optional backdrop image (public path), shown dimmed behind the card

exit.doc: ball hops off the card after the last word

title: Bulb marquee sign
description: Any word becomes a theatre marquee of evenly spaced warm bulbs on gold channel letters; letters ignite one per beat with a flash overshoot, then a chase runs across the sign and a tracked gold subtitle rises.
useFor: Counted reveals (countdowns, launch names, award winners), premiere / Vegas / theatre titles, event openers.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/art-deco demo/engine/bulbs.js bulb render + litSequence (MIT, LemoLab)

text.doc: word(s) to spell in bulbs (A–Z, 0–9, ! ? - . & and spaces; keep it short, ≤ 10 letters)

subtitle.doc: tracked gold caps under the sign (empty = none)

chaseGap.doc: frames after the last letter before the chase starts

spacing.doc: bulb spacing along the strokes in cap-height/6 units (smaller = more bulbs)

channelColor.doc: enamel colour inside the gold channel letters

rays.doc: faint gold sunburst behind the sign

title: Carved plaque (shadow-theatre title)
description: A dark hide plaque with the title cut out so the letters glow with the lamp light behind; carved border with a meander band and cloud-scroll corner roundels, a vermilion seal with a cut glyph, carried on two thin rods, pressed on to enter and lifted off to exit.
useFor: Titles, end cards and chapter cards for heritage, myths and festivals (Lunar New Year, Diwali shadow plays), "a tale of ..." openers; works over lamp-screen or any bright backdrop.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/shadow-puppet demo/stage.js (plaque), DEMO.md "Title plaque" (MIT, LemoLab)

default.text: a shadow play in three acts

lines.doc: title lines [{text, font (cormorant|playfair|bungee|oldItalic|gothic|...), size, weight}]

seal.doc: single glyph cut into the seal

exitAt.doc: frame the plaque lifts off (-1 = stays)

backdrop.doc: 'lamp' (lit cloth behind) or 'color'

title: Channel intro sting (3 s)
description: A 3-second bumper: five flat shapes snap in on the beat, spin and collapse to a point with a flash; a colour band shoots across and the channel name slams in letter by letter, a tagline pill slides in under it, then everything wipes out.
useFor: Channel / show intro bumpers, section stingers and "from the makers of" openers; optional logo picture above the name.

name.doc: channel / show name that slams in

tagline.doc: small pill under the name ("" = none)

src.doc: optional logo picture shown above the name (public/ path or URL)

background.doc: backdrop colour, or "transparent" to sit over footage

ink.doc: name colour (must read on the accent band)

speed.doc: timing multiplier (1.3 = faster, hits a shorter beat)

fontFamily.doc: optional CSS font-family for the name

title: Chapter countdown (3-2-1 ring)
description: A tick-marked ring counts 3-2-1: each number pops in and the ring sweeps once per count while the ticks light up; the ring then snaps shut into a line that opens sideways, with the chapter label, title and subtitle rising out from behind it.
useFor: Chapter / section intros in tutorials, courses and long videos; "starting in 3-2-1" openers before a segment, with the chapter title.

preLabel.doc: small line under the ring while counting ("" = none)

chapterLabel.doc: small tracked label above the title (e.g. "Chapter 02", "Part 3")

subtitle.default: Set up your workspace in five minutes

background.doc: backdrop colour, or "transparent" to sit over footage

accent.doc: ring, ticks, label and line colour

fontFamily.doc: optional CSS font-family for the number and title

title: Chapter header
description: Numbered chapter/stage header that steps through titles: tracked title + segmented progress bar, era badge card, or vertical location tag.
useFor: Step-by-step explainers, timelines, era/location markers and chapter breaks.

variant.doc: stage (video8 top-left block) | era (video14 top-right year card) | location (video10 vertical tag) | fight-banner (tilted dark band snapping across the frame, heavy italic gold word + sub-line; title = word, subtitle = sub) | fantasy (radial navy card, CHAPTER I capitals over a gold diamond ornament, glowing italic serif name, drifting ember; title = name, subtitle = chapter label)

stages.doc: [{title, subtitle}] stepped through in order; [] = built-in sample for the variant

startIndex.doc: stage: number shown for the first stage

total.doc: stage: total count shown after the slash (progress dashes = total + 1)

scale.doc: overall size multiplier (1 = source size at 1080p)

backdrop.doc: auto (dunes / warm / dusk per variant) | any backdrop kind

src.doc: optional public/ image behind the header

goldColor.doc: fight-banner / fantasy: gold rules, word and ornament colour

title: Chrome 80s title
description: Heavy italic title in a sky-to-sunset chrome gradient with a white horizon line, dark outline plus neon outline glowing through; flickers on, a light bar sweeps the letters, a star glint pops, katakana line above, red year below.
useFor: Synthwave / retro / 80s anime title cards, YouTube intros and game or film trailers.

title.doc: main title (caps recommended; wraps to two lines at 9:16)

tagline.doc: small tracked caps line under the year

flicker.doc: flicker on at 12 fps with a 2-frame white flash

title: Chrome title slam
description: An extruded 80s chrome logotype slams in from huge scale, flashes the frame white and shakes: sky-to-sunset split face with a bright horizon line, dark outline, neon edge, stacked purple extrusion, bevel slivers and reflection lines; then a diagonal glint sweeps across and a four-point star pops.
useFor: Retro title cards, gaming / esports intros, event posters and Y2K chrome brand moments; the extruded, slammed cousin of `chrome-80s-title`.

text.doc: the logotype (short, caps)

subtitle.doc: small letter-spaced line under it (empty = none)

skyColors.doc: face gradient stops, top to the horizon line (2-4 hex colours)

sunColors.doc: face gradient stops, below the horizon line

rimColor.doc: colour of the bright rim stroke

extrudeColor.doc: extrusion colour at the face; it darkens with depth

slamAt.doc: frame the title starts slamming in

glintAt.doc: frame the diagonal glint starts (0.6 s sweep)

starGlint.doc: pop a four-point star + streak at the end of the sweep

title: Cinematic title card
description: Letterbox bars slide in over a slowly pushing backdrop (your picture or a graded gradient with a drifting light leak); floating dust catches the light, a small kicker appears, a wide-tracked serif title resolves from blur as its tracking tightens, a thin rule and subtitle follow, and the card fades to black.
useFor: Film and documentary titles, trailers, "a film by" cards, episode titles and any moody opening over a photo or colour.

kicker.doc: tiny tracked line above the title, e.g. "a film by" ("" = none)

src.doc: backdrop picture (public/ path or URL); empty = graded gradient with light leak

background.doc: base colour (the gradient shade / picture tint); "transparent" = bars and text only over your footage

ratio.doc: letterbox aspect ratio (2.39 = scope, 1.85 = flat); bars are capped at 27 % of the height

push.doc: slow push-in over the whole card (0.08 = 8 %)

tracking.doc: final letter spacing of the title in em

startAt.doc: frame the bars start closing in

fadeOut.doc: fade to black over the last 20 frames

fontFamily.doc: optional CSS font-family for the title

title: Comic SFX burst
description: Comic onomatopoeia (BONK! POP!) in a jagged halftone starburst that springs in after an impact frame, wobbles and boils, with speed lines and a shockwave ring.
useFor: Impacts, punchlines, notifications and any "sound you can see" beat.

bursts.doc: [{text, at, x, y, palette?, rotate?, size?, impact?, life?}] — palette pink | yellow | white | cyan | green; impact = 3-frame yellow smash frame before it; life = frames until it pops away

speedLines.doc: radial speed lines whip in on each burst

shockwave.doc: ground shockwave ellipse under each burst

outline.doc: ink colour for outlines and shadows

backdrop.doc: comic | dusk | warm | … procedural scene behind

src.doc: optional public/ image as the scene

variant.doc: burst (starburst + onomatopoeia) | telop (huge outlined verdict word pops at an angle, drifts up, with a star + ring + speed-line burst)

angle.doc: telop: default tilt in degrees (a burst rotate overrides it)

strokeRatio.doc: telop: ink outline width as a share of the font size

tagCorner.doc: telop: after the hold the word shrinks into a small tag in the top-left corner and stays

skewDeg.doc: telop: horizontal skew of the word

title: Art deco title bar
description: An art-deco title card unfolding from a centre point: hairline → stepped lacquer bar with double gold keyline → title rises in Limelight gold → wings with speed lines, over a stepped arch and a 72-ray sunburst, with a diamond year badge and a specular sheen across the gold.
useFor: Openers and end cards for galas, launches, 1920s themes, hotel / luxury brands and New Year countdowns.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/art-deco demo/engine/type.js titleBar, yearBadge; engine/deco.js goldGrad, gline, sunburst, archFrame (MIT, LemoLab)

title.doc: main title (set in Limelight caps; long titles shrink to fit the bar)

subtitle.doc: tracked caps line under the bar

badge.doc: text in the diamond badge, split in two halves (e.g. "2026" → 20 / 26)

caption.doc: thin tracked caps line under the badge (empty = none)

rays.doc: sunburst ray count (alternate wedges are drawn)

steps.doc: stepped arch frames drawn above the bar

accent.doc: burgundy jewel accent at the bar ends

sheenAt.doc: frame the specular sheen sweeps across the gold

title: Definition card
description: A dictionary entry card: big headword with a speaker icon, phonetic spelling and part-of-speech pill, a rule that draws, the definition typing on with a caret, then an italic example sentence.
useFor: Vocabulary and "what does X mean" explainers, glossary beats, language lessons, jargon-busting intros — pass the word, phonetic, part of speech, definition and example.

partOfSpeech.doc: noun / verb / adjective ... shown as a pill

definition.default: A general rise in prices over time, which means each unit of money buys a little less than it did before.

example.default: With inflation at 3%, a $100 basket of groceries costs $103 next year.
example.doc: optional example sentence (empty string hides it)

accent.doc: pill, rule, caret and left-edge colour

fontFamily.doc: optional CSS font-family for the word and example (empty = serif)

typeSpeed.doc: typing speed multiplier for the definition

title: Diagonal assemble title (shatter into title)
description: The previous scene slices into 23 strips along a 30-degree cut that slide off alternately; the title letters then fly in along the same diagonal from alternating sides, spinning and landing one per sixteenth note, the title sitting split along the cut until the halves close with a click.
useFor: Logo and name reveals ("the chase ends at the brand"), event openers, trailers: an assemble-the-title finale with real graphic punch.

title.doc: title lines (one or two short lines)

cutAngle.doc: cut line angle from vertical, degrees

strips.doc: number of strips the outgoing scene is cut into

splitGap.doc: gap between the two title halves in u

closeAt.doc: frame the halves close with a click

scene.doc: show the outgoing scene (false = start straight on the title)

title: Diagonal band title
description: Constructivist title package on warm paper: an archive-footage window slams down, a red girder band slams in along a −18° axis with a decaying shake, a huge Oswald number stamps digit by digit (one per eighth note) with its unit in red, and a caps line rides on the band; everything printed in one ink, one red.
useFor: Bold documentary, anniversary and report openers; launch numbers with real photos (pass src).
source: lemo-opuscar styles/kino-montage (MIT, LemoLab) — STYLE.md §6 title package, poster.jpg, index.html slam/slant

number.doc: the huge number (stamped digit by digit)

unit.doc: unit word in red beside it

line.default: Northwind Tower · built floor by floor
line.doc: caps line riding on the red band

tag.doc: Space Mono source tag on the footage window

src.doc: optional photo/still in public/ for the footage window (print-graded to ink/paper)

footage.doc: procedural archive scene when no src: 'tower' | 'girder' | 'crowd' | 'street' | 'works'

bpm.doc: beat grid: digits land on eighth notes

title: End card credits
description: Bottom scrim fades in over a drifting landscape; headline, mono stat lines and a credit stagger in with a blur fade-up, then fade to black.
useFor: Closing cards, "how it was made" stats, credits and calls to action over the last shot.

title.doc: optional wide-tracked serif title shown above the headline ("" = none)

headline.default: every pixel you just saw is math.

default: 0 images · 0 footage · 0 video models · 0 audio samples
terrain · erosion · light · sky · clouds · lens · music — 1,135 lines of code
lines.doc: mono stat lines (first at 85 % white, the rest 55 %)

offsets.doc: seconds after the headline for each stat line and the credit (video8: 0.55, 1.2, 2.0)

headlineY.doc: vertical centre of the text block as a fraction of height

fadeToBlack.doc: fade to black over the last 11 frames

backdrop.doc: peaks (sunrise over mountains) | dunes | dusk | ocean | … scene behind

src.doc: optional public/ image or still of your last shot

layout.doc: stack (headline block over a bottom scrim) | storybook (calm: serif title blurs in at the top over a slow pull-back, CTA low in the frame)

ctaAt.doc: frame the CTA pops in (0 = visible from the first frame)

pullBack.doc: slow pull-back (≈3 %/s) with a slight truck right instead of the drift-in

title: End screen with video cards
description: Outro screen: headline, two video-card slots (thumbnail or placeholder, label, running timer bar) and a round subscribe circle with a rotating ring of text and pulsing halos; everything rises in staggered, then a supporting line fades in. Lays out 3-across on 16:9 and stacks on 1:1 and 9:16.
useFor: YouTube / social end screens, "watch next" outros and channel sign-offs; keep the card areas for the platform end-screen elements.

subtitle.doc: supporting line at the bottom ("" = none)

cards.doc: [{label, src}] up to 2 video cards; src = thumbnail image (public/ path or URL), empty = placeholder

circleLabel.doc: text inside the circle when no circleSrc is given

circleSrc.doc: channel avatar / logo picture for the circle

ringText.doc: text that rotates around the circle (repeat it to fill the ring)

background.doc: backdrop colour, or "transparent" to place over footage

accent.doc: brand colour of the circle, halos and timer bars

timerBars.doc: show the running timer bar along the bottom of each card

fontFamily.doc: optional CSS font-family for all text

title: Flipbook riffle outro
description: A hand-drawn end card (scalloped red title plate, flame mascot, sparkles) pulls back in three drawings to become the top sheet of an animation-paper stack on a peg bar on a desk; a red pencil writes and circles the drawing count, a cartoon thumb lifts the corner and riffles back through earlier drawings on ones, then settles on the top sheet and the mascot winks.
useFor: A memorable "it was all hand-made" signature ending for studio reels, behind-the-scenes, craft and handmade brands.
source: mg-styles-15 05-cel-boil 9.0-9.7 s, scene.js drawDesk / drawThumb / RIFFLE (MIT, Vincentwei1021) — technique after mg-styles-15

subtitle.doc: small caps line inside the plate

tagline.default: drawn one sheet at a time

countLabel.doc: red-pencil drawing count that gets circled

sceneLabel.doc: slate text top-left of every sheet

src.doc: optional image (public/ path or URL) shown in place of the title plate

pegBar.doc: draw the peg bar, peg holes and tape

riffleCount.doc: earlier drawings flashed during the riffle (2–8, one per frame)

showFlame.doc: flame mascot peeking over the plate

title: Follower milestone
description: A counter climbs to a milestone while a progress bar fills and little hearts float up; it lands with a shockwave, rays and a confetti burst, then a thank-you line pops in word by word.
useFor: Follower / subscriber / download / sales milestones, community thank-you posts, anniversary and goal-reached celebrations, "we hit 100K" announcements.

value.doc: the milestone the counter climbs to

label.doc: unit under the number (followers, subscribers, users…)

caption.doc: small line above the number

thankYou.doc: big thank-you line that pops in after the burst

subtitle.default: We could not have done it without you

climbFrames.doc: frames the counter takes to climb

floaters.doc: floating hearts / plus marks during the climb

background.doc: frame colour, or "transparent" to overlay content

accent.doc: number glow, bar and burst colour

title: Glyph fractal push
description: A big word on a phosphor terminal holds, then the camera pushes on an exponential curve into one glyph until you see it is made of lines of smaller text (names, logs, headlines); outside the glyph the text is barely visible.
useFor: Scale reveals for text-heavy stories: "a company made of its people", "a year made of headlines", "a model made of a million lines".
source: lemo-opuscar styles/ascii-crt demo/main.js fractal section, term.js thin bitmaps (MIT, LemoLab)

word.doc: the big word (A–Z, 0–9; 2–6 letters reads best)

target.doc: index of the letter the camera pushes into

innerText.doc: strings that make up the small text (names, log lines, headlines); empty = 24 neutral placeholder names

holdFrames.doc: frames the whole word holds before the push

zoomTo.doc: final zoom (the small text reads at ≈ 30 px at the end)

title: Glyph-orbit logo build
description: Glyphs fly in and orbit a ring, then resolve into a typed mono logotype (scrambled letter fragments, blue dot becomes the i tittle); a frame draws around it and tagline lines type below.
useFor: Logo reveals, brand end cards, product names and title lock-ups.
avoid: Change logo / tagline / pill (defaults are sample text).

logo.doc: logotype text (monospaced; the first lowercase i/j gets the blue dot)

tagline.doc: up to two lines typed under the logo: [small tracked line, bold line]

pill.doc: double-ruled label typed at the bottom ("" = none)

orbitRadius.doc: glyph orbit radius in px at 1080p

framesPerChar.doc: logotype typing speed (frames per letter; each letter scrambles for 3 frames)

backdrop.doc: ink (blueprint black) | any backdrop kind

variant.doc: orbit (typed with jumble) | fly (wordmark-fly-assemble: letters fly out of the hero point one after another, motion-blurred, and settle into the wordmark)

travel.doc: fly: frames each letter takes to travel (0.42 s = 12)

paletteDashes.doc: fly: colours of short dashes that line up under the logo as a palette signature (e.g. ['#FF5A4A','#FFC24A','#3FB6C8'])

dotColor.doc: colour of the focus / tittle dot ('' = accent)

title: Halftone exhibit numeral
description: A giant rounded numeral bleeds off the right edge in flat yellow overprinted with an orange Ben-Day halftone clipped to the glyph, rising in with a back-ease behind a boiling evidence tag, while a misregistered slab headline drops letter by letter and a navy caption pill pops — all on mottled archive paper.

source: lemo-opuscar styles/halftone-dossier (MIT, LemoLab) — demo/index.html halftone(), radial(), charge-card scene, caption, boil filter

headline.doc: slab headline with misregistered shadow (letters drop in)

tag.doc: navy pill under the case number

caption.default: Left the oven on 17 times this year.
caption.doc: caption pill text (empty = none)

keyword.doc: part of the caption shown in yellow

numeralColor.doc: flat spot ink of the numeral (yellow / pale pink)

dotColor.doc: halftone overprint colour inside the numeral

shadowColor.doc: misregistration shadow colour of the headline

src.doc: optional public/ image shown as the exhibit (boiling evidence tag otherwise)

exhibitLabel.doc: small caps label above the numeral on the card

title: Hanazi caption
description: A fat rounded variety-show caption made of five stacked layers (offset extrusion, coloured outer stroke, white stroke, gradient fill, top gloss) pops in character by character on a damped spring with a slight drop and rotation, then wiggles, bobs and breathes before popping out; a small handwritten aside and sparkles ride along.
useFor: Social packaging (Douyin / Bilibili / Reels / TikTok), vlogs, interviews and reaction moments: drop emotional captions on top of footage.
source: mg-styles-15 demos/18-hanazi HZ, charXf, driveHZ, spring (MIT)

text.doc: the caption (Latin or CJK)

preset.doc: joy | shock | aside | question | bye: colours, font and skew

aside.doc: small handwritten line under it (empty = none)

src.doc: optional photo/video frame (public/) to caption over; empty = demo sky

background.doc: backdrop colour behind the demo sky

title: Handwrite-on title
description: Text written glyph by glyph with a pen: outline strokes on, ink fill follows; optional fast un-write.
useFor: Friendly titles, end cards, chapter interstitials and handwritten captions.

lines.doc: array of {text, color?, size?, delay?} — each line written after the previous

unwriteAt.doc: frame to start erasing backwards at 2x speed (0 = never)

title: Intertitle card (silent-film)
description: A full-frame black painted silent-film card with an Art-Deco border whose ornament follows the emotion (narration, shout, tender, title), set in small-caps and italic serifs, with weave, flicker, scratches, dust and a hair of print damage.

ping.doc: cyan floor ping at the end

accent2.doc: marker colour for every second highlight

title: Kinetic word captions

framesPerLine.doc: frames each line stays on screen

background.doc: scene colour; "transparent" = caption overlay on top of other motions

variant.doc: kinetic (word pop + highlight boxes) | premium (calm line, words brighten as spoken, soft scrim) | slam (huge left-aligned chunks split by |, {keyword} on a colour block, optional secondLines) | toast (UI notification pill with live dot) | frosted-bar (blurred glass slab + accent line) | terminal (LOG tag, > prompt, words typed with the voice) | print (glyph-drop headline with offset overprint shadow) | karaoke (outline words fill as sung) | rise (calm per-word fade + rise)

accent.doc: premium/toast/terminal/karaoke: accent colour (starred words, dot, tag, current word)

title: Kinetic type slam (phrases)
description: Huge 2-4 word phrases land one word per beat: each word rises through its own mask with a 1.25→1 (or 0.6→1) scale punch, they stack (or justify full-width, or swap in place), one accent word takes the brand colour, then the whole line is shoved off the top by the next phrase while the camera creeps in.
useFor: Hooks for shorts, launch films, manifestos and title sequences: pass `lines` (accent word per line), pick `layout`, set `beatFrames` to your music grid.

lines.doc: [{text, accent?: word or index, at?: start frame}] — 2-4 words each

layout.doc: 'stack' words stacked at one size · 'fill' each word justified to full width · 'center' one word at a time

beatFrames.doc: frames per word (6-15; match your beat grid)

holdBeats.doc: beats a finished line holds before being pushed off

capHeight.doc: cap height of the biggest word as a fraction of frame height (0.25-0.45)

entryScale.doc: start scale of even words (1.25 punch-in); odd words use ≤0.6 pop-up

push.doc: camera push-in over the whole clip (0.06 = +6 %)

title: Knife cut (strike a row out)
description: A thin red rule shoots across a list row in three frames, then the row collapses vertically to its own midline and is gone; the rows below re-flow into the freed space nearest first and the running total counts down. Precise Swiss deletion.
useFor: Removing text, bullets, prices or features with a precise non-fade beat: "budget cut", quote tidy-ups, feature trimming; pairs with kinetic captions.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/swiss-motion demo/film.js drawPosterText cut (MIT / CC BY 4.0, LemoLab)

items.doc: rows: label + numeric amount

cuts.doc: indexes of the rows to strike out

cutAt.doc: frame each cut line lands (one per cut)

lineFrames.doc: frames the rule takes to cross

title: Letters become image
description: A typed sentence on a phosphor terminal breaks apart: its letters fly as particles into the cells of a picture made only of those letters, landing bottom-to-top with a flash on each landing while the source letters dim.
useFor: Text-to-image climaxes: a manifesto becomes a city, a product name becomes the product, a recipe becomes the dish.
source: lemo-opuscar styles/ascii-crt demo/main.js letter-fall block + term.js (MIT, LemoLab)

sentence.default: Every city is made of small lights
sentence.doc: the typed sentence; the picture is built only from its letters

src.doc: public/ image to build (empty = procedural night plate)

splitAt.doc: frame the sentence breaks apart (≈1.5 s after typing ends)

spreadFrames.doc: frames from the first landing row to the last

order.doc: bottomUp = ground lands first, random = scattered

title: Logo assemble (wireframe, shards lock in)
description: The logo draws on as a triangle wireframe, then faceted shards fly in from depth (or scatter) with a stagger, overshoot about 2 % and lock into place; a soft thud (camera punch, glow and ring) and a diagonal light sweep follow, then a tracked tagline. Works from a word or from an image / SVG logo.
useFor: Logo stings, brand intros and end cards; set text to the brand name or src to a logo file.
source: prompt-corpus research: logo-assemble (12 cases, ideas only; original implementation)

src.doc: public/ path or URL of a logo image / SVG (overrides text)

logoAspect.doc: width / height of the src logo

fontRole.doc: font role for the text logo: sans | display | grotesk | serif | mono

weight.doc: font weight for the text logo

tagline.doc: tracked line under the logo ("" = none)

origin.doc: 'depth' (fly from the camera side) | 'scatter' (fly in from all around)

title: Logo reveal: sweeping lines
description: Fine rules sweep in from alternating sides across the frame, converge on the logo box (outer rules become top and bottom rule, the rest merge into a bright centre line), the logo opens out of that line with a sheen and the tagline tracks in.

text.doc: wordmark shown when no src is given (use \n for two lines)

tagline.doc: small tracked line under the logo ("" = none)

src.doc: logo image (public/ path or https URL, transparent PNG/SVG best); empty = wordmark text

lines.doc: how many sweeping rules (3-24)

background.doc: backdrop colour, or "transparent" to sit over other footage

accent.doc: brand colour of the main rules and ticks

fontFamily.doc: optional CSS font-family for the wordmark text

exit.doc: fade everything out over the last 14 frames

title: Marquee ticker
description: Endless horizontal bands of big uppercase text (solid, outline or pill-logo style) scrolling seamlessly with star/dot/arrow separators — one band, or several tilted and crossing in opposite directions — wiping in staggered.
useFor: Hype reels, event promos, client-logo walls (pill style), website section dividers, "now playing" bars; replace the items with your own words.

bands.doc: [{items[], speed(px/s at 1080), direction(1 right|-1 left), tilt(deg), bg, ink, style(solid|outline|pill), offsetY(-0.5..0.5 of frame height), height?}]

stagger.doc: frames between each band wiping in

title: Mask-rise title
description: Editorial title whose letters rise out of baseline masks with motion blur; chapter variant rolls a red italic numeral and types a subtitle, stack variant builds an end-card headline.

avoid: Change chapter / lines / sideCopy / sideMono (defaults like STAGING, 12 PRINCIPLES are sample text).

chapter.doc: {number, title, kicker?, subtitle?} shown (after the swap if fromChapter is set)

text.doc: variants water / numeral / vertical / breathing: the headline ('' = a built-in sample word per variant)

eyebrow.doc: breathing: mono eyebrow typed above the headline behind a block cursor

sideLine.doc: vertical: small tracked caps line running alongside the vertical word

dotColor.doc: breathing: accent dot colour (also its rings and the rule tick)

breathPeriod.doc: breathing: seconds per breath (dot swells, ring emitted)

steps.doc: numeral: number of eased climb steps

exitAt.doc: water / numeral / vertical / breathing: frame to exit (0 = the last 12 frames when exit is true)

font.doc: water / numeral / vertical / breathing: display | sans | serif | instrument | rounded | grotesk

title: Myth vs fact
description: A MYTH card drops in, a red FALSE stamp slams across it and shakes the card, then the card flips in 3D to a FACT card with a green tick.

myth.default: We only use 10% of our brains.

fact.default: Brain scans show that nearly every region is active over the course of a day.

stampText.doc: word stamped across the myth (FALSE, BUSTED, WRONG...)

factStamp.doc: small caption at the bottom of the fact card

fontFamily.doc: optional CSS font-family for the statements (empty = grotesk)

startAt.doc: frame the card starts dropping in

hold.doc: frames the myth is read before the stamp lands

title: Neon sign ignite
description: Dark plum plate on a brick wall; rounded neon lettering strikes on letter by letter with flicker, then hums, with one faulty letter stuttering and glow spilling onto the wall.
useFor: Shop/venue names, nightlife or retro beats, "open" moments and glowing titles.
avoid: Change lines (default NOODLES / open late is sample text).

igniteSpread.doc: frames over which the letters strike in random order

noPlate.doc: script: transparent background so the neon floats over another scene

title: News strap (broadcast lower third)
description: Persistent broadcast lower third: lemon category tab on a paper strap with a lemon left bar, ink headline + olive caps sub-line, ink end block with the channel name, offset drop shadow and a mono source line; content changes flip vertically and the tab flashes on a new category. Overlay-capable (backdrop "none").

disclaimer.doc: small caps disclaimer under the strap

title: Newsreel ident (searchlights & globe)
description: Late-1920s newsreel opener: searchlight beams snap on with a flash and sweep from the bottom corners, a 36-wedge sunburst turns slowly, a shaded wireframe globe grows and spins, the channel name lands in Art-Deco silver lettering with a big overshoot over a spaced subtitle, and an iris closes on the globe.

title: Number counter
description: Huge thin-mono counter that ticks or odometer-rolls through dwell keyframes, with unit, label and derived readouts (pressure, light, temperature, percent).
useFor: Depth/altitude/speed meters, growing stats, countdowns, progress percentages and scoreboards.

decimals.doc: decimal places (tick mode; roll mode uses integers)

backdrop.doc: ocean | ink | dunes | … scene behind

rollDuration.doc: block hook: seconds of the scale slam

title: Paper strip title (scroll unroll + seal)
description: Vertical columns of brush calligraphy on cut gold-paper strips unroll from their anchor edge one per beat — the strip is uncovered, glyphs never squash — each casting a soft shadow, then a small red seal stamps beside the last column; a horizontal serif mode unrolls lines the same way.

title: Pixel logo drop
description: A chunky gold pixel-glyph logo falls with gravity, lands on a white flash frame, squashes and rebounds in 2-frame steps with a screen shake, puffs dithered dust and sparks, gets a diagonal shine sweep and corner glints; a red ribbon unfolds under it, types a subtitle and PRESS START blinks.

pressStart.doc: blinking line at the bottom (empty = none)

seed.doc: seed for stars, dust and sparks

description: A QUIZ tag and question, lettered option cards dealing in, a draining timer ring with a countdown, then the correct option lights up with a tick and a pulse while the rest dim.

timerSeconds.doc: length of the countdown ring in seconds

accent2.doc: colour of the timer in its last third

title: Ransom-note type
description: Each letter sits on its own scrap of paper (newsprint, red, black, white) with a different typeface, slightly rotated and jittered, slapped onto kraft one by one; then a diagonal black band with condensed caps, a torn masthead strip and a speech scrap slap in.

title: Rolling credits

openWideFrames.doc: frame the camera starts moving in from the wide establishing view

title: Type marquee field
description: A heavy grotesk word rises letter by letter from a baseline mask (a red dot replaces one letter), then outline and solid rows of the word fill the frame, marquee-scrolling in alternating directions while the whole field rolls ≈ −8° and pushes in.
useFor: Kinetic-type backgrounds for a brand word, poster-style title cards, a "type" chapter in a principles reel.

word.doc: the hero word (repeated in every row)

dotLetter.doc: letter replaced by the accent dot (first occurrence; empty = none)

font.doc: display (Archivo Black) | sans (Inter ExtraBold) | grotesk (Space Grotesk Bold)

outlineEvery.doc: rows alternate outline/solid with this period (1 = all outline, 0 = all solid)

speed.doc: marquee speed in frame widths per second (alternating direction per row)

roll.doc: final roll of the field in degrees

push.doc: final push-in scale

rowsAt.doc: frame the rows start fading in (roll/push follow)

hud.doc: show the reel HUD (crop marks, label, timecode, segment bar)

title: Typewriter code window
description: macOS-style code editor or terminal window that types syntax-coloured code with a block cursor; the panel grows upward line by line.
useFor: Show the code behind a visual, a command being run, or a "made with code" credit beat.

lines.doc: code lines (strings, or {text, color}); in terminal mode "$ " lines type, other lines are output

mode.doc: editor (line numbers, syntax colours) | terminal (bold, prompt/output colours)

title.doc: filename centred in the title bar

charsPerSecond.doc: typing speed (video17 ≈ 30, video8 time-boxes ≈ 150 chars in 1 s)

startFrame.doc: frame the first character types (panel fades in 6 frames before)

outputDelay.doc: terminal: frames between a command finishing and its output appearing

colors.doc: override any of keyword, fn, number, string, comment, text, prompt, command, ok, warn, error, lineNo

panelColor.doc: window body colour (empty = grey for editor, plum for terminal)

backdrop.doc: auto | dunes | warm | ink | cream | peaks | dusk | ocean | none — procedural scene behind the panel

src.doc: optional public/ image behind the panel (overrides backdrop)

theme.doc: dark | paper (light editor card, teal accents)

highlightLines.doc: code-run-sync: 0-based lines a pale teal band steps through after typing ends, e.g. [4,5,6,7]

highlightEvery.doc: frames the band rests on each line

consoleLines.doc: serial-monitor / console pane below the code, lines appended one by one while it runs; the play button turns into a red stop

runAt.doc: frame the Run is pressed (-1 = shortly after typing ends)

chips.doc: numeric literals on small rounded chips

title: Typewriter signature
description: Small lowercase credit typed into a corner two frames per character, no cursor; optional glyph-scramble dissolve out.
useFor: Sign-offs, maker credits, version tags and quiet end stamps.

text.doc: the credit text

framesPerChar.doc: frames per typing step (2 = video6; video1 uses 2 with charsPerStep 2)

wordPause.doc: extra frames held after the first word

scrambleAt.doc: frame the scramble-out starts (0 = 14 frames before the end)

decor.doc: draw a faint flower-of-life construction behind the credit

mode.doc: type (typed on) | decode (random symbols resolve into the real letters, then break back into symbols)

decodeFrames.doc: decode: frames the resolve takes (≈20 ms per char in the source)

reseedEvery.doc: decode: frames between re-randomising unresolved glyphs

pool.doc: decode: glyph pool (empty = brackets, symbols, letters)

direction.doc: decode: ltr | center-out | random resolve order

decodeOut.doc: decode: frames the break-back-to-symbols exit takes at scrambleAt (0 = no decode exit)

title: Bokeh drift
description: Soft depth-of-field light discs in three depth bands drifting through the frame with a gentle twinkle; circle or hexagon bokeh.
useFor: Dreamy or festive backgrounds behind titles, night-city and party moods, wedding / event / luxury intros; overlay on footage with a transparent background.

direction.doc: drift direction in degrees (0 = right, 90 = up, 180 = left)

speed.doc: drift distance over the clip (loops by wrap-around)

softness.doc: blur of the discs in u (higher = more defocused)

ring.doc: bright rim on each disc (0 = flat disc, 1 = strong lens ring)

title: Hide-carve patterns (openwork library)
description: The openwork vocabulary of shadow theatre on lit cloth: crescent fish-scale holes, diamond lattice, coin holes, cloud scrolls, meander bands, bead lines, tapered rain slits and leaf holes, each hide piece pressed on and cut by a sweeping knife.
useFor: Makes generated silhouettes (animals, buildings, logos) read as crafted lace instead of clip-art; the carve.* path generators (scales, lattice, coins, cloud, meander, taper, beads) in r2-lb2-kit are reusable for papercut and folk looks.

startAt.doc: frame the first piece presses on

title: Light-leak wash
description: Analogue film light leaks: hot colour blobs bleed in from the frame edges, swell, drift and fall away, screen-blended.
useFor: Warm nostalgic transitions and accents over footage or photos, wedding / travel / memory edits, title cards that need an analogue glow; use transparent background as an overlay.

colors.doc: leak colours (cycled per leak; first of each pair is the body, the next the hot core)

leakAt.doc: start frames of each leak (empty = spaced evenly)

leakFrames.doc: life of each leak in frames

softness.doc: blur of the blobs in u

streak.doc: thin light streak that rides each leak

title: Pattern scroll
description: Seamless tiling geometric background (dots, lines, checks, waves, diamonds, plus) scrolling in any direction, loop-perfect.
useFor: Brandable looping backgrounds behind titles, lower thirds, slides and web sections; retro / Memphis / editorial wallpaper; set background transparent for a pattern overlay.

pattern.doc: dots | lines | checks | waves | diamonds | plus

angle.doc: rotation of the whole pattern, degrees (also sets scroll direction)

speed.doc: cells per second along the pattern x axis; whole number of cells per clip loops seamlessly

alternate.doc: every second row scrolls the opposite way

thickness.doc: mark size / stroke weight (fraction of a cell)

accentEvery.doc: every Nth tile uses the accent colour (0 = none)

pulse.doc: size breathing wave across the pattern (0 = none)

fade.doc: fade the pattern out towards the edges (0..1)

title: Match cut (shape continues)
description: A record button in an app screen becomes a sun in a sunrise scene at exactly the same position and size: the shape is held 3 frames across the cut (scaled 1 -> 1.6 first), then scene B opens through a clip-path that grows from that shape to the full frame while the sun drifts to its rest position.
useFor: Premium launch films, showreels and one-shot explainers: copy the rect/clip-path maths into any scene change so a button, screen or circle continues as a shape in the next scene (pairs with cursor-driver and ui-shape-morph).

from.doc: matched shape in scene A: {x,y in % of frame centre, w,h in u}

to.doc: where the shape comes to rest in scene B

holdFrames.doc: frames the matched shape is held across the cut (2-4)

expandFrames.doc: frames for B to open to full frame

scaleThrough.doc: scale of the matched shape just before the cut (1 = none)

imageB.doc: optional public image path for scene B (replaces the procedural sunrise)

title: Transition reel
description: Every scene transition in the library, one after another, between contrasting labelled colour panels.
useFor: Previewing and choosing transitions; each panel names the transition (and variant) that revealed it.

types.doc: transition entries to show in order, "type" or "type:variant" (e.g. "page-turn:roll")

include.doc: "default" = just `types`; "all" = `types` plus every other transition and variant in transitions.json (each labelled); "extra" = only the ones `types` lacks. The default render length covers only the default list: for "all"/"extra" pass a longer duration (render --frames N, N = reelDuration)

holdFrames.doc: frames each panel holds between transitions

transitionFrames.doc: length of every transition in frames; 0 = each type's recommended length

subtitle.doc: note under the opening label; {n} = number of transitions

variantLabel.doc: word before the variant name on a panel

panels.doc: [[background, ink, accent], ...] colours of the labelled panels, cycled

notes.doc: overrides for the small note on each panel, keyed "type" or "type:variant"

light.doc: light vector [x, y] for the height shadows

description: Rounded, shadowed browser window on a blue-grey backdrop showing a landing page whose hero illustration is a living cinemagraph; cursor clicks the CTA, page scrolls.

title: Card fan: deal & play / connect
description: Cards deal from a pile into a fanned hand, one is hovered, played to centre and hits an enemy (white flash, slash, damage pop, HP drain); 'connect' mode links three glass cards' icons and merges them.

title: Card stack cascade (bento + focus)
description: Feature cards scale in from 30 % with a fade, staggered 4 f apart, into a bento grid (or a row, or a fanned deck) with a gentle idle float; then one card flies to the centre and grows to ~60 % of the frame while the rest dim to 40 % and defocus, and everything settles back.

default.title: Realtime sync

default.title: Automations
default.body: Hand the boring parts to a workflow that never sleeps.

cards.doc: [{title, body?, icon?: bolt|shield|chart|chat|globe|spark|lock|cog|user|db|cloud|star, image?: public path, span?: "2x1" | number of columns}]

unfocusAt.doc: frame when everything settles back (0 = never)

dimTo.doc: opacity of the other cards during focus

title: Carousel 3D
description: Cards or clips on a 3D ring rotate past the camera over a glossy floor with mirrored reflections; a motion-blurred whip lands the hero card face-on, which pushes forward while the others dim.
useFor: Portfolio reels, product galleries, template showcases, "pick from the collection" beats.

title: Chat bubbles, chips & thought bubble
description: Chat bubbles and comment / prompt chips pop in one by one around a box-bot, a speech balloon snaps on, then a thought bubble rises (dots -> cloud -> icons -> caption) and a green verdict chip drops in.
useFor: Conversations, user feedback / comments, "what people are asking", a character thinking back over its day, verdict reveals.

default.text: it forgot what it just did

stagger.doc: frames between messages when `at` is not given

thoughtIcons.doc: icons that pop into the thought cloud (alarm|train|toast|flask|button|moon|sun|coffee|bolt|heart|star|gear|chat|leaf|check|flame|shield|sword)

verdict.doc: text of the green chip that drops in at the end ("" = none)

title: Circuit rebuild
description: Isometric hardware assembly on drafting paper that rebuilds itself on every step: old parts and cables pop off and retract, the camera re-frames, then base pieces slide in, small parts drop with a tiny bounce, large props grow from a floor tile and cables grow last. Step card and header stay fixed.
useFor: Step-by-step product / hardware / architecture explainers ("add a database, then a cache"), onboarding tours, kit unboxing, any "here is step N" sequence.

default.title: Blink an LED

steps.doc: array of {title, text, parts:[{id, kind, fp?:[x,y,w,d,h], z?}]}; kinds: board breadboard resistor led button sensor wall motor servo light car ball. Parts are diffed by id between steps.

teardownFrames.doc: frames the outgoing parts take to leave (0.12-0.2 s)

cables.doc: draw cables from the board pin to each part pin (grow last, retract on teardown)

headerRight.doc: small right-aligned label in the top bar

card.doc: show the step info card at the bottom

margin.doc: auto-frame margin as a fraction of the viewport

title: Clock and calendar time-lapse
description: An analog clock whose hands sweep from one time to another over a night-dawn-day-dusk sky tint with a digital readout, beside a wall calendar whose pages flip (or tear off) day by day while the date rolls, ending with a pulse ring and a circled final date.
useFor: Deadlines, "a day in the life" and history-in-a-day stories, countdowns, project timelines, "X days later" beats. Use mode to show only the clock or only the calendar.

sky.doc: tint the background by time of day (clock modes)

accent.doc: header band, weekend days, seconds hand, end circle

holdEnd.doc: frames held after it ends (pulse + circle)

title: Command palette typing
description: A dot grows into a search / prompt bar, a caret types the query with jittered keystrokes while matching suggestions stagger in and filter themselves, Enter presses the bar (scale 0.97 plus an accent glow), the list collapses and a result card slides in and streams its answer with tag chips.

description: A comment section streaming up: avatars with initials, names and speech bubbles pop in one after another at the bottom and push older comments up under a fade, with a counting header and optional like badges.
useFor: Social proof, "what people are saying", reaction / reply montages, community and live-chat moments, comment-section explainers and ad reaction walls.
